works.title: The global distribution of plant diversity
Karst habitat islands drove a largely nonadaptive and allopatric radiation in Petrocodon (Gesneriaceae)
works.abstract: Whether evolutionary radiations are primarily driven by ecological or neutral processes remains an unresolved question. The karst-endemic genus Petrocodon, distributed across southern China and northern Indochina, provides a powerful system for testing these alternatives. We generated whole-genome sequencing data for 54 of the 60 described species and integrated these with morphological, geographic, and paleoclimatic data to evaluate the relative roles of ecological and neutral processes in diversification. Our analyses revealed a robust nuclear phylogeny but extensive cytonuclear discordance, likely due to pervasive ancient hybridization and introgression. Macroevolutionary and biogeographic analyses indicate that diversification began during a favorable climatic period enabling range expansion, but subsequent species accumulation was primarily driven by geographic isolation and allopatric divergence rather than ecological niche differentiation. Morphological evolution decoupled from lineage diversification, with most morphological diversity accumulating relatively late. Further analyses support genetic drift in small, isolated populations driving morphological evolution, although stabilizing selection cannot be excluded, and reticulate evolution may have additionally contributed to phenotypic innovation. Together, these results support a largely nonadaptive radiation in Petrocodon, in which spatial opportunity played a central role in species accumulation, while demographic and reticulate processes may have contributed to its striking phenotypic diversity.

works.title: Targeted rewiring of the rhizosphere metabolite–microbe axis restores phosphorus acquisition in inefficient citrus rootstock
works.abstract: Low phosphorus (P) availability limits citrus production, while genotypic determinants governing rhizosphere P mobilization remain elusive. Here, we investigated P-acquisition strategies in citrus rootstocks. We performed a systematic screening of citrus rootstocks under P-deficient conditions and identified two contrasting genotypes: P-efficient Citrus tangerina and P-inefficient Citrus junos. Comparative metabolomics, microbiome profiling, targeted strain isolation, and inoculation assays were combined to unravel metabolic and microbial drivers governing P mobilization. The superior P acquisition of C. tangerina stemmed from a unique root-exudate profile enriched in 2-hydroxyflavanone, scopoletin, raffinose, and gallic acid. These metabolites selectively enriched Methylobacterium sp. strain HA110, a robust P-solubilizing bacterium. Exogenous exudate application enhanced C. junos P acquisition, yet this beneficial effect was abolished under soil sterilization, demonstrating an essential role of microbiota. Combined supplementation of the metabolites and strain HA110 enhanced rhizosphere P activation, which in turn strengthened the P-acquisition capacity of C. junos and consequently stimulated its growth. Collectively, these findings uncover a novel metabolite-microbe axis: P-efficient rootstocks reshape their rhizosphere microbiome through specific exudates. This axis is amenable to rational reconfiguration to restore P acquisition in P-inefficient genotypes, laying a theoretical basis for exudate-derived biofertilizers to boost P-use efficiency in sustainable citriculture.

works.title: Cell lineages of soybean anther morphogenesis reveal developmental trajectory of microsporocytes at single-cell resolution
works.abstract: In flowering plants, anther morphogenesis and microspore mother cell (MMC) specification of the male reproductive organ are critical for fertility and seed-setting or yield, but their underlying mechanisms in soybean (Glycine max) remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we cytologically established a staged developmental framework of early soybean anthers that were collected to generate a high-resolution single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas. We further characterized 11 major cell types annotated by cluster-specific marker genes and validated by RNA in situ hybridization. Pseudotime trajectory analysis reconstructed the differentiation process of microsporocytes, tapetum, and middle layer from archesporial cells, and established a regulatory network governing germline development. Parallel comparison of mitotic dividing cells (DCs) and meiotic MMCs revealed divergent transcriptional and cell-cycle programs. DCs follow a linear mitotic cascade with smooth, continuous transcriptional regulation, whereas MMCs undergo lineage-specific transcriptional reprogramming with an oscillatory activation of cell-cycle regulators to orchestrate meiotic transitions and progression. By comparing the transcriptional regulatory network of DCs and MMCs, we identified a pair of C2H2 zinc finger factors GmKNUa/b, the homologs of Arabidopsis KNUCKLES, as a key switch for MMC differentiation in soybean. The CRISPR-Cas9-edited Gmknua/b double mutants lack meiocytes, and GmKNUa/b might trigger the mitosis-to-meiosis transition by repressing the persistent mitotic cell cycle. Taken together, these results reveal the cellular signatures and molecular basis of early soybean anther morphogenesis and germline specialization, and provide candidate targets for manipulating germline fate and male fertility in soybean.

works.title: Passport to protection: Xa1 must enter the nucleus to fight bacterial blight in rice
HDAC1/2 mediates the chloroplast unfolded protein response through histone H4 deacetylation in Chlamydomonas
works.abstract: Disruption of chloroplast proteostasis activates retrograde signaling that reprograms nuclear gene expression. However, how these signals are integrated with chromatin-based transcriptional regulation remains poorly understood. Here, using a genetic suppressor screen of a conditional ClpP1-depletion mutant, we identified a histone deacetylase HDAC1/2 as a regulator of chloroplast stress signaling in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. Loss of HDAC1/2 alleviated growth inhibition and reduced cell death caused by disruption of chloroplast proteostasis following ClpP1 depletion. Furthermore, HDAC1/2 deficiency enhanced tolerance to high-light, oxidative, and endoplasmic reticulum stresses, as well as chloroplast translation inhibition. These stress conditions increased H2O2 levels and HDAC1/2 protein accumulation, suggesting that H2O2 may act as a common upstream signal. Additionally, HDAC1/2 deficiency also disrupted the transcriptional response to ClpP1 depletion, particularly affecting genes involved in photosynthesis, redox homeostasis, DNA metabolism, cell-cycle regulation, and ROS scavenging. This altered response was accompanied by increased histone H4 acetylation. Together, our findings identify HDAC1/2 as an important regulator connecting organellar proteostasis signaling with nuclear epigenetic regulation and suggest a role for H2O2 associated chromatin remodeling in coordinating cellular stress responses.

works.title: No one-size-fits-all in pollination
Teosinte allele extends maize husk blade
The ZmNAC41‐ZmABC‐ZmCP regulatory module mediates jasmonate‐dependent resistance to southern corn rust in maize
works.abstract: Plant disease resistance is often governed by complex multigene modules, yet their composition and regulation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a maize defense module comprising the NAC (NAM, ATAF1/2, and CUC2) transcription factor ZmNAC41, the PADRE domain-containing protein ZmABC, and the cysteine protease ZmCP. This module contributes to resistance to southern corn rust (SCR) caused by Puccinia polysora and is linked to jasmonic acid (JA)-associated defense responses. Upon pathogen infection, ZmNAC41 was rapidly induced and directly activated ZmABC transcription. ZmABC physically interacted with ZmCP. Increased JA accumulation and induction of JA biosynthetic and JA-responsive genes were also observed. Silencing any one of the three genes markedly attenuated JA-associated defense responses and compromised resistance, supporting a functional contribution of all three components to maize defense. Importantly, natural variation analysis identified elite haplotypes carrying favorable alleles of ZmNAC41, ZmABC, and ZmCP, and these allele combinations were significantly associated with enhanced field resistance. Together, our findings reveal a maize defense module that integrates transcriptional regulation and protein interaction and contributes to SCR resistance in association with JA-associated defense responses. These findings provide genetic targets for breeding maize with improved resistance to SCR.

works.title: Two major QTL for Cadmium accumulation in oat (Avena sativa L.) grains
works.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a heavy-metal that accumulates in the environment, in cereal grains and ultimately in humans posing significant health risks. With the increased demand on plant-based products, the production of oats for food products has increased as well, and with it the risk of uptake of Cd. However, limited research exists on the genetic control of Cd accumulation in oat grains. This study evaluated a panel of 620 Nordic spring oat breeding lines in field trials in Sweden during 2015-2021. GWAS was conducted for 596 lines for Cd grain content, thousand kernel weight (tkw), and hectolitre weight (hlw). Fifteen and six significant marker trait associations were identified for tkw and hlw, respectively. Some of which corresponded to previously reported QTL and some of which represent putatively new loci. Two new major QTL were identified associated with Cd grain accumulation located on chromosomes 3D (432.54 Mbp) and 4A (381.23 Mbp), explaining 34.69% and 27.92% of the phenotypic variation, respectively. KEY MESSAGE : A total of 596 oat breeding lines were analysed for Cadmium accumulation in the grains. Genome-wide association studies identified two major QTL as well as strong candidate genes.

works.title: The Tudor domain protein gene CaTdp1 contributes to resistance against Phytophthora capsici race 3 in pepper (Capsicum annuum L.)
Virus-induced DCL2b relocalization strengthens antiviral defence in tomato
Glycan perception
A novel transducer of the hypoxia response
The evolutionary history of brackish specialization from marine ancestry in the seagrass Ruppia sinensis
works.abstract: Ruppia sinensis, a unique seagrass species that originated in the marine environment yet successfully colonized extreme inland habitats, offers a rare window onto how plants cope with major habitat shifts and clarifies the mechanisms of adaptive evolution during marine-to-brackish transitions. We assembled a chromosome-level genome, conducted comparative phylogenomic analyses, assessed salinity tolerance through physiological experiments, and analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 103 individuals representing 19 coastal and inland populations. R. sinensis falls in the core seagrass PRC (Posidoniaceae, Ruppiaceae, and Cymodoceaceae) clade with a Ruppiaceae-specific whole-genome duplication yet has lost tolerance to full-strength seawater and is an obligate brackish specialist. Coastal and inland lineages diverged c. 25 000 yr ago; dramatic sea-level fluctuations since the Last Glacial Period repeatedly displaced coastal populations, causing reductions in effective population size, loss of genetic diversity, and elevated genetic load. Inland populations persisted in saline-lake refugia and retain nearly twice the genetic diversity. The marine-to-brackish shift is an evolutionary trade-off rather than passive habitat tracking, with inland saline lakes serving as refugia that preserved diversity. Such shifts may be a recurrent adaptive strategy in seagrass evolution, and these diverse inland populations warrant conservation priority under climate change.

works.title: Speciation and biogeographical history in the European Alpine System: the radiation of Ranunculus sect. Euromontani (Ranunculaceae)
works.abstract: High mountain systems provide manifold preconditions for allopatric and sympatric speciation. We hypothesize that allopatric speciation due to geographical isolation of mountain chains, and sympatric speciation via allopolyploidy played major roles for a radiation within Ranunculus sect. Euromontani within the European Alpine System (EAS). We used target enrichment of 1249 nuclear gene loci on 81 samples for phylogenomics, biogeographical analysis, species delimitation, SNPs for genetic structure and NeighborNet analysis, flow cytometry for ploidy determination, and morphometrics for selected species pairs. We also included type material. The core R. sect. Euromontani comprises 12 monophyletic species, most of them (sub)endemic to one mountain system. The section originated probably from a widespread lineage and diversified 1.39 million years ago. Founder-event speciation was the most common mechanism; only one species (Ranunculus montanus) originated likely in situ via allopolyploidy. In the West Carpathians, the new species Ranunculus tatrimontanus was recognized as different from Ranunculus gruinalis (= Ranunculus pseudomontanus) in the South Carpathians. In the Pyrenees, clinal variation suggested inclusion of Ranunculus ruscinonensis into Ranunculus gouanii. Peripatric speciation during the Pleistocene was the predominant mechanism for this geographical/climatic radiation in the EAS, whereas sympatric speciation via allopolyploidy happened only in the Alps.

works.title: In Planta Haploid Induction by Genome Editing of DMP8 in Pennisetum alopecuroides
From pots to plots: Pathways from understanding plant response to drought to crop impact on-farm
works.abstract: A lot of research has been dedicated to better understand plant response to drought. To reduce the complexity of drought, much of that research has been done in pots, leading to a disconnection with field plots, where the impact of this research is expected. This viewpoint clarifies several confusions about drought tolerance of annual crops, and re-establishes a synergistic link between pots and plots. One confusion is between crop's capacity to survive under water limitation and its capacity to sustain growth, although at a limited rate, under water limitation. This confusion derives from the pot protocols that have been designed and widely used to assess plant responses to water limitation, although they differ greatly from the plot reality. The review proposes a drought tolerance definition (higher yield under water limitation in the field), and a drought tolerance framework that cluster traits that may scale up to higher yield under stress in the field, in a context-dependent manner, into five hubs (water demand, water budget size, speed of water use, water use efficiency, timing of water use). There, the question of scaling is critical because many "drought tolerance" traits, measured in pots, have been proposed in the literature, but few only scaled up to yield in the field. For example, a massive body of work has been done on traits to fight against oxidative stress under drought, although this research was unable to scale up at field level. Plants in pots and plants forming a canopy are exposed to very different atmospheric conditions regarding light exposure and evaporative demand. This has important consequences for their physiology and their interactions with the environment, which need to be considered in the interpretation of plant responses to drought in pots. Finally, the disconnection between pots and plots has also overlooked the importance of crop agronomy in the drought response. The last section of the review is then an advocacy to re-look more closely at the potential of agronomic practices to cope with water limitations. Agronomic practices that can contribute to drought tolerance, also in a context-dependent manner, are then mapped to the drought tolerance framework.

works.title: The DNA Demethylase CaDML2 Functions as a Transcriptional Activator in the Control of Pepper Fruit Ripening
works.abstract: Fruit ripening is controlled by intertwined hormonal, transcriptional, and epigenetic networks. Although DNA methylation dynamics modulate ripening in several species, their regulatory effects on non-climacteric pepper (Capsicum annuum) fruit ripening and carotenoid-based secondary metabolism remain poorly understood. Here, pepper fruit ripening was accompanied by global CHH hypermethylation and non‑CHH (CG/CHG) hypomethylation. CHH methylation was associated with the activation of a non‑canonical, RDR6/DCL2‑dependent RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway, whereas non‑CHH demethylation was correlated with the strong activation of the DNA demethylase DEMETER-like 2 (CaDML2). CaDML2 not only functions as a DNA demethylase but also directly activates the transcription of downstream target genes, including RIN, DIVARICATA1, capsanthin/capsorubin synthase (CCS), and the abscisic acid (ABA) biosynthesis-related gene NCED1. Moreover, CaDML2-induced demethylation of cytosines within the promoter regions of these target genes leads to increased transcription, thereby promoting ABA accumulation and enhancing carotenoid synthesis. Silencing of CaDML2 delayed pepper fruit ripening, whereas its heterologous expression restored ripening in tomato sldml2 mutants. These results reveal a dual epigenetic module in which CaDML2‑mediated DNA demethylation and transcriptional activation refine programmes for ABA production and carotenoid metabolism, clarifying the epigenetic basis of non‑climacteric fruit ripening and identifying CaDML2‑centred pathways as targets for manipulating pepper fruit ripening and quality traits.

works.title: The Gibberellin‐Responsive Module RsRGL3a‐RsGID1b‐1‐ RsATL56 Orchestrates Parthenocarpic Fruit Formation in Seedless Chestnut Rose ( Rosa sterilis )
works.abstract: Summary statement Seedlessness is a fruit trait highly favoured by consumers, with parthenocarpy serving as an important means to achieve seedless fruit. In this work, RsGID1b‐1 responds to GAs and promotes parthenocarpic fruitsetting by activating RsATL56 transcription in seedless chestnut rose ( Rosa sterilis ). RsRGL3a antagonizes RsGID1b‐1 and represses RsATL56 , negatively regulating parthenocarpy.

works.title: An Indole‐3‐Acetic Acid‐Amido Synthetase, GmGH3.2, Negatively Regulates Salt Tolerance in Soybean
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Soil salinization severely restricts soybean growth and productivity. Therefore, uncovering salt‐tolerance genes and their regulatory mechanisms is critical for breeding salt‐tolerant soybean varieties. In this study, a genome‐wide association study (GWAS) was conducted across four environments, and 7 quantitative trait locus (QTLs) associated with salt‐tolerance traits were identified. Furthermore, the candidate gene GmGH3.2 was cloned at qSTG2‐1 , which encodes an indole‐3‐acetic acid‐amido synthetase. Functional analyses revealed that interfering with expression of GmGH3.2 in soybean hairy roots significantly enhanced salt tolerance, as evidenced by an increase in total root length, surface area, volume, and tip number. Conversely, the overexpression of GmGH3.2 markedly inhibited root growth under salt stress when compared with the control. Additionally, GmGH3.2 negatively regulates salt tolerance by influencing K + ‐Na + homeostasis and the expression of six salt tolerance‐associated genes ( GmSOS1 , GmNHX1 , GmSALT3 , GmAKT1 , GmHKT1 , and GmSKOR ). Moreover, GmGH3.2 interacts with GmKH1 in the nucleus and may collaboratively participate in the regulation of salt tolerance. In summary, our findings establish GmGH3.2 as a negative regulator of salt tolerance in soybean, providing valuable theoretical insights and genetic resources for molecular breeding of salt‐tolerant cultivars.

works.title: MdMYB1R1 Activates MdMAPKKK18 and Additional Defense Pathways to Confer Resistance to Woody Fungal Pathogens in Apple
works.abstract: Trunk diseases caused by woody plant pathogens, including Valsa mali and Botryosphaeria dothidea, represent a major threat to global apple production; however, the molecular basis of host resistance remains largely elusive. In this study, we employed TMT-based quantitative proteomic profiling to compare necrotic and uninfected twig tissues of apple following V. mali inoculation, identifying 904 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs). Among these, the MYB transcription factor, MdMYB1R1, exhibited a pronounced induction in response to pathogen infection. Subcellular localization and transactivation assays revealed that MdMYB1R1 localizes to the nucleus and acts as a transcriptional activator. Transient overexpression of MdMYB1R1 in Nicotiana benthamiana potentiated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and activated MAPK signaling, correlating with enhanced resistance against Sclerotinia sclerotiorum. Stable overexpression of MdMYB1R1 in apple markedly enhanced resistance to both V. mali and B. dothidea, whereas silencing of MdMYB1R1 impaired disease tolerance. Through DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq), yeast one-hybrid (Y1H), electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA), and dual-luciferase reporter assays, we demonstrated that MdMYB1R1 binds to the promoter region of MdMAPKKK18 and activates its transcription, a gene encoding a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase involved in MAPK signaling. Genetic epistasis analysis further revealed that overexpression of MdMAPKKK18 only partially rescued the compromised resistance in MdMYB1R1-RNAi plants. Collectively, our findings identify MdMYB1R1 as a key positive regulator of apple resistance against trunk fungal diseases, acting at least in part by directly activating the MdMAPKKK18-mediated MAPK cascade and by regulating additional defense pathways, thus providing a promising candidate for breeding disease-resistant apple cultivars.

works.title: Identification of the sunflower EDL gene family reveals that HaEDL2 confers salt tolerance in sunflower
Combined loss of mitochondrial MDH1 and NAD-malic enzyme impairs Arabidopsis growth and photosynthesis under energy-limiting conditions
works.abstract: Malate is a central metabolite in plant energy metabolism and biosynthesis and a major carrier of carbon and reducing equivalents between chloroplasts, the cytosol, and mitochondria. Here, we combined reverse genetics with multiple complementary approaches to investigate how disruption of the major mitochondrial malate-converting enzymes affects plant performance under different environmental conditions. We generated two independent mutant lines (mdh1 me1 me2) lacking the predominant mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase isoform MDH1 and both subunits of NAD-dependent malic enzyme (NAD-ME), ME1 and ME2. Growth under contrasting photoperiods and irradiances revealed a conditional phenotype that was most pronounced under short-day/low-light condition. Under this condition, the mutants exhibited impaired growth and photosynthetic performance, accompanied by cytosolic redox imbalance and altered chloroplast ultrastructure. Transfer experiments demonstrated that this phenotype was reversible and determined by the prevailing growth conditions: plants initially grown under short days and low light recovered in newly formed leaves after transfer to long-day/normal-light condition, whereas the reciprocal transfer reproduced the growth impairment in newly formed leaves. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed dawn-associated perturbations in photosynthetic and redox homeostasis, characterized by reduced investment in chloroplast translation and photosynthetic machinery alongside enhanced proteome maintenance, photoprotection and repair, and iron/ROS homeostasis. Branched-chain amino acids also accumulated in the mutants at the end of the night under low light. Together, these results show that the combined loss of mitochondrial MDH1 and NAD-ME causes a reversible, light-regime-dependent impairment of Arabidopsis growth and photosynthetic performance, highlighting the importance of the simultaneous contribution of both the MDH1 and NAD-ME systems to mitochondrial malate conversion when photosynthetic energy input is limited.

works.title: Northern Hemisphere permafrost vegetation is greening but becoming less resilient
Strigolactones modulate iron uptake in plants
works.abstract: Summary Strigolactone (SL) hormones influence a wide range of developmental and physiological processes but have not previously been linked to plant iron homeostasis. Here, we identify the gene underlying the iron‐deficient maize mutant interveinal yellow ( ivy ) as ZmCCD8 , a key enzyme in SL biosynthesis. Maize ivy/ccd8 mutants exhibit reduced expression of iron‐regulated genes, including IRO2 and genes involved in iron chelator and transporter biosynthesis. Application of the synthetic SL rac ‐GR24 restores gene expression and alleviates chlorosis. Under iron‐deficient conditions, ccd8 mutants show normal upregulation of iron uptake genes, indicating that SLs are not required for the deficiency response but are essential for maintaining basal iron gene expression under sufficient iron. Similar chlorosis in Arabidopsis and rice SL mutants under moderate iron suggests a conserved role for SLs in iron regulation, with potential agricultural applications. We propose that strigolactone signaling acts as an upstream regulatory input to the established FIT/IRO2‐centered iron‐deficiency network, with SMXL/D53 proteins functioning as negative regulators and iron deficiency providing the principal activating cue.

works.title: The cyanobacterium Anabaena uses pleomorphism as an acclimation strategy to high‐light stress
works.abstract: Phytoplankton species display characteristic morphologies that are generally assumed to confer adaptive advantages, yet the functional significance of cell shape remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether pleomorphism contributes to acclimation to changing light environments. Using the cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 as a model system, we combined molecular genetics, microscopy, physiological measurements and biophysical analyses to determine how morphology is regulated and how it affects photosynthetic performance under different light intensities. We show that Anabaena undergoes a reversible light-dependent morphological transition from rod-shaped cells under low light to large globular cells under high-light stress. This transition is controlled by the relative activities of the elongasome and class A penicillin-binding proteins and is accompanied by thylakoid reorganization. The globular morphology reduces light absorption and enables cells to maintain photosynthetic activity under photoinhibitory conditions. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between cell-wall remodeling, cellular optics and photosynthetic performance, revealing pleomorphism as a dynamic acclimation strategy to high-light stress. More broadly, this work provides experimental support for the packaging effect and highlights morphology as an active determinant of phytoplankton acclimation capacity.

works.title: Chlorophagy targets chloroplasts irreversibly damaged by photoinhibition
works.abstract: Chlorophagy removes photodamaged chloroplasts in plants, while individual chloroplasts are also protected by mechanisms that limit damage to the photosynthetic apparatus caused by excess light energy, known as photoinhibition. How chlorophagy is functionally coupled with chloroplast-level protective mechanisms during acclimation to photoinhibition remains unclear. We investigated acclimatory responses to photoinhibition at the intracellular level in Arabidopsis thaliana through an integrative analysis combining Chl fluorescence measurements, microscopy imaging, and genetic analyses using mutants defective in nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) or the chloroplast avoidance response. The functionality of individual chloroplasts was further assessed by Chl fluorescence lifetime imaging and probe-based visualization of singlet oxygen and starch. Severe photoinhibition of photosystem II precedes the appearance of abnormally swollen chloroplasts, which are subsequently recognized by the autophagy machinery for degradation. The swollen chloroplasts represent irreversibly damaged chloroplasts that accumulate reactive oxygen species and lose photosynthetic function. The formation of these nonfunctional chloroplasts was enhanced in mutants defective in NPQ or the chloroplast avoidance response, and hyperaccumulation of nonfunctional chloroplasts led to necrotic cell death. Together, our findings illustrate how multilayered responses coordinate acclimation to photoinhibition: Chloroplast protective mechanisms minimize the formation of nonfunctional chloroplasts while chlorophagy removes them when they arise.

works.title: FERONIA Limits Jasmonic Acid Overaccumulation and Oxidative Stress to Enable Plant Survival Under Sustained Elevated Temperature
works.abstract: Plants, as sessile organisms, must continually adapt to fluctuating temperatures to ensure survival. The plasma membrane-localized receptor-like kinase FERONIA (FER) coordinates diverse physiological processes and responses to various biotic and abiotic stresses. However, the role of FER in plant adaptation to elevated temperatures remains largely unexplored. Here, we report that FER is indispensable for plant growth and survival at warm temperatures. We found that fer loss-of-function mutants exhibit impaired thermomorphogenic growth and are hypersensitive to mild heat stress, displaying extensive oxidative stress-mediated cell death at elevated temperatures. Combined genetic and molecular analyses revealed that these temperature-sensitive defects in fer mutants are caused by an overaccumulation of jasmonic acid (JA), which subsequently triggers excessive production of reactive oxygen species. Furthermore, we show that this aberrant JA accumulation and oxidative stress are attributable to impaired FER-mediated regulation of turgor-dependent cell wall tensile stress. Taken together, our results suggest that FER-mediated cell wall tensile stress regulation serves as a critical mechanism to prevent aberrant JA accumulation and oxidative stress at sustained elevated temperatures, thereby enabling plants to adapt to and survive under such conditions.

works.title: Climate‐Driven UV‐B Variability Across the Indo‐Gangetic Plains Alters Grain Traits, Nutrient Sequestration, and Flour Functionality of Tropical Pearl Millet Cultivars
works.abstract: Summary statement This study unravels how enhanced UV‐B modulates cultivar‐specific adaptive and metabolic responses in pearl millet grain quality. By integrating these multifaceted responses, we propose a mechanistic model for understanding the role of this critical, potent stressor in affecting crop grain quality in view of climate‐changing environments.

works.title: Root Microbiota Reprogram Aboveground Metabolite Allocation Across Tea Plant Tissues
works.abstract: Tea quality is determined by the composition and spatial distribution of specialized metabolites, such as amino acids, catechins, and caffeine, which vary across tissues and developmental stages. However, the mechanisms underlying metabolite allocation among tissues remain unclear. Plant-associated microbiota, particularly root communities, play important roles in regulating plant metabolism, yet their coordinated effects across plant compartments are poorly understood. Here, we combined metabolomic and microbiome analyses to investigate metabolic-microbial interactions in the white tea cultivar Zhenghe Dabai. Metabolite-associated microbial taxa identified from leaves were linked to root-derived isolates, and two synthetic communities (SynCom1 and SynCom2) were constructed and applied to the rhizosphere. Both SynComs enhanced flavan metabolite accumulation, especially proanthocyanidins, but exhibited distinct regulatory patterns. SynCom1 increased stem-enriched proanthocyanidins and multiple amino acids, including theanine, while SynCom2 promoted specific flavan derivatives and amino acids such as glutamate and tryptophan. Transcriptomic analysis revealed differential activation of flavonoid biosynthesis and amino acid transport pathways, with SynCom1 upregulating the transporter gene CsCAT1. Overall, our results demonstrate that root microbiota can differentially regulate host metabolism and metabolite allocation, providing new insights into microbiome-mediated quality formation in tea and highlighting the potential of synthetic microbial communities for crop improvement.

works.title: Alternative Splicing of CsCPL Relieves the Inhibitory Effect of CsCPL on Trichome Formation and Anthocyanin Biosynthesis in Tea Plants
works.abstract: The downy buds on tender branches of tea plants are used to produce high-quality green, black, dark, and white teas due to their abundance of polyphenols, theanine, caffeine, and aroma constituents. The trichomes covering the downy buds (known as 'háo' in Chinese) contribute significantly to beverage quality. However, the molecular and regulatory mechanisms underlying tea trichome development are still not fully elucidated. Here, we identify an R3 MYB transcription repressor involved in trichome formation, CsCAPRIC-like (CPL), which undergoes alternative splicing in tea plants to generate two transcripts: the conventional isoform CsCPL and the intron-retaining form CsCPL AS. The conventional isoform CsCPL competitively binds to CsGL3 (a bHLH component of the MYB‑bHLH‑WD40 complex), thereby preventing the formation of the CsMYB15-CsGL3-CsWD40 and CsMYB6-CsGL3-CsWD40 complexes, and further inhibiting the expression of two key downstream genes: CsGL2 (GLABRA2, HD-Zip IV transcription factor), responsible for trichome formation, and CsANS (anthocyanidin synthase), responsible for anthocyanin biosynthesis. Due to alternative splicing within the conserved CsGL3-binding motif, the CsCPL AS cannot bind to CsGL3, but can interact with the conventional isoform CsCPL to form a non-functional heterodimer. This interaction alleviates the inhibitory effect of CsCPL protein on the formation of MBW complexes, thereby reducing its inhibitory effect on trichome formation and anthocyanin biosynthesis. These findings reveal a unique mechanism for trichome formation mediated by alternative splicing of CsCPL, which is fundamental to tea plant growth and quality.

works.title: Synthetic Community Driven by a Keystone Rhizosphere Bacterium Suppresses Whitefly‐Mediated Begomovirus Transmission via the Jasmonate Signaling Pathway in Tomato
works.abstract: Tomato production is threatened by the combined stress of whiteflies and the whitefly-transmitted Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV). Although the rhizosphere microbiome plays a critical role in plant defense, the rational assembly strategy and underlying mechanisms of a synthetic microbial community (SynCom) targeting this insect-virus complex remain unclear. Here, leveraging the beneficial soil legacy induced by Beauveria bassiana, we constructed an eight-strain synthetic community through multi-omics analysis, soil incubation, and root exudate chemotaxis assays. One-strain knockout experiments confirmed that strain N2 is the keystone species driving the biocontrol function. Through supernatant cross-culture assays, we further refined this consortium into an optimized synthetic community (OptSynM) consisting of the single keystone strain and four helper strains. Bioassays demonstrated that OptSynM significantly reduced whitefly fitness and suppressed TYLCV accumulation in tomato plants. Within the consortium, the helper strains enhanced the rhizosphere colonization of N2 by promoting its growth and biofilm formation. Mechanistically, OptSynM activated host systemic immunity via the jasmonic acid signaling pathway. Furthermore, OptSynM maintained robust biocontrol efficacy in pot trials conducted with natural agricultural soil. Our findings highlight the practical promise of microbiome-based interventions and provide a strategic framework for using synthetic microbial communities to facilitate sustainable agricultural practices.

works.title: Drought‐Induced Dieback Emerges From Microsite‐Driven Functional Divergence in European Beech
works.abstract: Why neighbouring trees exposed to the same climatic extremes follow contrasting decline trajectories remains a central question in understanding climate-driven forest dieback. Here, we reconstructed the processes underlying drought-induced decline in a rear-edge European beech (Fagus sylvatica) forest by integrating dendroecology, wood anatomy, stable isotopes, leaf physiology, fine-root traits and soil fungal community analyses. Tree vulnerability was primarily linked to long-term functional divergence driven by microsite heterogeneity rather than recent climatic stress. Vigorous trees occupied deeper soils and experienced higher local competition, exhibiting safer hydraulic architecture, greater stem storage capacity, deeper water uptake, lower long-term intrinsic water-use efficiency and stronger ectomycorrhizal mediation of resource acquisition. In contrast, trees on shallower soils and under low competition displayed more vulnerable hydraulic trajectories, reduced access to deep water sources and weaker drought buffering. These differences were detectable decades before growth trajectories diverged. Extreme droughts and compound drought-frost events exposed pre-existing vulnerabilities. Following a critical drought-frost event in 1995, declining trees failed to recover and entered a self-reinforcing cascade involving crown dieback, reduced carbon assimilation, constrained growth, diminished formation of conductive and storage tissues, and weaker carbon allocation to ectomycorrhizal fungi. The contrasting trajectories emerged from organ-specific adjustments, rather than from a uniform shift along a single whole-plant strategy. Our results show that forest decline often reflects the delayed expression of long-standing vulnerabilities shaped by fine-scale microsite heterogeneity.

works.title: C2H2 zinc‐finger transcription factor FveJAG cooperates with SIMPLE LEAF1 to regulate compound leaf morphogenesis in strawberry
works.abstract: Leaves play a vital role in photosynthesis, respiration, and transpiration, significantly impacting a plant's adaptability and crop yield. Strawberry plants develop trifoliate compound leaves, the molecular regulatory pathways of which are not well-understood. Here, we identified a woodland strawberry (Fragaria vesca) mutant, designated simple leaf 2 (sl2), which exhibits the complete suppression of the two lateral leaflets. The causal gene encodes a C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor that is homologous to JAGGED and is named FveJAG. A point mutation located within the intron triggers alternative splicing and generates a premature stop codon. The prior key transcriptional regulator of leaflet initiation, SIMPLE LEAF1 (SL1), directly targets the promoter of FveJAG to activate its transcription. The synergistic interaction between sl1 and sl2 indicates that SL1 and FveJAG function within the same regulatory pathway. Genetic and expression analyses suggest that FveJAG also acts downstream of FveMYB117a during leaflet initiation. Taken together, our results uncover a direct SL1 target gene and elucidate a complex regulatory network involving SL1, FveJAG, and FveMYB117a in strawberry compound leaf morphogenesis, offering further mechanistic insights into the genetic regulation of leaf complexity.

works.title: PGCopilot : an AI ‐assisted research agent for plant functional genomics
works.abstract: The exponential expansion of multi-omic data presents a major bottleneck for researchers seeking to derive biological insights from heterogeneous genomic resources. Although large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction with scientific knowledge, general-purpose LLMs are not designed to reason over plant-specific biological issues and frequently produce hallucinated or oversimplified outputs. We developed PGCopilot, an AI-assisted research agent tailored for plant functional genomics. It integrated task planning, identifier disambiguation, and tool orchestration to actively retrieve and synthesize evidence across heterogeneous biological databases using the Model Context Protocol. Built on a knowledge base of 1.83 million records, together with online access to PubMed titles and available abstracts covering over 33 million indexed articles and STRING protein-protein interaction data, it could plan retrieval strategies and integrate evidence into grounded responses, reducing unsupported outputs and addressing data fragmentation and identifier discrepancies. In expert-guided benchmarking, PGCopilot achieved higher performance than the evaluated baseline LLMs, demonstrating advantages in task relevance, evidence integration, hallucination control, and research utility, and providing more verifiable citations and explicit reporting of cross-database inconsistencies. As an autonomous agent supporting multiturn tool interaction, it streamlined cross-database evidence integration from labor-intensive search-and-retrieval to automated analysis-and-synthesis. This approach streamlines cross-database navigation and evidence integration, allowing researchers to focus more on hypothesis formulation, experimental design, and critical interpretation of comprehensive evidence.

works.title: Revisiting lipid droplets in plant virus infection: scarcity of data, abundance of questions
works.abstract: Yicheng Liu, Sangmin Lee, Ho-Seok Lee, Eun Yu Kim; Revisiting lipid droplets in plant virus infection: scarcity of data, abundance of questions, Journal of

works.title: A SNP in the MdWRKY11 promoter controls the segregation of Glomerella leaf blotch susceptibility in apple
works.abstract: Glomerella leaf blotch (GLB), a severe fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, threatens the apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) industry worldwide. The susceptibility of apple to GLB is controlled by a single dominant locus. Although several markers for GLB susceptibility have been developed, the causal genes and their functional variations have not been explored. In this study, we used MapQTL and fine mapping to identify SNP544 C/G in the MdWRKY11 promoter as the major factor underlying the variation in GLB susceptibility in apple. The SNP544 G allele generates a W-box motif that is directly bound by MdWRKY29 and activates MdWRKY11 expression during C. gloeosporioides infection. In turn, MdWRKY11 binds to the MdDMR6.1 promoter and activates its expression, leading to salicylic acid degradation and leaf necrosis. The MdWRKY11 SNP544 G allele was strongly associated with GLB susceptibility, with a prediction accuracy of 96.2% in 767 Malus accessions. In addition to SNP544, we identified nine allelic variations in MdWRKY11 across 29 Malus accessions, with a combined prediction accuracy for GLB susceptibility of 99.6%. These findings shed light on the genetic control of GLB susceptibility in apple and provide an efficient molecular marker for breeding GLB-resistant cultivars.

works.title: Auxin-dependent miR167-ARF6/8.1-SAURs module coordinates local growth to shape floret diversification in Asteraceae
works.abstract: The corolla is a primary determinant of floral architecture and reproductive success. However, the processes that translate localized growth patterns into species-specific morphologies remain unclear. The complex inflorescences (capitula) of Asteraceae consist of different types of flowers. In Chrysanthemum × morifolium, anemone-type varieties represent a distinct floral form characterized by dramatically elongated corolla tubes in bisexual disc florets. Using the anemone-type chrysanthemum, characterized by dramatically elongated disc florets, we demonstrate that sustained corolla formation depends on localized auxin enrichment. Two auxin response factors, CmARF6 and CmARF8.1, have been identified as positive regulators of this process. These ARFs are post-transcriptionally regulated by miR167 in a dose-dependent manner, establishing a regulatory module that directly activates the auxin-biosynthesis gene CmYUC2 and auxin-transport gene CmPILS1. Concurrently, CmARF6 and CmARF8.1 stimulate localized tissue proliferation by activating CmSAUR64 and CmSAUR76. Comparative analyses across diverse Asteraceae species suggest that auxin-associated regulatory mechanisms may contribute to region-specific corolla growth. Our findings demonstrate that auxin regulation contributes to region-specific corolla growth in the bisexual disc florets of chrysanthemum, providing a framework for investigating related morphological variation in other Asteraceae species.

works.title: Sucrose signaling regulates theanine accumulation via the CsYABBY2-CsMYB5- CsPDX2.1 module in tea plants
works.abstract: Theanine is a specialized non-protein amino acid that determines the quality of tea (Camellia sinensis), yet the regulatory mechanisms controlling its hydrolysis remain unknown. Here we show that sucrose acts as a signal to modulate theanine accumulation by regulating a transcriptional repressor module that suppresses the theanine hydrolase gene CsPDX2.1. Using a yeast one-hybrid screen, we identified two transcription factors, CsYABBY2 and CsMYB5, that directly bind to distinct cis-elements (TAATGATT and TAACCA) in the CsPDX2.1 promoter. We demonstrate that CsYABBY2 and CsMYB5 interact to form a complex, and that co-expression of both proteins synergistically enhances repression of CsPDX2.1 transcription. Functional analyses via virus-induced gene silencing and transient overexpression confirmed that this module negatively regulates CsPDX2.1 expression and positively controls theanine accumulation. Importantly, exogenous sucrose suppresses CsYABBY2 and CsMYB5 expression, thereby derepressing CsPDX2.1 expression and reducing theanine levels, suggesting that sucrose functions as a regulatory factor affecting this pathway. Our findings reveal a sucrose-responsive (CsYABBY2-CsMYB5-CsPDX2.1) module that mediates theanine accumulation, providing a molecular basis for understanding varietal differences in theanine content.

works.title: Author Correction: Liquid–liquid phase separation of TZP promotes PPK-mediated phosphorylation of the phytochrome A photoreceptor
The CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis governs citrus plant regeneration in association with chromatin remodeling
works.abstract: Plant regeneration underpins crop genetic improvement, yet its regulatory mechanism remains poorly characterized in woody fruit trees. The RWP-RK domain-containing (RKD) transcription factor CitRWP acts as a pleiotropic regulator of nucellar polyembryony and somatic embryogenesis (SE) in citrus, but its downstream molecular network remains elusive. We demonstrate that CsWUS, a core stem cell regulator, is a direct downstream target of CitRWP. CitRWP binds to the CsWUS promoter to activate its transcription. Additionally, CitRWP interacts with the SWItch/Sucrose Non-Fermentable (SWI/SNF) chromatin-remodeling ATPase SPLAYED (SYD), synergistically enhancing CsWUS activation, while chromatin accessibility at the CsWUS locus is enhanced upon CitRWP overexpression. We further uncover that CsWUS negatively regulates CitRWP expression via a feedback loop. CsWUS overexpression promotes SE in recalcitrant citrus callus, but causes abnormal meristem proliferation and impairs shoot organogenesis from epicotyl segments. CsWUS greatly enhanced in planta transformation efficiency in the model citrus. This study establishes the CitRWP-CsWUS regulatory axis as a central module that coordinates multiple developmental fate transitions in association with chromatin remodeling, providing novel insights into the mechanisms of cellular totipotency and plant regeneration.

works.title: PhYAB4 directly activates PhAGL6‐2 to regulate lip‐related organ curvature morphology in Paphiopedilum henryanum
works.abstract: The orchid lip is a highly specialized floral organ that contributes to floral architecture and pollinator interaction. However, the developmental and molecular mechanisms underlying lip-related organ curvature in Paphiopedilum remain poorly understood. Using Paphiopedilum henryanum and its Type A peloric mutant, we found that visible divergence between wild-type petals and mutant lip-like petals begins at Stage 4. Curvature was associated with adaxial-abaxial epidermal cell number imbalance in the distal region, whereas average epidermal cell area remained largely unchanged. Transcriptome and expression analyses identified PhAGL6-2 as a lip-associated AGL6 homolog enriched in lips and lip-like petals during Stages 4-5. PhAGL6-2 was preferentially expressed on the abaxial side, particularly in regions associated with curvature. Virus-induced gene silencing-mediated silencing of PhAGL6-2 in Dendrobium Chao Praya Smile and P. henryanum affected perianth organ curvature, suggesting a broader role in floral organ morphogenesis. The YABBY transcription factor PhYAB4 directly bound the AGTGTG motif in the PhAGL6-2 promoter and activated its transcription. Silencing PhYAB4 reduced PhAGL6-2 expression and caused stronger floral curvature, lip outgrowths, and partial disruption of floral symmetry. These findings identify a PhYAB4-PhAGL6-2 pathway associated with epidermal cell number imbalance and lip-related organ curvature.

works.title: Banana fruit with nutritionally significant concentrations of iron and zinc: results from the field evaluation of genetically modified bananas ( Musa spp.) in Australia
works.abstract: Summary Iron deficiency remains a major public health problem in East Africa, where banana is a staple food for > 30 million people. This study investigated whether genetic modification could produce banana fruit containing nutritionally significant concentrations of iron while maintaining agronomic performance under field conditions. Six transgenes associated with iron homeostasis were expressed singly or in combination in Cavendish and Lady Finger bananas. In total, 450 genetically modified plants were field evaluated in Australia and fruit mineral concentrations assessed in the first planting crop. Elevated fruit iron and zinc concentrations, reaching 45.5 and 51.9 mg kg −1 dry weight, respectively, were associated with increased nicotianamine (NA) accumulation following expression of OsNAS . Iron concentrations sufficient to meet 50% of the estimated average requirement for children were achieved in 28 lines, with elevated NA suggesting improved iron bioavailability. Increased mineral accumulation negatively correlated with yield; however, this effect was partly mitigated by co‐expression of OsVIT1 . Early indicators of yield penalty included low corm iron, high leaf zinc concentrations and reduced photosynthetic efficiency. These findings demonstrate the potential of using genetic modification for the mineral biofortification of bananas in East Africa while highlighting factors that may assist in the early identification of high‐performing biofortified lines.

works.title: Discovery and Deployment of Herbicide Tolerance in Domesticated Pennycress ( Thlaspi arvense L.) to Enable Modern Agronomic Integration
works.abstract: Modern agronomic systems for large-scale oilseed production rely heavily on chemical weed control, presenting a barrier to the adoption of newly domesticated crops that lack herbicide tolerance. Pennycress (Thlaspi arvense L.), a domesticated winter oilseed developed to increase land productivity and support sustainable biofuel production, is highly sensitive to commonly used herbicides targeting acetolactate synthase (ALS) and 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPPD). Here, we report complementary strategies for identifying and deploying herbicide-tolerant alleles in pennycress. ALS inhibitor tolerance was identified through Ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)-derived chemical mutagenesis, whereas HPPD inhibitor tolerance was explored using a microbial-based rational enzyme design platform as proof of concept. Selected alleles were introduced into advanced germplasm via homology-directed repair (HDR) and evaluated across developmental stages. Plants carrying the P187S mutation in the ALS gene exhibited robust tolerance at both seedling and rosette stages without detectable penalties to growth or seed yield. In contrast, the G419A allele in the HPPD gene conferred tolerance to residual herbicide activity when overexpressed but showed limited efficacy when expressed from its native locus, indicating context-dependent functionality. Collectively, this study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating herbicide tolerance into a newly domesticated oilseed crop and highlights the utility of combining mutagenesis-based discovery, rational enzyme engineering, and precision genome editing to support agronomic compatibility and crop deployment.

works.title: CSLB4 modulates primary cell wall architecture and resistance to Brevicoryne brassicae in Arabidopsis thaliana
works.abstract: The plant cell wall (CW) is a key determinant of plant defense; however, the extent to which natural variation in primary CW architecture contributes to resistance against phloem-feeding insects remains unclear. Here, we combined genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with functional analyses to identify genetic determinants of resistance against the specialist aphid Brevicoryne brassicae in Arabidopsis thaliana. GWAS identified a significant locus on chromosome 2 associated with aphid performance. Integration of haplotype and epidermis-specific expression data prioritized CSLB4, a member of the cellulose synthase-like B family. Loss-of-function analysis using two independent T-DNA insertion alleles reduced B. brassicae offspring by 39-56%, indicating enhanced resistance, whereas performance of the generalist aphid Myzus persicae was unaffected. Electrical penetration graph analyses revealed that cslb4 mutants reached sustained phloem ingestion earlier than wild type despite reduced performance, indicating that their enhanced resistance was not associated with impaired phloem access. Biochemical, immunolocalization, and transcriptional analyses revealed constitutive alterations in primary CW architecture and aphid-induced defense responses, including changes in pectin composition, increased xyloglucan epitope accessibility, reduced callose deposition, and attenuated induction of defense-related genes. Together, these findings identify CSLB4 as a modulator of primary CW architecture and plant susceptibility to B. brassicae.

works.title: FaWRKY7 modulates jasmonate signaling responses and enhances strawberry fruit resistance to Botrytis cinerea
works.abstract: WRKY transcription factors and jasmonic acid (JA) signaling are essential for plant responses to stress, but their roles in strawberry resistance to Botrytis cinerea remain unclear. Here, we investigated the function of FaWRKY7 in strawberry fruit and transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana. FaWRKY7 expression was significantly induced at 72 h after B. cinerea inoculation. Transient overexpression of FaWRKY7 enhanced strawberry fruit resistance to B. cinerea, whereas silencing increased susceptibility. Similarly, FaWRKY7-overexpressing Arabidopsis plants showed enhanced resistance to B. cinerea and greater responsiveness to exogenous methyl jasmonate (MeJA), although basal levels of free JA, JA-Ile, and OPDA were not detectably altered in non-inoculated samples. Pharmacological assays further showed that FaWRKY7-mediated resistance was maintained under MeJA treatment and only partially reduced by Jarin-1, an inhibitor of JA-Ile formation, indicating that this effect is only partially dependent on JA-Ile formation. Mechanistically, DAP-seq, yeast one-hybrid, EMSA, and dual-luciferase assays showed that FaWRKY7 directly binds to the promoters of FaJAZ4 and FaJAZ8 and represses their transcription. These findings indicate that FaWRKY7 enhances resistance to B. cinerea, at least in part by directly repressing FaJAZ4 and FaJAZ8 and thereby modulating jasmonate signaling responses.

works.title: The transcriptional regulation of specialized terpenoid biosynthesis and its regulation by jasmonic acid
works.abstract: All plants produce terpenoids for their general metabolism but most, if not all, also produce terpenoids in their specialized metabolism. These specialized metabolites play an essential role in the interaction of plants with their environment, in particular with other organisms. They are also of great economic value to us as they are used as medicine, in our food and as perfumes. The regulation of terpenoid biosynthesis has received much attention as it is costly for the plants to produce even though they only contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Some terpenoids are constitutively produced but most of them are induced upon biotic stress with a key role for the phytohormone jasmonate-isoleucine (JA-Ile). It has become clear that the regulation is mostly at the level of transcription with an important role for basic-helix-loop-helix (bHLH) and MYB transcription factors in the JA-Ile inducible pathways. This review summarizes recent breakthroughs with examples of specific mono-, sesqui- and diterpenoids, describing the complex molecular network regulating their biosynthesis in certain model systems with other phytohormones involved as well. It also points out that several other avenues of regulation need more attention to understand the fine tuning of the regulation. This will help optimizing the production of these specialized metabolites in our crops.

works.title: A game of two leaf sides: Abaxial vs Adaxial stomata
works.abstract: Stomata are of the utmost importance to plant function, growth and productivity, as they enable gas exchange for photosynthesis, as well as facilitate transpiration for evaporative cooling and nutrient uptake. The balance between these two processes depends on stomatal density, size and behaviour, which together determine stomatal conductance and intrinsic water use efficiency. There has been great progress in elucidating the genetic pathways that govern the development of stomatal patterning and density, however, although many species have stomata on both surfaces of the leaf, traditionally the importance of adaxial stomata has been largely overlooked in the literature. Recent studies have started to evaluate the impact of the varying contribution of adaxial (AD) vs abaxial (AB) stomata to gas exchange, the costs and benefits of different AD:AB ratios for different species and growth conditions, as well as differences in sensitivity to environmental cues between the two surfaces. Our review focuses on the environmental drivers of differential stomatal patterning and physiological function and the potential to manipulate surface-specific stomatal patterning independently to optimize leaf gas exchange for crops growing in different environments.

works.title: HvMAPK5‐Mediated Phosphorylation of HvWRKY75 Enhances Salt Tolerance in Barley
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Soil salinization is a significant constraint on crop productivity, necessitating the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying salt tolerance in cereals such as barley. In this study, a novel regulatory module comprising the ion transporter HvHKT1;2 , the transcription factor HvWRKY75 , and the mitogen‐activated protein kinase HvMAPK5 was identified. HvHKT1;2 localized to the plasma membrane, and its overexpression promoted Na + efflux at the root apex, reduced Na + accumulation in shoots, increased the K + /Na + ratio, and enhanced salt tolerance, whereas HvHKT1;2 knockdown produced the opposite phenotype. Furthermore, HvWRKY75 directly bound to the HvHKT1;2 promoter and activated its transcription. Under salt stress, HvMAPK5 interacted with and phosphorylated HvWRKY75 at Ser21, thereby enhancing HvWRKY75 protein stability and transcriptional activity toward HvHKT1;2. Consistently, HvMAPK5 overexpression increased HvWRKY75 protein abundance, upregulated HvHKT1;2 expression, and enhanced salt tolerance, whereas HvMAPK5 knockdown accelerated HvWRKY75 degradation and compromised salt tolerance. Collectively, our findings identify a regulatory module consisting of HvMAPK5 , HvWRKY75 , and HvHKT1;2 that maintains cellular Na + /K + homeostasis during salt stress, providing a mechanistic framework for breeding salt‐tolerant barley varieties.

works.title: Single‐Nucleus Transcriptomics Reveals Cell Type Specific Defence Responses and Identifies AhWRKY40 as a Key Regulator of Peanut Resistance to Sclerotium rolfsii
works.abstract: Peanut stem rot caused by Sclerotium rolfsii is a devastating soil borne disease that severely constrains peanut production worldwide. Despite its economic importance, highly resistant peanut cultivars are still largely unavailable, and the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance remain poorly understood. We obtained a total of 29,308 high-quality nuclei, annotated five major cell types, and detected 52,819 expressed genes. Comparative analysis revealed widespread transcriptional reprogramming and a predominance of downregulated genes in response to pathogen infection, accompanied by a substantial reduction in cell abundance across all cell populations. Notably, epidermal cells harboured the highest proportion of disease resistance genes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further demonstrated that S. rolfsii infection altered cellular transcriptional states and induced cell type specific immune reprogramming. Integrative analyses combining gene coexpression, pseudotime dynamics, virtual knockout, and transgenic validation consistently identified AhWRKY40 as a key regulatory factor associated with disease resistance. Overexpression of AhWRKY40 enhanced resistance to S. rolfsii and was accompanied by increased accumulation of jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA), suggesting its involvement in hormone-mediated defence responses. Collectively, our study provides new insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance to stem rot, identifies AhWRKY40 as a promising candidate gene for disease resistance, and establishes a valuable resource for functional genomics and molecular breeding to improve southern blight resistance in peanut.

works.title: Comprehensive meta-QTL analysis uncovers stable loci for fruit traits, morphological development, anthocyanin regulation, and biotic stress resistance in eggplant
PbAGO4‐dependent hypermethylation of the PbNAC71 promoter regulates anthocyanin synthesis in pear
works.abstract: Bud mutations in perennial fruit trees often involve epigenetic variation, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We identified a spontaneous green bud mutant of the red-skinned pear "Aohong No. 1" that fails to accumulate anthocyanins under light. Integrated methylome and transcriptome analyses revealed that in the mutant, hypermethylation of a 148-bp light-responsive enhancer in the PbNAC71 promoter, maintained by PbAGO4, represses PbNAC71 expression. In the wild type, this enhancer remains hypomethylated, whereas in the mutant, it is hypermethylated; this differential methylation is detectable at the young fruit stage and stably maintained at the post-harvest stages examined, representing a pre-set epigenetic state. Silencing of PbNAC71 downregulated PbMYB10 and PbCHI1, and attenuated PbMYB10-mediated activation of PbCHS1 and PbDFR3, thereby suppressing anthocyanin accumulation. Both PbAGO4 knockout in callus and PbAGO4 silencing in fruit peel reduced enhancer methylation, and increased PbNAC71 expression and anthocyanin accumulation. Together, these results reveal a mechanism by which PbAGO4-dependent methylation of a light-responsive enhancer establishes a stable pre-set state that controls how environmental light signals regulate anthocyanin synthesis.

works.title: MaizeGP: An open graph‐based maize pangenome platform for integrative multi‐scale exploration of structural variation
works.abstract: MaizeGP, an interactive graph-based pangenome platform, integrates structural variation from 48 diverse maize genomes with functional annotations and visualization tools. MaizeGP enables multi-scale exploration of genomic variation across individual loci, gene families, and trait associations. This accessible resource supports future investigation of maize genome diversity and its biological implications.

works.title: COP1 proteins integrate light signaling to fruit plastid development via the HY5-GLK2 module in tomato
works.abstract: Light signaling regulates plant development, yet how it differentially controls plastid development across organs remains unclear. Here, we show that two tomato COP1 proteins restrict plastid development in fruits but not in leaves. With CRISPR-Cas9 mutants, we demonstrate that SlCOP1s repress photomorphogenesis by destabilizing SlHY5 and controlling large-scale light-responsive transcription in seedlings. In fruits, SlCOP1s suppress chloroplast development and chlorophyll accumulation by inhibiting SlHY5-dependent activation of GLK2, a key regulator of plastid biogenesis. SlHY5 directly binds the GLK2 promoter and activates its expression in fruits, but not in leaves, highlighting tissue-specific deployment of the SlCOP1-SlHY5 module. This pathway is distinct from CUL4-DDB1-DET1-mediated regulation of GLK stability, indicating multilayered control of GLK2. Enhanced plastid development in Slcop1 double mutants is associated with increased carotenoid accumulation in fruit. Together, these findings uncover a SlCOP1-SlHY5-GLK2 module that links light signaling to fruit plastid development and illustrate how conserved pathways are rewired to control organelle development in a tissue-dependent manner.

works.title: Hitting the sweet spot: Stomatal regulation depends on the location and concentration of sucrose
works.abstract: Alison R Gill; Hitting the sweet spot: Stomatal regulation depends on the location and concentration of sucrose, Plant Physiology, , kiag834, https://doi.o

works.title: OsPIL1 modulates growth–yield–blast resistance trade-offs involving OsINV3 and jasmonate signaling
works.abstract: Phytochrome-interacting factor-like proteins coordinate plant growth and defense, but the influence of genetic background on their functions in rice remains unclear. We characterized OsPIL1 in japonica cv. Lijiangxintuanheigu (LTH) and examined its association with OsINV3 in LTH and indica cv. Acuce. Although the cultivars shared identical OsPIL1 coding sequences, OsPIL1 overexpression restricted growth, reduced yield-related traits, and increased blast susceptibility in LTH, contrasting with previously reported effects in Acuce. In uninoculated LTH plants, overexpression increased peroxidase activity and several defense-related transcripts but reduced reactive oxygen species and jasmonate accumulation. Following Magnaporthe oryzae inoculation, OsPIL1 knockout lines showed enhanced resistance, lower fungal biomass, and elevated defense outputs. Exogenous jasmonate alleviated symptoms in wild-type, knockout, and overexpression plants, indicating that this protection did not strictly require functional OsPIL1. Transcriptome profiling linked OsPIL1 perturbation to photosynthesis, phenylpropanoid metabolism, and defense signaling. OsPIL1 overexpression was associated with reduced OsINV3 expression in stems of both cultivars, whereas leaf responses depended on cultivar and developmental stage. Combined loss of OsPIL1 and OsINV3 enhanced resistance in LTH but reduced resistance in Acuce, accompanied by differences in downstream gene expression. These findings establish contrasting phenotypic outcomes of OsPIL1-associated networks in two rice backgrounds and identify candidate relationships for investigating growth and defense coordination.

works.title: Allelic Homogenization of Detoxification Genes RsCYP3A24 and RsGSTF5 Is Associated with Metabolic Resistance to SYP-14288 in Rhizoctonia solani
works.abstract: Fungicide resistance in multinucleate fungi, such as Rhizoctonia solani, poses a growing challenge for effective disease management. This study explores the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance to the fungicide SYP-14288 in R. solani, focusing on the role of two detoxification genes (RsCYP3A24 and RsGSTF5) and fungal nuclear heterogeneity. Genotyping analysis revealed that the parental R. solani strain harbors mixed allelic variants. Under fungicide stress, continuous subculturing reduced nuclear heterogeneity in resistant mutants, which progressively showed apparent allelic fixation of selected sequence variants, a genotypic shift toward homokaryotization. Transcriptomic and genomic analyses revealed significant upregulation and optimized gene composition of these detoxification genes in the resistant mutants. Functional validation through enzymatic activity assays confirmed that RsCYP3A24 participates in phase I oxidation, whereas RsGSTF5 mediates phase II glutathione-conjugation detoxification. Heterologous expression in Escherichia coli demonstrated that the detoxification proteins of resistant strains with fixed resistance-associated alleles possessed greater detoxification efficiency for SYP-14288. These genes were coordinately upregulated and functionally enhanced under fungicide selection pressure. This selective pressure altered the nuclear composition of heterokaryotic populations and promoted adaptive evolution characterized by allelic homogenization. Overall, this study provides new insights into the relationship between allelic variation and metabolic resistance in multinucleate fungi and offers valuable guidance for the sustainable management of fungicide resistance.

works.title: Extending the range of photosynthetically active radiation (PAR): the significance of far-red photons for photosynthesis
works.abstract: Photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) for oxygenic photosynthesis has traditionally been defined as the 400-700 nm wavelength range. However, recent studies revisiting the Emerson enhancement effect, an early demonstration of wavelength synergy in photosynthesis, have provided compelling evidence that longer-wavelength far-red (FR; 700-750 nm) photons contribute to plant photosynthesis far more effectively than previously thought when combined with shorter-wavelength photons. Nonetheless, the reported magnitude of this contribution varies among studies, prompting ongoing debate over whether the definition of PAR should be expanded to include FR photons. In this review, we (i) synthesize recent advances in our understanding of the photosynthetic role of FR photons and the physiological mechanisms underlying their synergistic interactions with shorter-wavelength photons; (ii) critically evaluate the factors contributing to differences among studies in the estimated photosynthetic contribution of FR photons, and (iii) discuss the implications of these findings for redefining PAR and improving the measurement and modeling of photosynthesis under both sunlight and electric lighting.

works.title: Multifaceted alfalfa improvement through FTO overexpression facilitated by an efficient MsPep1-based transformation platform
works.abstract: Alfalfa (Medicago sativa) as one of the most important leguminous forages globally, plays an irreplaceable role in the development of animal husbandry and ecological conservation. However, its low genetic transformation efficiency severely constrains molecular breeding progress. In this study, the application of elicitor peptides MsPep1 significantly increased the genetic transformation efficiency of alfalfa by 1.61 times and shortened the transformation cycle by 20 days. Using this improved transformation system, we investigated FTO, an m⁶A RNA demethylase gene that regulates plant growth and stress responses. In the greenhouse, overexpression of FTO in alfalfa significantly enhanced plant height, root length, the number of lateral roots, as well as drought and salt tolerance. Under field conditions, it substantially increased fresh weight per plant by 24.98%, relative feed value (RFV) by 10% and hundred-seed weight. Through transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq), we inferred that the FTO gene promotes alfalfa growth by regulating auxin, optimizes forage quality by enhancing secondary metabolite synthesis and enhances salt-drought tolerance by activating oxidative stress pathways. FTO mediates large amounts of m6A demethylation in plant RNA, altering chromatin composition and transcriptional activation. In summary, these findings provide molecular breeding support for developing novel alfalfa cultivars with high yield, superior quality and strong stress resilience.

works.title: Verticillium dahliae CAP-containing effectors hijack the β-subunit of the SnRK1 complex to suppress plant immunity
works.abstract: The soil-borne fungus Verticillium dahliae causes Verticillium wilt, a devastating disease threatening global cotton production. Like many pathogens, V. dahliae delivers effectors into plant cells to facilitate infection. The CAP (Cysteine-rich secretory protein, Antigen 5 and Pathogenesis-related protein 1) superfamily represents a typical group of secretory proteins that function as virulence factors and modulate plant immunity. Although V. dahliae utilizes CAP proteins to disrupt plant immune responses, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we initially screened the targets of VdCAP1 in cotton and demonstrated that it interacts with the β-subunit of SnRK1 complex both in vivo and in vitro. Silencing GhSnRK1β1 significantly enhanced susceptibility to V. dahliae infection, indicating its positive role in cotton defense against the pathogen. Further investigation revealed that VdCAP1 disrupts the interaction between SnRK1β1 and the core α-subunit of the SnRK1 complex and reduces the nuclear accumulation of GhSnRK1β1. Notably, GhSnRK1β1 exhibits opposing roles depending on its subcellular localization. Nuclear-localized GhSnRK1β1 promotes flg22-triggered ROS accumulation, whereas cytoplasmic-localized GhSnRK1β1 suppresses ROS accumulation. Furthermore, co-expression of VdCAP1 also promotes GhSnRK1β1-mediated ROS scavenging. Another secretory protein, VdCAP3, which functions as a plant immunity suppressor, interacts with GhSnRK1β1 and similarly restricts its nuclear accumulation to suppress plant immunity. Collectively, these findings indicated that VdCAP1/3 suppresses plant immunity by targeting SnRK1β1, thereby increasing V. dahliae pathogenicity.

works.title: Machine learning empowers plant virology: AI-driven mapping of host-virus protein interactomes
Plant potassium channel β -subunits confer antiviral defense via disrupting potyviral 6K2-mediated vesicle maturation and trafficking
works.abstract: Potyviruses constitute the largest known group of plant RNA viruses. Their 6K2 protein is an integral membrane protein that induces the formation of vesicular structures, which support viral RNA replication and act as vehicles for intracellular movement. While multiple host proteins are known to regulate either viral replication or movement, it remains largely unclear whether and how a single host protein can coordinately modulate both processes. Here, we identify NbKNB1, a Nicotiana benthamiana homolog of the plant potassium channel β-subunit. Genetic assays demonstrate that NbKNB1 confers antiviral activity against turnip mosaic virus (TuMV). NbKNB1 localizes predominantly to the plasma membrane in healthy cells, but relocalizes to 6K2-induced viral replication complexes during TuMV infection. Biochemical analyses show that NbKNB1 directly interacts with 6K2, disrupting 6K2 self-association and impairing the maturation of 6K2-tagged vesicles. NbKNB1 also competes with the viral cylindrical inclusion (CI) protein for 6K2 binding, thereby inhibiting TuMV cell-to-cell movement. A 6K2-binding-deficient mutant, NbKNB1Δ270-279, fails to restrict both viral replication and intercellular movement, confirming that direct interaction with 6K2 is required for NbKNB1-mediated suppression of TuMV infection. Moreover, NbKNB1 and its maize homolog ZmKZB1 also reduce infection by other potyviruses. Collectively, these findings reveal a novel antiviral strategy in which plant potassium channel β-subunit homologs target the viral 6K2 protein to counteract potyvirus infection, and provide a promising target for antiviral breeding.

works.title: C4 photosynthetic pathway fluxes in transgenic rice plants
works.abstract: Abstract Most land plants photosynthesize using the C 3 pathway, in which ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) fixes CO 2 into three-carbon acids. The C 4 pathway, a biochemical CO 2 -concentrating mechanism that operates in the context of specialized leaf anatomy to concentrate CO 2 around Rubisco, is more efficient. Introduction of the C 4 pathway into the C 3 crop rice could increase yield by 50%. Expression of five C 4 enzymes in transgenic rice previously led to flux through the first step. However, there was no evidence for flux later in the cycle. Here we developed new transgenic rice lines and protocols to detect C 4 -cycle activity: CO 2 fixation into C 4 acids by the carboxylation of a C 3 compound, decarboxylation, refixation of CO 2 by Rubisco and regeneration of the C 3 donor. We demonstrate that these four core C 4 reactions are operating in rice, establishing the in vivo flux framework needed to progress towards a functional carbon-concentrating mechanism.

works.title: TSL-phosphorylated SGS3 shifts RDR6 from terminal nucleotidyltransferase to polymerase activity to promote RNAi and immunity
Regulation of the 22-nt antiviral silencing pathway in tomato by two RNA viruses
Reply to Leuzinger and Körner: Increasing tree size across Amazonia detected by plot-networks
Trees grow until they fall: why small permanent plots cannot identify an Amazon carbon sink

works.abstract: Cover Legend The liverwort Marchantia polymorpha reproduces asexually through clonal propagules called gemmae. Gemma formation is controlled by a developmental program that balances auxin levels and restricts gemma-cell identity through the conserved microRNA MpmiR166A, which targets the transcription factor MpC3HDZ. The image depicts a gemma deficient in microRNA production due to mutations in MpDCL1a, a key enzyme in miRNA biogenesis; reduced MpmiR166a levels disrupt auxin homeostasis and release the repression of MpC3HDZ, leading to the formation of supernumerary meristems and papillae (pink), precursors of gemmae (blue) and ectopic gemmae (yellow), that emerge from the epidermal surface. works.title: How to build a shoot: insights from Physcomitrium patens
works.abstract: The evolution of body plans with multiple cell layers provided structural rigidity and enabled tissue specialisation, which were both essential for the colonisation of land by plants. Building such structure requires apical cell divisions that generate merophytes along all three axes (3D growth), as well as the spatial control of cell fate. The shoot (gametophore) of the moss Physcomitrium patens is an ideal model for studying these processes. Recent studies have identified a genetic network integrating hormone signalling, cell wall biosynthesis and cell shape to regulate division orientation in the gametophore. Additionally, reporter-based markers have revealed localised hormone activity that maintains the gametophore apical cell.
