This review summarises these findings to provide an updated perspective on 3D growth in Physcomitrium patens.

works.title: Navigating through complexity: a roadmap to disentangle multi‐level drivers of intraspecific seed‐trait variability and prioritise research efforts
works.abstract: Seed traits underpin plant regeneration and are central to predicting species' responses to environmental change, yet their intraspecific variability remains poorly integrated into trait-based frameworks. Progress has been limited by the conflation of processes operating across nested levels, from regions and populations to mother plants and individual seeds, and by weak integration of genetic drivers with environmental and phenotypic data. Drawing on published literature and analyses of seed traits in wild tree populations, we show that substantial seed-trait variation can occur among mother plants and individual seeds within populations, meaning that population-level macroenvironmental variables often capture only part of the observed variation. To address these limitations, we propose a roadmap to disentangle hierarchical drivers of intraspecific trait variability (ITV) in seeds. We outline a strategic plan to quantify seed-trait variation across hierarchical levels, investigate its drivers where variation is concentrated, and assess its consequences for recruitment and demographic outcomes. We recommend coordinated, standardised sampling and experiments that retain mother-plant and individual-seed identity, integrate genetic, environmental and phenotypic data, and use scalable approaches to link seed traits to performance across recruitment stages. Recognising and integrating ITV across nested levels is essential for improving predictions of plant regeneration under environmental change.

works.title: Jasmonate control of barley grain size across generations
SlExp1 Genetically Interacts With Cell Wall‐Modifying Enzymes to Coordinate Tomato Fruit Softening
Large variation of maize lines in acclimation to low phosphate availability and the synergistic coupling to nitrogen
works.abstract: Phosphorus (P) is an essential plant nutrient with low bioavailability in soils, and its uptake and that of nitrogen (N) are crucial for optimal growth. Here, diverse maize genotypes with distinct breeding histories, including doubled haploids from landraces, were grown under two P levels. The genotypes showed substantial variation in internal P concentrations and in performance under low P. Several lines maintained adequate N regardless of P supply; however, two lines from the heterotic dent pool performed poorly under low P and exhibited N deficiency. Only these lines lacked a robust transcriptional phosphate starvation response (PSR) in roots. Although N-related gene expression varied among lines, it did not explain differences in N acquisition. Inositol pyrophosphates (PP-InsPs), potential key regulators of P status signalling, were similarly diminished in contrasting lines under P deficiency, suggesting that they may be required, but not sufficient for PSR responses in roots. Overall, the results reveal large genotypic variation in low-P responses, line-specific N-P interactions at the post-transcriptional level and a critical role of shoot-root communication, which are discussed in the context of differential responses to P availability.

works.title: Sustained metabolic defense and male-specific volatile repellence shape tea plant- Helopeltis theivora interactions
works.abstract: Plant-herbivore interactions are shaped not only by plant defensive responses but also by herbivore perception of host-associated chemical cues. However, how tea plants coordinate chemical defenses and how Helopeltis theivora responds behaviorally to induced plant signals remain poorly understood. Here, we combined transcriptomic, metabolomic, behavioral, and electrophysiological approaches to dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying tea defense activation and herbivore behavioral adaptation. Following H. theivora infestation, JA signaling and its bioactive derivatives were rapidly induced. Meanwhile, phenylalanine accumulation and auxin metabolic remodeling increased progressively with infestation pressure. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed coordinated activation of the phenylpropanoid-flavonoid pathway as a central metabolic defense module. Pinobanksin-3-acetate accumulated substantially and was identified as a potential chemical component contributing to tea resistance. In parallel, feeding-induced (E)-β-ocimene emission increased significantly and elicited dose-dependent behavioral avoidance in adult male H. theivora, suggesting that this volatile may function as an olfactory cue for assessing host defensive status. Together, our findings reveal a complex ecological consequence of herbivore-induced defense: tea plants enhance metabolic resistance while simultaneously releasing volatile signals that may influence herbivore host-selection behavior. These insights provide potential chemical targets for developing sustainable pest management strategies through manipulation of plant defense pathways and insect behavioral responses.

works.title: Reciprocal Regulatory Interactions Between Class I TCP Transcription Factors and ABA Signalling Balance Growth and Stress Responses in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) plays a critical role in regulating plant responses to abiotic stress by modulating various physiological processes through complex molecular networks. TEOSINTE BRANCHED1/CYCLOIDEA/PROLIFERATING CELL FACTORS (TCP) transcription factors are known developmental regulators, but their roles in ABA signalling and abiotic stress responses remain poorly understood. We addressed this question by analysing the closely related Arabidopsis thaliana class I TCPs TCP14 and TCP15 using a variety of genetic and molecular approaches. We found that TCP14 and TCP15 negatively influence ABA and salt stress responses. They function by directly activating genes encoding negative regulators of ABA signalling, such as ABA-INSENSITIVE FIVE-BINDING PROTEIN 2 (AFP2), thereby suppressing the expression of ABA-INSENSITIVE 5 (ABI5) and downstream ABA-responsive genes to inhibit ABA responses under non-stressful conditions. Notably, the TCPs are targets of ABA-mediated regulation, as ABA negatively affects TCP14 and TCP15 protein abundance, providing a mechanism to limit TCP-dependent transcriptional growth responses and de-repress ABA-signalling pathways during times of stress. We propose that the antagonistic interplay between class I TCPs and ABA may serve to fine-tune plant growth and stress responses according to environmental conditions, positioning TCP14 and TCP15 as crucial players in balancing plant developmental progression and stress adaptation.

works.title: DOGL3 Maintains Seed Dormancy Under Heat Stress via Hsp20‐Mediated Protein Stabilization in Rice
works.abstract: Summary Statement In rice ( Oryza sativa L.), the DOGL3 protein maintains seed dormancy under heat stress by interacting with the chaperone Hsp20, which stabilizes DOGL3 and prevents pre‐harvest sprouting. Unlike its Arabidopsis homolog DOG1 , DOGL3 expression is induced by heat via transcription factors ONAC129, and HSFA2e.

works.title: An Antagonistic MdERF4–MdERF106 Switch Activates a MdWRKY33 Positive‐Feedback Circuit to Drive Irreversible Ethylene‐Induced Fruit Softening in Apple
works.abstract: Fruit softening represents a defining physiological transition of climacteric fruit ripening, yet the transcriptional mechanisms converting ethylene signalling into an irreversible developmental programme remain largely unresolved. In this study, we identify MdWRKY33 as a central hub linking ethylene signalling to cell wall remodelling during apple fruit softening. MdWRKY33 directly activates the cell wall-degrading enzyme gene MdPG, positively regulates its own transcription, and promotes ethylene production, thereby establishing a self-reinforcing regulatory circuit. Upstream of MdWRKY33, two ethylene-responsive transcription factors, MdERF4 and MdERF106, function antagonistically as a transcriptional repressor and activator, respectively. Ethylene coordinates this regulatory switch by suppressing MdERF4 while inducing MdERF106, thereby sustaining MdWRKY33 transcriptional activation and promoting rapid softening. Our findings reveal that an antagonistic ERF module is coupled with WRKY-mediated positive feedback to establish a robust transcriptional network that reinforces ethylene responses and drives irreversible commitment to the softening programme, providing mechanistic insights and potential targets for fruit quality improvement.

works.title: ZmTIP3‑1 Is Required for Seed Aging Tolerance via Modulation of Hydrogen Peroxide Homoeostasis in Maize
works.abstract: Summary statement This study reveals that the aquaporin ZmTIP3‐1 contributes to maize seed storage tolerance by likely facilitating H 2 O 2 membrane permeability and maintaining H 2 O 2 homoeostasis during aging. Its expression is regulated by ZmbZIP46 and ZmMYB9 , while its activity is modulated via hetero‐tetramerization with other ZmTIPs and interaction with the antioxidant enzyme ZmCAT1. Together, these findings uncover a coordinated H 2 O 2 ‑control module that links H 2 O 2 permeability to enzymatic scavenging, providing a mechanistic basis and a valuable breeding target for improving seed longevity and reducing post‐harvest losses in maize.

works.title: Temporal control of root system architecture under osmotic stress: ABA–SnRK2 signaling and adaptive plasticity
works.abstract: Drought and salt stress impose osmotic and ionic challenges on plant roots, with drought reducing soil water potential and salt imposing additional ionic toxicity beyond osmotic stress, driving the plastic remodeling of root system architecture (RSA). Abscisic acid (ABA) is a central hormone regulating root adaptability, and its signaling coordinates adaptive responses of roots across multiple time scales through the SNF1-related protein kinase 2 (SnRK2) family kinases. This review systematically summarizes the temporal coding mechanisms of the ABA-SnRK2 signaling network underlying root adaptation to osmotic stress. We propose that plant roots achieve a dynamic balance between short-term defense and long-term adaptation through the coordinated activities of different SnRK2 subgroups along the temporal axis. This proposed "balance point" of temporal coding is shaped by multiple temporal readouts. We also review how crosstalk between ABA and other hormones such as auxin fine-tunes root plasticity. Based on this framework, we propose a "balance point engineering" strategy that provides a theoretical blueprint for designing stress-tolerant crops with tunable durations of stress responses.

works.title: SlMED2 regulates locule number through the SlTPL−SlKNU floral meristem module
works.abstract: The Mediator complex subunit SlMED2 controls carpel number in tomato through promoter-proximal and long-range genomic interactions with the SlTPL-SlKNU floral meristem module, which represses SlWUS and SlCLV3, resulting in termination of stem cell activity.

works.title: Local auxin biosynthesis links cell wall remodeling to lateral root emergence
works.abstract: Auxin promotes lateral root emergence by remodeling surrounding root tissues. Cell wall modifications, including altered lignin deposition, are associated with successful root emergence, revealing a mechanism by which plants establish branched root systems to sustain growth and survival.

works.title: ZmSGT1‐mediated competitive protection of ZmBBI1 enhances maize resistance to Rhizoctonia solani
works.abstract: Banded leaf and sheath blight (BLSB), incited by the necrotrophic basidiomycete Rhizoctonia solani, is a devastating soil-borne disease that severely constrains global maize (Zea mays) production. Bowman-Birk inhibitors (BBIs) constitute a critical class of protease inhibitors in plant innate immunity; yet, their biological functions and upstream regulatory circuits in maize defense against necrotrophic pathogens remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we show that ZmBBI1, a BBI family member transcriptionally upregulated upon R. solani infection, positively modulates BLSB resistance. Its defense activity is strictly dependent on trypsin-inhibitory function, mediated by the evolutionarily conserved Thr52 and Arg53 residues in its canonical reactive loop. We identify Rs03254, a secreted virulence effector from R. solani, that directly engages ZmBBI1 and biochemically inactivates its protease-inhibitory activity to promote fungal colonization. We further demonstrate that the conserved immune co-chaperone ZmSGT1 physically interacts with ZmBBI1 and is genetically required for its full defense function. Mechanistically, ZmSGT1 competes with Rs03254 for binding to ZmBBI1, displacing the pathogen effector and restoring ZmBBI1's trypsin-inhibitory activity. Our work defines a tripartite molecular arms race module in the maize-R. solani pathosystem and uncovers a noncanonical role for SGT1 as a molecular bodyguard that protects host defense factors from effector-mediated suppression, providing actionable targets for engineering durable BLSB resistance in maize.

works.title: Precision recreation and multiplex stacking of disease-resistance alleles in tomato using optimized prime editing
works.abstract: Prime editing enables precise modification of plant genomes and provides a means to recreate beneficial alleles underlying agronomically important traits. However, efficient and multiplexable prime editing systems remain limited in dicot crops. Here, we developed optimized prime editing systems for tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) and applied them to engineer and stack disease-resistance alleles. Using three tomato prime editors, TomPE2, TomPE6c, and TomPE7, we recreated a naturally occurring resistance-associated deletion identified in pepper by precisely deleting two leucine residues from the CYSTM-domain proteins SlBs5 and SlBs5L. The resulting tomato lines exhibited enhanced resistance to Xanthomonas, demonstrating that a resistance allele can be functionally recreated across related crop species. In parallel, introduction of premature stop codons into the susceptibility gene SlDMR6 conferred resistance to both Xanthomonas and Pseudomonas syringae. Transcriptome profiling revealed distinct defense states: Slbs5/Slbs5L plants predominantly exhibited enhanced pathogen-induced defense responses, whereas Sldmr6 plants showed elevated basal defense. Comparison of prime editor architectures and culture temperatures revealed differences in editing activity and precision, with TomPE6c producing the highest proportion of precise edits. We further developed a modular multiplex prime editing system capable of simultaneously modifying multiple loci, enabling resistance alleles and regulatory variants to be combined within a single generation. The engineered alleles were stably inherited, and resistance phenotypes were maintained under elevated temperature conditions. Together, these results establish prime editing as an effective platform for precise recreation, engineering, and multiplex stacking of disease-resistance alleles and provide a framework for accelerating resistance breeding in crops.

works.title: Plant Single-Cell Metabolomics and Metabolite Imaging: Current Advances and Future Directions
works.abstract: Plants are multicellular systems composed of highly specialized cell types, whose distinct transcriptomes, proteomes, and metabolomes collectively shape growth, development, defense, and environmental adaptation. While single-cell transcriptomics has transformed our understanding of plant cellular heterogeneity, metabolites provide a direct and integrative readout of cellular biochemical activity and physiological state and can offer valuable insights into phenotype. They provide essential information that gene expression alone does not capture. Recent advances in mass spectrometry-based single-cell metabolomics (scMet) have enabled direct measurement of metabolic variation across individual cells and subcellular domains. In parallel, mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) has emerged as a powerful approach for mapping the spatial organization of metabolites within intact plant organs, offering new opportunities to connect chemical diversity with anatomy, cell identity, and biological functions. This review summarizes current technologies for plant single-cell sampling, scMet, and MSI for spatial metabolomics. It further highlights emerging efforts to illuminate the plant's cellular and spatial dark metabolome through spectral libraries, computational metabolomics, and AI-assisted annotation. A long-term objective is to build quantitative, spatially resolved, and biologically interpretable plant signaling and metabolic networks at single-cell resolution.

works.title: Comparative transcriptomics reveals a novel variant of an energy signaling regulator for lateral branch domestication in cucumber
works.abstract: Genetic alleles derived from wild resources are of great importance for crop breeding and improvement; however, connecting the dots between the functional variants and genetic traits is a significant challenge due to the need for precise, diverse, and large-scale phenotyping. Differential transcripts, which carry genetic variants or alternative splicing (AS) sites, may exhibit altered gene expression and protein coding, therefore influence phenotypes, showing their potential for high-throughput identification of functional genes. In this study, full-length transcripts were assembled and analyzed from eight developmental stage tissues of wild and cultivated cucumbers, utilizing PacBio Iso-seq and Illumina RNA-seq. We identified 6,980 genes underwent AS in cucumber. Approximately 66% of AS events were cultivar-specific, and genetic variants significantly increased around these divergent AS events. Based on the transcript structure of genes and variant annotation, we focused on cis-acting genetic variants that may affect gene function, in which a 21-bp insertion in the 5' untranslated region (UTR) of SnRK-Activating Kinase1 (CsSnAK1), an energy signaling regulator, was demonstrated to inhibit lateral branch development in cultivated cucumber by promoting CsSnAK1 mRNA abundance. Our work provides a straightforward yet reliable approach for integrating transcript structure and variant annotation to identify novel functional alleles in domestication traits.

works.title: Phosphorylation Alters the Condensation State of the Potato Transcription Factor bZIP18 to Enhance Plant Immunity
works.abstract: Biomolecular condensates formed by transcription factors (TFs) via liquid-liquid phase separation enable precise spatiotemporal control of eukaryotic gene expression. Although phosphorylation is a well-established regulator of TF activity, its capacity to remodel condensate organization and transcriptional function in plant immunity remains largely undefined. Here, we report that pathogen-induced phosphorylation converts a pre-existing TF condensate into a dynamic transcriptional hub to enhance the immune response in potato. Upon infection by the oomycete pathogen Phytophthora infestans, the mitogen-activated protein kinase StMPK9 phosphorylates the TF StbZIP18 at the conserved residue threonine 337. This modification triggers rapid changes in the nuclear StbZIP18 condensates, transforming pre-existing condensates into numerous smaller assemblies. The phospho-null StbZIP18T337A mutant maintains its presence in low-activity condensates and compromises immunity, whereas the phospho-mimetic variant StbZIP18T337E constitutively forms active condensates and enhances resistance. The gene encoding the TF StMYB44 was identified as the direct downstream gene target of StbZIP18. TurboID-based proximity labeling revealed that both wild-type StbZIP18 and StbZIP18T337E, but not the phospho-null variant StbZIP18T337A, selectively interact with the transcriptional cofactor StMBF1c to form transcriptional activation hubs that drive defense gene expression, including StMYB44. Together, our findings establish that phosphorylation-directed condensate reprogramming operates as a tunable phase-separation switch, converting a low-activity assembly into a transcriptional amplifier. This study unveils a biophysical mechanism for signal amplification in plant immunity and provides insight into how post-translational modifications modulate transcriptional condensate function.

works.title: Telomere-to-telomere assemblies of Glycine soja and Glycine max uncover novel genomic features of soybean
works.abstract: Achieving complete, gap-free genome assemblies remains a central challenge in genomics, particularly for repeat-rich plant genomes. Although several telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assemblies have been reported for soybean, highly repetitive genomic regions and the mitochondrial genome remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we assembled gap-free T2T nuclear genomes together with complete mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes for the wild soybean (Glycine soja) SoyW02 and the cultivated soybean (Glycine max) Zhonghuang 13. These assemblies substantially improved the resolution of repetitive genomic regions and enabled biological insights that were previously inaccessible. Comparative analyses uncovered a conserved subtelomeric exchange hub and refined the landscape of soybean satellite repeats, including pericentromere-enriched and chromosome-specific satellites. We further developed a de novo pipeline for identifying tandem duplication gene clusters, enabling systematic analyses of transcriptional and protein sequence divergence, and experimentally demonstrating expression and functional diversification between two duplicated oxidosqualene cyclases. Together, these assemblies establish a foundation for investigating the evolution and functional organization of repetitive genomic regions and will facilitate future soybean functional genomics and molecular breeding.

works.title: Distinct Splicing Complexes Formed by RS2Z32 Isoforms Modulate Alternative Splicing and Flowering
works.abstract: Serine/arginine (SR) splicing factors can alter downstream precursor messenger RNA (pre-mRNA) splicing patterns and influence gene expression. However, the influences of different isoforms generated by alternative splicing of SR proteins themselves on the transcription and splicing of downstream target genes in plants remain to be elucidated. Here, we demonstrate that the interaction between arginine/serine-rich zinc knuckle-containing protein 32 (RS2Z32) splicing isoforms and the Arabidopsis thaliana ortholog of human splicing factor SC35 (SC35) leads to the formation of distinct complexes, through which the recognition of splice sites within intron 3 of the transcription factor circadian clock associated 1 (CCA1) gene is regulated, ultimately resulting in an altered ratio of the CCA1 splice variants. Competitive binding of CCA1α and CCA1β to the flowering locus C (FLC) gene promoter can either promote or inhibit FLC transcription and flowering. This study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which RS2Z32 regulates FLC expression independently of its canonical splicing function, enhancing our understanding of transcriptional regulation mediated by splicing factors in plants.

works.title: The MaPUB23-mediated degradation of the MaHSFB1-MaHDA2 counteracts high temperature-inhibited chlorophyll degradation in banana
works.abstract: Banana fruits ripening at or above 30 °C soften but retain a green peel. Elucidating the mechanism underlying this high temperature-induced repression of chlorophyll catabolism would help to improve the marketability of bananas. Toward this end, we compared banana fruits ripened at 20 °C and 30 °C using transcriptome analysis, revealing several E3 ubiquitin ligases repressed in green fruits ripened at 30 °C. Among them, only the U-box type E3 ligase MaPUB23 promoted chlorophyll degradation when transiently overexpressed in tobacco leaves. MaPUB23 interacted with and targeted MaHSFB1 and MaHDA2 for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. MaHSFB1 specifically interacted with and recruited MaHDA2 to the promoters of chlorophyll catabolic genes (CCGs), transcriptionally repressed these genes via decreased histone acetylation, and inhibited chlorophyll degradation. However, high temperature attenuated the MaPUB23-mediated degradation of MaHSFB1 and MaHDA2, which enhanced the MaHSFB1-MaHDA2-mediated repression of CCGs. These results suggest that high temperature attenuates the MaPUB23-mediated proteasomal degradation of MaHSFB1-MaHDA2, leading to green ripening in banana fruit. This study thus illustrates a novel, dynamic regulatory module controlling the high temperature-induced repression of chlorophyll catabolism in banana fruits. Elucidating this mechanism provides a theoretical basis for strategies to manage temperature-induced fruit quality deterioration.

works.title: Polychrome activity profiling distinguishes Cys proteases and their isoforms in plants
authors: Renier A. L. van der Hoorn
works.abstract: Activity-based profiling with fluorescent probes is a powerful tool for the functional characterization of whole enzyme classes in crude proteomes. Here, we discovered that probe cocktails consisting of the E-64 warhead carrying different fluorophores via short linkers distinguishes the labeling of papain-like cysteine proteases and their isoforms because of their differential affinity to these probes. This causes 'polychrome labeling' with specific apparent colors for different protease families and isoforms. Polychrome labeling revealed differential labeling of isoforms of RD21-like proteases carrying C-terminal granulin domains. Molecular modeling of the RD21 isoforms revealed that the C-terminal granulin may create a fluorophore-binding pocket with the substrate-binding groove, implying that the granulin domain influences substrate selectivity. The concept of polychrome labeling may be widely applicable to other chemical probes for the characterization of protein families in all kingdoms of life.

works.title: ABA mediates seasonal drought-induced citrate accumulation in citrus fruit through transcriptional and post-translational regulation of CsMADS1
works.abstract: Seasonal drought at fruit enlargement stage increases citrus fruit acidity, but the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood. Here, CsMADS1, a MADS-box transcription factor, was identified as a positive regulator of abscisic acid (ABA)-induced citrate accumulation associated with seasonal drought in citrus fruit. CsMADS1 was upregulated by drought and ABA, and its expression was positively correlated with citrate content in citrus cultivars. Overexpression of CsMADS1 in citrus tissues enhanced citrate accumulation, whereas CsMADS1 silencing reduced it. CsMADS1 directly bound to the promoter of ANTHOCYANIN1 (CsAN1), a bHLH transcription factor involved in citrate transport, and activated its transcription. CsAN1 further activated CsPH8, a P3A-ATPase proton pump gene, thereby contributing to vacuolar acidification. In addition, the ABA-responsive protein kinase CsSnRK2.6 interacted with and phosphorylated CsMADS1 at Ser140. This phosphorylation enhanced CsMADS1-mediated transactivation of CsAN1 but was not strictly required for ABA responsiveness. Citrate measurements in citrus calli showed that CsSnRK2.6 promoted citrate accumulation mainly under ABA treatment and that the phosphomimetic CsMADS1S140D variant showed stronger activity than CsMADS1. Together, these findings support a refined model in which ABA regulates CsMADS1 through both transcriptional induction and post-translational phosphorylation, leading to activation of the CsAN1-CsPH8 pathway and citrate accumulation. Our findings provide insights into ABA-mediated citrate accumulation and suggest a potential strategy for improving citrus fruit quality.

works.title: A link to the past: the Bangia genome connects an ancient body plan to modern stress biology
works.abstract: Benjamin J M Tremblay; A link to the past: the Bangia genome connects an ancient body plan to modern stress biology, Plant Physiology, , kiag830, https://d

works.title: An Anther-Specific Sugar Transporter SlSTP9 Is Modulated by SlDof12 to Regulate Anther Elongation and Reproductive Success in Tomato
works.abstract: Successful pollination in crops relies on the intricate coordination between the anther and the style. However, the role of sugar transporters in modulating floral architecture and influencing pollination success remains poorly understood. This study investigates the function and transcriptional regulation of the tomato sugar transporter, SlSTP9, using a combination of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing, yeast functional complementation, microscale thermophoresis, transcriptomic, and metabolic profiling. We identify SlSTP9 as an anther endothecium/middle-layer-specific sugar transporter localized to the plasma membrane. Loss of SlSTP9 function results in impaired endothecium and middle-layer cell expansion, leading to shortened anthers, premature dehiscence, stigma exsertion, and ultimately pollination failure. In contrast, overexpression of SlSTP9 enhances fruit set. Functional assays show that SlSTP9 exhibits high affinity for fructose and galactose, and its loss in the slstp9 mutant leads to excessive accumulation of galactose, activation of phenylpropanoid metabolism, and premature lignification of endothecium cells. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Dof-family transcription factor SlDof12, which is also localized in the anther endothecium and middle layer, directly represses SlSTP9 expression. Overexpression of SlDof12 recapitulates the floral defects observed in the slstp9 mutant. These findings reveal a regulatory module involving SlDof12 and SlSTP9 that controls anther elongation by preventing premature lignification, highlighting a novel role for sugar transporters in shaping floral architecture and modulating reproductive success.

works.title: A GmGTF3A-GmSTF1/2 module governs GmPsbS -dependent photoprotection under high-light stress in soybean
works.abstract: Non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) dissipates excess light energy as heat, preventing photosystem damage. PsbS is essential for energy-dependent quenching (qE), but its transcriptional regulation in crops remains unclear. Here, we characterize the functional roles of two PsbS paralogs in soybean and identify a transcriptional regulatory module that governs their expression under high-light stress. We show that GmPsbS1 and GmPsbS2 are predominantly expressed in leaves, exhibit diurnal rhythms, and encode chloroplast-localized proteins. The CRISPR/Cas9-generated double mutant showed strong photoinhibition under high light, with reduced Pn, impaired NPQ, lower photosystem protein levels, higher ROS accumulation, and greater oxidative damage. Using yeast one-hybrid screening, we identified the bZIP transcription factor GmSTF1 as a direct activator of both GmPsbS genes. GmSTF1/2 activate their respective transcriptional expression by directly binding to the TGACGT cis-element located within their promoter regions, and overexpression of GmSTF1 in soybean enhances NPQ, mitigates oxidative stress, and confers improved tolerance to high-light stress. Furthermore, the C2H2 zinc finger protein GmGTF3A physically interacts with GmSTF1/2 and enhances their transcriptional activation of GmPsbS in transient assays, suggesting that it may function as a putative transcriptional co-activator. Collectively, our findings establish GmPsbS as a key photoprotective executor in soybean, with GmSTF1/2 and GmGTF3A cooperatively activating its expression to fine-tune NPQ under high-light stress, offering insights and targets for improving photosynthetic resilience.

works.title: Are plant annexins new components of protein complexes at membrane contact sites?
works.abstract: Annexins, as cytosolic and membrane-associated proteins, are essential for cellular processes in a wide range of eukaryotic organisms, spanning from humans to plants. They can bind calcium ions, phospholipids and cytoskeletal components, and thus play a crucial role in membrane organization, dynamics and trafficking, as well as in development and environmental stress responses of eukaryotes. A relatively new concept suggests that animal annexins AnxA6 and AnxA1 participate in protein complexes with other proteins, such as Drp1, Rab GTPase 7, TBC1D15, or FIS1, that are important for the establishment and function of membrane contact sites (MCSs) between several subcellular compartments. Plant annexins show diverse subcellular localizations, including putative MCSs between organelles, but their participation in MCS protein complexes is unknown. Despite limited homology with the MCS-localized animal annexins AnxA6 and AnxA1, bioinformatic analyses, AlphaFold-Multimer modelling and fluorescence confocal microscopy support a possible role for Arabidopsis annexins in MCS formation and function. All eight Arabidopsis annexins are predicted to have FFAT motifs that may be potentially important for MCSs formation between endoplasmic reticulum and other organelles. Moreover, there are plant dynamin, Rab GTPase, TBC1D15, and FIS1 and VAMP homologs, which might form functional complexes with some plant annexins in MCSs. This update provides a new perspective on plant annexins, presenting them as new putative players in protein complexes important for organellar interactions in MCSs.

works.title: Author Correction: Systemic movement of long non-coding RNA ELENA1 attenuates leaf senescence under nitrogen deficiency
OsERF27 ‐ OsPLT4 regulatory module and ROS equilibrium control temporospatial rice crown root patterning
works.abstract: In rice (Oryza sativa), the root architecture is heavily shaped by shoot-borne crown roots that arise from the phytomers at the stem base. Each phytomer typically generates two spatially distinct crown root populations - lower/proximal and upper/distal crown roots - that also emerge temporally, with the proximal roots forming first. The mechanisms that coordinate this temporospatial patterning, however, remain poorly understood. Here, we identify an AP2/ERF gene OsERF27 which is differentially expressed between proximal and distal crown root primordia and is specifically required for the timely development of proximal roots. We further show that OsPLT4 functions downstream of OsERF27, defining an OsERF27-OsPLT4 regulatory module that drives the outgrowth and emergence of proximal crown roots. Interestingly, we uncover a requirement for reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis in crown root development: Loss-of-function mutants display disturbed ROS accumulation pattern and sensitized root formation to ROS perturbation, indicating that this module promotes root emergence by spatially maintaining optimal redox balance. Together, our findings reveal a multi-layered regulatory network that integrates genetic elements with positional cues with redox control to pattern distinct crown root populations. Our study highlights how localized developmental programmes scale to shape root system architecture for tuning plant form and function in grasses.

works.title: Oviposition fluid protein NlOFP1 in the brown planthopper suppresses rice plant defenses
works.abstract: Insect oviposition fluid plays a role in the early recognition of plants and the initiation of plant defense responses. However, the characterization of oviposition fluid proteins and their relationship with plant defenses remains poorly understood. The oviposition fluid protein NlOFP1 in the brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens) is synthesized in the ovarian follicular cells and can be deposited into rice tissue. Functional studies reveal that NlOFP1 helps eggs resist desiccation stress. Furthermore, it can suppress plant defenses. NlOFP1-silencing leads to decreased honeydew secretion, fecundity, and egg hatching rate. Orthologs of NlOFP1 in other planthopper species exhibit highly conserved functions. Transgenic rice overexpressing NlOFP1 showed reduced lignin and salicylic acid, increased cellulose, and downregulated resistance genes, indicating weakened defense responses of plants. This phenotype effectively compensated for the adaptive loss caused by NlOFP1 silencing in the brown planthopper. NlOFP1 interacted with the photosynthetic electron transport chain component OsFeS. This interaction partially impaired the import of OsFeS into the chloroplasts and might lead to a decline in plant resistance. Our study reveals that NlOFP1 acts as an effector against plant defense responses and provides insights into pest reproduction and host defense evasion.

works.title: Engineering crop immunity: cyclic nucleotide‐gated channels as promising targets for broad‐spectrum disease resistance
works.abstract: Engineering crop immunity: cyclic nucleotide-gated channels as promising targets for broad-spectrum disease resistance

works.title: Duality of root‐dominated net soil organic carbon gain and mycelium‐mediated carbon loss in hyper‐arid afforestation
works.abstract: Afforestation regulates soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration via plant- and microbial-derived carbon (C) inputs, but root- and mycelium-derived C inputs differ in quantity, turnover, and stabilization mechanisms, and these differences may shift as stands develop. However, how root vs mycelium pathways drive SOC dynamics across a dryland afforestation chronosequence remains unclear. Using the ingrowth-core method along a dryland afforestation chronosequence (young forests, middle-aged forests, and mature forests), we quantified the contributions of root and mycelium pathways to SOC. The root pathway promoted SOC accumulation via particulate organic C and mineral-associated organic C inputs, contributing to 77.19-85.05% of the SOC changes. By contrast, the mycelium pathway induced net SOC loss via particulate organic C depletion, contributing to 14.95-22.81% of the SOC changes. SOC concentrations peaked in middle-aged forests, whereas relative SOC stability peaked in young forests. This study provides the first quantitative assessment of the distinct contributions of root and mycelium pathways to SOC accumulation and stabilization during dryland afforestation, advancing understanding of their roles in regulating SOC dynamics. As climate change intensifies land-use pressure, management strategies should integrate stage-specific root and mycelial traits to enhance SOC sequestration in arid forests.

works.title: ZmPHO2 ‐Mediated Phosphorus Homeostasis Modulates PAMP ‐Triggered Immunity and Disease Resistance in Maize
works.abstract: Maize production is influenced by both macronutrient-driven growth and resistance to various abiotic and biotic stresses. While phosphorus (P) is essential for maize growth and productivity, its role in maize immunity remains elusive. Here, we characterized a maize lesion mimic mutant, les33, which exhibits enhanced resistance to southern corn rust (SCR) and Curvularia leaf spot (CLS). Positional cloning indicated that ZmPHO2, encoding an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme involved in P homeostasis, was the causal gene. In les33, increased P level was accompanied by upregulated defence-related gene expression and elevated accumulation of phenylalanine-derived salicylic acid, lignin, and flavonoids, establishing a genetic link between P status and immune activation. Consistently, exogenous phosphate (Pi) application activates defence-related gene expression and enhances resistance to SCR and CLS in a hydroponics system. In particular, flg22-triggered defence marker gene expression, phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and burst of reactive oxygen species (ROS) were enhanced by Pi application, indicating a positive role of P in potentiating PAMP-triggered immunity (PTI). Moreover, field trials showed that application of Pi fertilizer improved SCR resistance in a Pi-dose-dependent manner, further supporting a critical role of P in maize immunity. Taken together, this study provides both genetic and agronomic evidence that P primes defence responses, and highlights optimized Pi fertilization as a practical strategy to coordinate growth and immunity in maize production.

works.title: Pikz , a Novel Allele at the Rice Pik Locus Conferring Resistance Against Magnaporthe oryzae
Functional divergence of the repressors of photomorphogenesis SPA2 and SPA3 during Arabidopsis seedling deetiolation
works.abstract: The COP1/SPA ubiquitin ligase is a key repressor of photomorphogenesis that is inactivated by photoreceptors to initiate light signalling. The four SPA proteins (SPA1-SPA4) confer functional specificity to COP1 during plant growth, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we used a domain-swap approach in transgenic seedlings to address the functional divergence of SPA2 and SPA3. We show that the respective N-terminal kinase domain determines the contrasting protein stabilities of SPA2 and SPA3 in light-grown seedlings. The instability of SPA2 correlates with a specific ability of the SPA2 N-terminal domain to bind phytochrome A in the light, suggesting that phytochrome A promotes the CUL4DET1/COP1-dependent degradation of SPA2 but not of SPA3. We uncover that the coiled-coiled and WD-repeat domains of SPA2 and SPA3 substantially differ in their activity in repression of photomorphogenesis, with those of SPA2 being more active repressors than those of SPA3. Thus, SPA2 combines a potent repressor activity with light-induced instability. We conclude that the evolution of SPA2 instability in response to light counterbalances its inherent strong repressor activity, thereby allowing seedling etiolation in darkness followed by rapid reduction in COP1/SPA activity through SPA2 degradation upon light-exposure as seedlings emerge from soil to initiate photosynthetic growth.

works.title: Everything, Everywhere, not at Once: How Abscisic Acid Shapes Root Responses to Salt Stress
works.abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a central hormone in plants to regulate salinity response, which is an increasing threat to plant growth and crop productivity. This review focuses on the role of ABA in salinity response in roots - an essential organ for plant nutrition acquisition and anchorage. It provides an overview of how ABA responses in roots vary across time, tissues, and salt intensity, and why these dynamics are essential for understanding root salt response. We present ABA-related gene transcriptomic profiles based on public transcriptomic datasets generated from salt-treated seedlings, including genes involved in biosynthesis, catabolism, (de)conjugation, transport and signalling of ABA. We discuss how genes and interaction networks governing each of these steps are coordinated in spatial-temporal, and salt-dose dependent manners. Finally, we highlight how ABA can potentially act as secondary signalling wave to regulate root salt responses, including the salt-avoidance response-halotropism.

works.title: Metabolite traffic: tracking chorismate and isochorismate reveals dynamics of aromatic metabolism
works.abstract: Praveen Khatri, Ved Prakash; Metabolite traffic: tracking chorismate and isochorismate reveals dynamics of aromatic metabolism, The Plant Cell, , koag334,

works.title: CsLUX-CsPME6/CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 modulates pectin methylesterification to coordinate cold tolerance and growth in tea plants
works.abstract: Cell wall pectin methylesterification is critical for plant defense and development, yet how it coordinately regulates cold tolerance and growth in perennial crops remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that cold stress significantly reduces the degree of methylesterification (DM) of pectin in tea plants, concurrent with extensive remodeling of cellular and subcellular structures, including enhanced xylem development, altered mesophyll architecture, and impaired chloroplast morphology. Genome-wide analysis identifies 100 pectin methylesterase (PME) and 42 PME inhibitor (PMEI) genes, among which CsPME6, CsPMEI8, and CsPMEI17 exhibit cold-responsive expression and localize to the nucleus and apoplast. Functional studies demonstrate that CsPME6 positively regulates cold tolerance in tea plants, while CsPMEI8 and CsPMEI17 act as negative regulators. Mechanistically, CsPME6 elevates PME activity to lower pectin DM, whereas CsPMEI8 directly inhibit CsPME6 activity to maintain high pectin DM. Also, CsPMEI17 also negatively enhanced total PME activity to enhance the cold tolerance in tea plants. Notably, our findings suggested that the circadian clock component CsLUX directly binds to the LBS motifs in the promoters of these three genes, activating CsPME6 and repressing CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 expression, which contributes to pectin methylesterification homeostasis. Besides, CsLUX-CsPME6/CsPMEI8/CsPMEI17 module also promote glutamate/γ-aminobutyric acid metabolism, leaf thickness, plant height, and root elongation in tea plants. Our findings underscore the importance of pectin methylesterification dynamics mediated by CsLUX-CsPME/PMEI involving cold tolerance and growth development in tea plants.

works.title: Phytochrome-Interacting Factors Regulate Katanin-Mediated Microtubule Severing to Control Hypocotyl/Mesocotyl Elongation During Skotomorphogenesis
works.abstract: The ability of plant seeds to emerge from the soil is achieved either by mesocotyl elongation in monocots or by hypocotyl elongation in dicots. Phytochrome-interacting factors (PIFs) are required for skotomorphogenesis, and microtubule remodeling plays a key driving role in cell elongation. However, the underlying cellular mechanisms in which PIFs act in concert with microtubule remodeling to control cell elongation during skotomorphogenesis remain unknown. Here, we demonstrate that in S. italica, the microtubule-severing defective mutant Siktn1 exhibits shortened mesocotyls and disorganized microtubule arrays. Similarly, in Arabidopsis, the microtubule-severing defective mutants lue1 and ktn80.1234 show shortened hypocotyls and abnormal microtubule arrays, which are caused by impaired microtubule severing. Intriguingly, pifq mutants exhibit shortened hypocotyls with reduced KTN1 and KTN80 expression, prompting us to investigate the relationship between PIFs and microtubule severing. Importantly, we found that PIFs transcriptionally activate KTN1 expression either in Arabidopsis or in S. italica. Further live-cell imaging confirmed that pifq mutants show reduced severing frequency and dwell time of the katanin complex. Taken together, these findings uncover a mechanism that PIFs orchestrate microtubule dynamics by regulating katanin activity, thereby fine-tuning cell elongation of hypocotyls/mesocotyls during skotomorphogenesis.

works.title: The CsANT1 Regulatory Module Coordinates Margin Lobing and Cell Proliferation
An ancestral T2 RNase provides insights into the origin and evolution of self-incompatible S-RNase
works.abstract: With the evolution of true floral structures, angiosperms have become the most diverse and successful plant group, a success largely attributed to the genetic diversity generated by self-incompatibility. The canonical S-RNase (class III T2 RNase)/F-boxes locus that mediates gametophytic self-incompatibility is present across multiple lineages of core eudicots, and its origin has been traced back to the last common ancestor of core eudicots. However, because class III T2 RNases are completely absent from non-eudicot taxa, the origin of this S-RNase/F-boxes locus remains elusive. Here, we identify a rare class TI T2 RNase (EVM0017713)/F-boxes locus in the basal eudicot Akebia trifoliata as a candidate S-locus for late-acting self-incompatibility, sharing molecular features with the S-RNase/F-boxes locus. The class TI T2 RNase subfamily exhibits a continuous gradient transition from class I to class III T2 RNase subfamilies in terms of phylogenetic distribution, molecular structural characteristics, physicochemical properties, and gene structure. Crucially, the class TI EVM0017713/F-boxes locus is ancient and collinear with the S-RNase/F-boxes loci. These results suggest that the class TI T2 RNase/F-box locus may represent an ancestral form of the S-RNase/F-box system, offering new insights into the origin and evolution of plant self-incompatibility.

works.title: Enhanced forest temperature regulation covaries with greater heat resistance of ecosystem photosynthesis
Widespread reversal of vegetation resilience in permafrost ecosystems
Root age structure governs long‐term architecture and hydraulic function in perennial plants: a modelling framework
works.abstract: Perennial root systems develop over decades and exhibit continuous turnover of structural and absorptive components, yet most root architecture models treat woody roots as permanent and neglect root age structure. We developed an empirically constrained modelling framework that explicitly represents age-structured demography, growth regulation and dormancy in perennial root systems (Vitis vinifera). We extended the functional-structural plant model CPlantBox to simulate perennial root development over decades by integrating age-dependent survival, secondary radial growth and climate-driven dormancy. The model was parameterised using unique three-dimensional (3D) root system data from young and mature grapevines, together with dendrochronological root age measurements, and coupled to root hydraulic properties. Empirical analyses revealed multicohort age distributions and substantial turnover of lignified structural roots, contradicting the assumption of a static woody scaffold. The model reproduced age distributions, order-specific survival probabilities and fine-to-structural root length ratios, and generated realistic, genotype-specific 3D architectures. Simulated uptake profiles and hydraulic scenarios showed strong age- and architecture-driven effects. Explicitly representing woody root age distributions and age-dependent processes may fundamentally change predictions of perennial root system architecture and function. The framework advances root modelling beyond annual paradigms and provides a transferable tool for analysing long-term architectural and hydraulic consequences of genotype × climate interactions in perennial crops.

works.title: Identification of auxin response factor ARF27 as a regulator of maize root morphogenesis
works.abstract: Auxin is a central phytohormone that mediates root development. This study investigated the genetic basis of auxin-mediated primary root growth in Zea mays (maize) seedlings, which is not well-understood in this key cereal crop. To address this knowledge gap, 618 accessions from the Wisconsin Diversity panel were leveraged for a genome wide association study (GWAS) followed by reverse genetics and in silico gene regulatory network reconstruction (GRN). The GWAS identified several candidate genes associated with variation in root growth responses, including RAMOSA2 and multiple members of the AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR (ARF) gene family. Maize AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR27 (ZmARF27), an ortholog of Arabidopsis ARF7 and ARF19, was prioritized for functional characterization. A reduction in ZmARF27 levels led to short primary roots, insensitivity to exogenous auxin, and altered transcriptional responses. Reconstruction of an ZmARF27 GRN included known maize classical root development genes, such as ROOTLESS CONCERNING CROWN ROOTS, numerous auxin pathway genes, and genes associated with cell wall biogenesis. Altogether, this study identifies ZmARF27 as a novel genetic driver of auxin-mediated root growth and gene expression in maize.

works.title: Soil engineering by an invasive ant reprograms plant growth–defense trade‐offs to entrench a tripartite mutualism
works.abstract: Ants are ubiquitous ecosystem engineers, yet the mechanisms through which their nesting activity regulates mutualistic interactions remain elusive. Here, we provide evidence consistent with the hypothesis that ant nesting initiates a soil-plant-herbivore cascade that reinforces a tripartite mutualism. Using the invasive fire ant Solenopsis invicta as a model system in both laboratory and field settings, we show that ant nesting increases soil nitrate and ammonium concentrations, which are associated with enhanced plant growth. These nesting-related changes coincide with shifts in the host plant's hormonal signaling network: auxin signaling is systemically elevated, whereas salicylic acid defense pathways and jasmonate signal transduction are suppressed. Plants associated with ant nests exhibit compromised defense responses to aphid herbivory. This shift toward a growth-biased physiology supports larger aphid populations, which in turn provide increased carbohydrate rewards for ants, augmenting ant colony survival and brood biomass. Collectively, our findings suggest a potential terrestrial feedback loop in which ants indirectly enhance their own performance through nesting-associated changes in soil nutrients and plant physiology, which ultimately benefit a mutualist herbivore. In doing so, this study establishes a tripartite ant-plant-herbivore mutualism that extends beyond the 'food-for-protection' paradigm as classically defined.

works.title: Harnessing Host‐Pathogen Evolutionary Dynamics to Engineer Bacterial Blight and Leaf Streak Resistance in Basmati Rice
From Mediterranean wild grass to resilient Atlantic crop: tracing the evolution pathway of black oat ( Avena strigosa Schreb.)
works.abstract: Avena strigosa is a neglected diploid oat adapted to low-fertility environments, but its wild progenitor and domestication history remain unresolved because of taxonomic uncertainty among related wild oats. We combined DArTseq genotyping of 298 wild and cultivated Avena accessions with chromosome counts, population-structure analyses, phylogenetic reconstruction, EigenGWAS, and botanical and archaeobotanical evidence. The A. barbata-hirtula-lusitanica complex resolved into three differentiated lineages: tetraploid A. barbata, a diploid A. hirtula lineage associated with drier Mediterranean environments, and diploid A. lusitanica distributed along the humid Atlantic margin. Avena strigosa was genetically closest to, yet clearly separated from, A. lusitanica. This differentiation, together with domestication-related morphology and reduced diversity in the crop, supports a geographically localized domestication from A. lusitanica, possibly in Galicia. Avena strigosa comprised distinct Iberian and non-Iberian European gene pools, consistent with northward dispersal and adaptation after domestication. EigenGWAS identified highly differentiated loci in genes associated with environmental responses, including components of the CBF cold-acclimation network. These results clarify the evolution of diploid oats and identify wild and cultivated germplasm of value for conservation and breeding climate-resilient oats.

works.title: Phosphoprotein Phosphatases (PPP), Important Molecular Switchers in Plant Cell and Environment Responses
works.abstract: Protein phosphatases, the executors of protein dephosphorylation, play indispensable roles in plant growth, development, and stress adaptation. This review summarizes the classification and biological functions of plant protein phosphatases, with a specific focus on the phosphoprotein phosphatase (PPP) family. By forming dynamic holoenzyme complexes with diverse regulatory subunits, PPP precisely controls vital cellular processes such as hormone signalling pathways, cell division, and light responses. Recent studies highlight the critical involvement of PPP in immune defence and abiotic stress adaptation, including drought and salt tolerance. Although PP1 and PP2A are extensively studied in non-plant systems, functionally dissecting PPP in plants remains an essential frontier, particularly in elucidating isoform-specific functions, mapping regulatory subunit-substrate-kinase networks, and decoding post-translational modifications. Looking forward, integrating phosphoproteomics with advanced toolkits, such as TurboID proximity labelling, AP-MS, substrate-trapping mutants, as well as single-cell and spatial omics, alongside bioinformatics, will be pivotal in overcoming these challenges. Ultimately, engineering regulatory subunit-PPP-substrate modules for crop improvement. Given that protein phosphatases are emerging as a pivotal regulatory hub for balancing the growth-defence trade-off, unravelling their multifaceted roles will simultaneously advance fundamental plant biology and drive innovations in precision breeding.

works.title: Competitive Binding of OsYAB2 and OsYAB5 to OsKAN1 Modulates Gibberellin Levels and Regulates Plant Height in Rice
works.abstract: Summary statement OsYAB2 promotes rice height by directly activating OsKAN1 and competing with OsYAB5 for OsKAN1 binding. This interaction modulates the OsGA2ox6‐GA pathway to enhance internode cell elongation through increased bioactive GA levels and SLR1 degradation.

works.title: The Tartary Buckwheat FtMYB15 Coordinates Cadmium Uptake and Detoxification by Regulating FtZIP3 and FtGSTU19 Expression
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Tartary buckwheat ( Fagopyrum tataricum ) is a crop of significant value, yet its cultivation in cadmium (Cd)‐contaminated soils poses risks to food safety. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of Cd uptake is crucial for developing strategies to minimize its accumulation. Here, we demonstrate that the Tartary buckwheat transcription factor FtMYB15 promotes Cd 2+ influx and enhances Cd accumulation in transgenic hairy roots. Yeast one‐hybrid (Y1H) and electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) results indicate that FtMYB15 binds to the MYB‐binding sites (MBS) of the FtZIP3 promoter, thereby upregulating the expression of FtZIP3 , which encodes a zinc/iron‐regulated transporter‐like protein. Overexpression of FtZIP3 similarly enhances Cd 2+ influx and Cd accumulation in buckwheat hairy roots. Further analysis reveals that FtMYB15 binds to the MBS in the promoter of the tau glutathione S‐transferase gene FtGSTU19 and upregulates its expression in buckwheat hairy roots both before and after Cd exposure. Overexpression of FtGSTU19 in buckwheat hairy roots enhances Cd detoxification capacity via its glutathione transferase activity, thereby alleviating Cd‐induced oxidative stress. Heterologous expression of FtGSTU19 increases Cd tolerance in Arabidopsis . Expression of FtMYB15 , FtZIP3 , and FtGSTU19 is induced by Cd stress. Together, these findings demonstrate that FtMYB15 directly regulates the expression of FtZIP3 and FtGSTU19 , thereby coordinating Cd uptake and detoxification in plants.

works.title: Plant Receptor‐Like Kinase‐Mediated Drought Stress Response Mechanism—From Root Sensing to Stomatal Regulation
works.abstract: Drought is a multifaceted environmental constraint that alters water dynamics across the soil-plant-atmosphere system. In order to survive under drought stress, plants must respond at several levels from cellular signalling to whole-plant hydraulic regulation. Although receptor-like kinases (RLKs) have been reported to play important roles in these responses, they are often studied within individual molecular pathways rather than as integrators of environmental and physiological processes. Here, we review RLK-mediated drought signalling organised across three interconnected spatial scales. At the root-soil interface, RLKs perceive osmotic and mechanical cues to regulate root architecture, aquaporin dynamics and apoplastic barrier formation, thereby tuning root hydraulic conductivity. Over long distances, RLK-peptide modules and reactive oxygen species waves transmit water-deficit signals from roots to shoots via xylem transport and cell-to-cell propagation, while RLK-dependent vascular differentiation preserves hydraulic safety. In leaves, RLKs modulate stomatal aperture through ion-channel regulation, ROS-calcium signalling, cell-wall mechanosensing and developmental reprogramming of stomatal density. Importantly, we highlight how these pathways operate across distinct temporal scales-from rapid electrochemical responses to long-term anatomical remodelling-and identify key unresolved questions, including how signalling specificity is achieved among redundant RLK members and how hydraulic and biochemical cues are integrated. By linking RLK-mediated signalling to whole-plant physiological responses, this review offers potential avenues for enhancing crop drought resilience through targeted modulation of RLK pathways.

works.title: Plant Phenotyping in Plant Factories: Progress, Challenges and Prospects
works.abstract: Plant factories with artificial lighting (PFALs) are enclosed vertical cultivation systems equipped with customisable LED spectral regulation, whose stacked spatial structure and controlled light environments substantially differ from open fields and conventional greenhouses, bringing unique and specialised challenges to precise plant phenotyping. Driven by high-throughput sensing technologies and artificial intelligence (AI), plant phenotyping in PFALs has achieved considerable advances. This review comprehensively summarises progress in PFALs plant phenotyping, covering sensing techniques including RGB imaging, multispectral imaging, hyperspectral imaging, and 3D point cloud reconstruction, as well as advanced analytical models integrating machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and AI agents for phenotypic data mining. We further highlight the important bottlenecks restricting the industrial application of PFALs phenotyping: commercial phenotyping devices are generally bulky, costly, and incompatible with compact vertical cultivation layouts, while the shortage of PFALs-specific phenotypic datasets and scenario-adaptive optimisation models hinders large-scale industrial translation. To clarify the differentiated technical characteristics of PFALs phenotyping, we systematically compare the discrepancies in phenotyping strategies, technical demands, and application scenarios between PFALs and traditional greenhouses. On this basis, we propose targeted solutions and prospective development directions for PFALs phenotyping, focusing on miniaturised and integrated phenotyping equipment, optimised AI-driven analytical frameworks, and multi-omics intelligent breeding. Distinct from previous general phenotyping reviews, this paper specifically targets the vertical, controlled PFALs cultivation scenario, systematically sorting out its exclusive technical challenges and corresponding coping strategies, and providing actionable insights for the future intelligent upgrading and industrialisation of PFALs / vertical farm plant phenotyping technology.

works.title: Chemical cues and cognitive models: Integrating metabolomics and AI for plant stress resilience
works.abstract: Plants make thousands of different chemicals that reveal how they cope with changing climates. This view explains how evolving artificial intelligence approaches can combine these chemical fingerprints with genetics and environment to build a digital twin of a plant, helping breeders predict performance and develop climate-resilient crops much faster.

works.title: Engineering AP/Exo‐Cas12 as an efficient toolbox for rice genome editing via integrated repair and exonuclease modules
works.abstract: A modular apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP)/Exo-Cas12 toolbox integrates cell selection enrichment with AP-repair pathways or exonucleases for plant editing. It achieves efficient multiplex genome editing and easily detectable large DNA deletions in rice, providing a robust platform for multigene knockouts and crop improvement.

works.title: An alfalfa MYB71 ‐centered activation–attenuation module fine‐tunes redox homeostasis and drought tolerance in Medicago sativa
works.abstract: Drought severely constrains alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) productivity, yet dissecting drought-response mechanisms in this important perennial forage crop remains challenging because of its highly heterozygous autotetraploid genome, the extended cycle required for stable transformation and regeneration, and the time-consuming evaluation of drought responses in mature plants. Here, we identified MsMYB71, a drought-responsive R2R3-MYB transcription factor, as a positive regulator of drought tolerance in alfalfa. Mechanistically, MsMYB71 directly bound to the promoter of MsPrxQ (peroxiredoxin Q), encoding a chloroplast-associated peroxiredoxin Q, and activated its expression, thereby promoting redox homeostasis under drought stress. In contrast, MsPRL1 (PLEIOTROPIC REGULATORY LOCUS 1, a WD40-repeat protein) and MsCUL4 (Cullin4, a Cullin-family scaffold protein) interacted with MsMYB71 and attenuated its protein accumulation and transcriptional output. To establish the physiological relevance of this regulatory module directly in alfalfa, we generated stable overexpression and RNA interference lines for all four genes. Genetic and physiological analyses showed that MsMYB71 enhanced drought tolerance and restricted excessive reactive oxygen species accumulation. Stable manipulation of MsPrxQ further established its positive role in drought tolerance and antioxidant defense. In contrast, MsPRL1 and MsCUL4 negatively regulated drought tolerance and physically interacted with MsMYB71. Their co-expression reduced MsMYB71 protein accumulation in a proteasome-sensitive manner and attenuated MsMYB71-dependent activation of MsPrxQ, consistent with an MsPRL1/MsCUL4-associated attenuation mechanism. Together, our findings define an MsPRL1/MsCUL4-MsMYB71-MsPrxQ module that couples transcriptional activation with protein-level attenuation to fine-tune redox homeostasis and drought adaptation in alfalfa.

works.title: Use of two-colour autoluminescent reporters enables quantitative imaging of gene expression in plants
Author Correction: Pathogen-induced condensation of the guard cell RNA-binding protein SAIR1 fine-tunes translation for immunity
Four universal modules and their combinations for decoding amplitude and frequency of Ca 2+ signals in plants
works.abstract: Summary Calcium signals are fundamental for plants and play crucial roles in developmental processes and in rapid responses to environmental stimuli and stress factors. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying the decoding of calcium signals in plants are still largely unclear. We have addressed the question of Ca 2+ signal decoding in a bottom‐up modelling approach starting with the thermodynamics of Ca 2+ binding to EF hands (EF: Glutamic acid–Phenylalanine) in Ca 2+ ‐binding proteins (CBPs). On this basis, we identified four universal, fundamental Ca 2+ decoding modules, in which a CBP modulates the activity of a target protein (TP). Representatives of these basic modules are omnipresent in plant cells. Their Ca 2+ dependent properties are mainly determined by the interaction of the CBP with the TP rather than the Ca 2+ ‐binding properties of the EF hands. Combinations of the modules generated complexes that are also observed in plants, which decode not only the amplitude but also the frequency of Ca 2+ signals by setting specific ‘frequency islands’ in which a TP is active. The modelling approach presented here addresses the decoding of Ca 2+ signals from the microscopic to the systemic level and could help to find the ‘Rosetta Stone’ for Ca 2+ signalling in plants.

works.title: Allometric scaling of adaxial–abaxial stomatal allocation in amphistomatous plants worldwide
works.abstract: Amphistomatous plants distribute stomata between the adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces, but whether this dual-surface allocation follows a predictable scaling relationship, and why species deviate from it, remains poorly understood. Here, we compiled a global dataset of adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities for 559 species across 380 sites and 63 families. We quantified their allometric relationship using phylogenetic reduced major axis regression and calculated amphistomatal scaling residuals (ASR) as signed perpendicular deviations from the fitted scaling relationship. We then examined variation in ASR among plant functional groups and across climatic and edaphic gradients. Adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities showed a significant allometric relationship after accounting for phylogenetic nonindependence, with a slope significantly > 1. ASR showed a significant phylogenetic signal but did not differ significantly between woody and herbaceous species, evergreen and deciduous woody species, or annual and perennial herbs. Individual environmental associations with ASR were generally modest, whereas the selected phylogenetic model retained multiple interaction terms, indicating that associations between ASR and environmental conditions were strongly context-dependent. By quantifying departures from adaxial-abaxial scaling, our study identifies a distinct dimension of stomatal allocation that is structured by evolutionary history and associated with multidimensional climatic and edaphic context. This framework provides a basis for testing the physiological and evolutionary mechanisms underlying variation in amphistomatous stomatal allocation.

works.title: Why be deciduous in a tropical savanna climate? Insights from leaf deployment, stem growth and sap flow dynamics
works.abstract: Savannas are ecosystems with hot and wet summers and warm and dry winters. How and why savanna trees partition their physiological activity through this seasonal cycle is unknown; yet it is important to understand this temporal partitioning in order to anticipate how anthropogenic climatic change will impact the functioning of savannas. In a South African savanna ecosystem, we examined the temporal pattern of leaf deployment, sap flow and stem increment phenology over three growing seasons for six species. We found that although the phenologies varied between years, there was a high degree of temporal overlap in leaf, sap flow and stem increment phenology between the six study species. Further, we found that a surprisingly large proportion of days on which the measured soil water potential was sufficient for physiological activity remained unused. Although our data are consistent with convergent selection for deciduousness, the unused soil water niche we detected suggests that climate should select for evergreen strategies. Possible explanations for the dominance of deciduousness in these savannas relate to the costs of leaf construction coupled with the risk of leaf destruction due to fire and/or foliovory.

works.title: Cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction of conifer fine roots
works.abstract: Winter snowpack loss exposes fine roots to freeze-thaw cycles at high latitudes and elevations, but the mechanisms of injury and reasons for species differences in vulnerability are not well understood. Motivated by yellow-cedar decline, we evaluated competing mechanisms of freeze-thaw hydraulic dysfunction (xylem embolism and cortical lacunae) and whether root economics strategy predicts susceptibility. We subjected 96 seedlings of four co-occurring Pacific Northwest conifers (mountain hemlock, western hemlock, western redcedar, and yellow-cedar) to seven daily temperature cycles with minima of 3, -3, or -9°C, quantifying xylem and radial conductivity loss, cortical lacunae, and root economics traits. Xylem conductivity loss was low in all species and treatments (mean 11-14%). Yellow-cedar averaged 58% simulated radial conductivity loss at -9°C, with lacunae occupying 20% of cortical area. Hemlocks (with pervasively lignified cortical walls) rarely formed lacunae, whereas cedars (with largely unlignified walls reinforced by phi-thickenings) were more susceptible. More acquisitive roots were more vulnerable, among and within species. Our results indicate that cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze-thaw hydraulic dysfunction, which was most severe in yellow-cedar. Vulnerability corresponded to cortical wall construction and root economics strategy, providing a mechanistic basis for yellow-cedar's unique susceptibility to snowpack loss.

works.title: Emerging roles of inositol pyrophosphates in plants: from environmental stress acclimation to hormonal responses and terrestrialization
works.abstract: Diphosphate-containing inositol phosphates, also known as inositol pyrophosphates (PP-InsPs), are energy-rich signaling molecules that orchestrate an ever-expanding repertoire of cellular processes in eukaryotes. Recent advances in analytical methodologies have been instrumental in detecting these messengers in plant extracts and characterizing the enzymology underlying PP-InsP metabolism in plants. Collectively, these developments have been critical to establishing PP-InsPs as emerging cellular messengers that control a broad spectrum of physiological processes, including immunity, nutrient homeostasis, growth, and development in plants. In this Tansley insight, we synthesize current knowledge on the molecular basis of PP-InsP metabolism and their physiological functions, and outline potential future research directions. We further discuss the putative role of PP-InsPs in plant terrestrialization, a pivotal evolutionary transition that fundamentally reshaped Earth's biosphere approximately half a billion years ago.

works.title: PELOTA at the crossroads of tomato fertility and viral resistance
works.abstract: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is a major threat to tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) production, and durable resistance remains challenging to achieve. We show that complete loss of function of PELOTA (PELO), a conserved ribosome surveillance factor underlying the resistance allele ty-5, confers near-immunity to TYLCV. Unexpectedly, PELO is also required for reproductive development; pelo mutants display severe floral defects, impaired male and female fertility, and complete sterility, revealing a previously unknown role for PELO in tomato plant fertility. Using CRISPR-mediated promoter editing, we generated novel PELO alleles with reduced expression that maintain fertility while conferring enhanced resistance to TYLCV, providing a new strategy.

works.title: Overexpression of REMORIN1.2 affects salt signaling and tolerance in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: Salinity is among the most detrimental environmental plant stressors hampering growth, development and immunity. Its impact is increasing due to intensive agricultural practices and climate change. The molecular components linked to the early cellular and molecular events triggered by salt are mostly unknown. Here we show that genes encoding for members of the REMORIN proteins family exhibit dynamic temporal regulation following salt perception. Analogously to pattern-triggered immune signaling, we observed that salt rapidly induces the reorganization of REMORIN1.2 (REM1.2) into plasma membrane nanodomains which colocalize with the actin-nucleating protein FORMIN 6. Overexpression of REM1.2 inhibits early signaling and late cell morphological responses to salt, defects which correlated with an increase in salt sensitivity. Our findings connect early salt-triggered signaling events to changes in cell architecture and root resilience and describe FORMIN-containing REMORIN nanodomains as a convergent articulation point in biotic and abiotic signaling pathways.

works.title: Integrative transcriptome meta-analysis distinguishes compatibility and incompatibility in rice- Xanthomonas interaction
works.abstract: Diseases caused by the Xanthomonas oryzae pathovars are important constraints for global rice productivity. Despite being a well-studied pathosystem, the transcriptional mechanisms distinguishing resistance from susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we present a systems-level meta-analysis of more than a hundred publicly available rice-Xanthomonas transcriptome datasets. Using appropriate analysis pipelines, stringent filtering criteria and metadata integration, we identified rice functions that distinguish disease resistance and susceptibility with temporal resolution. Compatible interactions were characterized by early activation of abscisic-acid biosynthetic and signaling genes, and extensive transcriptional plasticity associated with susceptibility gene activation. In contrast, incompatible interactions displayed a restrained transcriptome reprogramming, enrichment of phenylpropanoid and aromatic-amino-acid biosynthetic pathways, and enrichment of an AP2/ERF-GCC-box regulatory module. Transient over-expression of three conserved infection-responsive genes, OsJAZ11, OsSYP131b, and OsMYB45, modestly enhanced defense gene expression and reduced lesion length caused by X. oryzae pv. oryzae in rice leaves, thus providing a proof-of-concept relevance of the candidates to rice-Xoo interaction. We also developed RiceXtra, an openly available database hosting the analyzed data (http://tdb.ccmb.res.in/RiceXtra), for exploring gene expression patterns during rice-Xanthomonas interactions. Overall, our study proposes a mechanistic framework connecting hormonal signalling and transcriptional plasticity with disease outcome, offering a foundation for engineering durable disease resistance.

works.title: Transcriptional Regulatory Crosstalk Between Heat Stress and Nitrogen–Sulfur Nutrition in Plants
works.abstract: Plant responses to high temperature depend on the nutritional state in which the stress occurs. Nitrogen and sulfur shape this state through photosynthetic capacity, protein synthesis, nitric oxide production, and thiol redox buffering, while heat alters nutrient uptake and assimilation. We review how nitrate and sulfate nutrition interact with heat responses through direct transcriptional cross-regulation, metabolite- or redox-mediated regulation, and convergence on shared processes. Nitrate provides the clearest transcriptional link: in Arabidopsis, the nitrate-responsive transcription factor NLP7 regulates HSFA2 and HSFA3, encoding heat stress transcription factors that sustain chaperone expression and acquired thermotolerance, and rice NLP3 binds the HsfA3 and HsfA7 promoters under heat. Nitrate reductase-derived nitric oxide modulates HSF activity, and warm temperature represses the nitrate transporter and sensor NRT1.1 through the transcription factor HY5. For sulfur, evidence comes mainly from glutathione-deficient mutants, glutathione application and hydrogen sulfide donors, which alter heat-responsive transcription factors and antioxidant genes; whether sulfate supply acts through these routes, and how sulfate sensing and the sulfate-limitation regulator SLIM1 contribute, remain unresolved. Comparing published Arabidopsis transcriptomic meta-analyses, we identify genes responding to heat and to nitrate or sulfate and propose candidate regulators. In crops, nitrogen maintains photosynthesis under heat but does not consistently protect yield.

works.title: Bromeliad Brocchinia reducta , a rare carnivorous monocot, is a holocarnivorous plant secreting its own digestive enzymes
works.abstract: Carnivorous bromeliad Brocchinia reducta is a rare carnivorous plant. As a monocot, it is the youngest and most distantly related to the remaining ∼800 dicot carnivorous plant species.
