Although considered carnivorous for more than 40 years, it is believed that it does not secrete digestive enzymes and relies on microorganism-mediated digestion. Here we investigated the digestive physiology of B. reducta by measuring enzyme activity and using LC-ESI-MS/MS in response to feeding. We found prey-induced pH regulation and digestive capacity with secreted hydrolytic enzymes (e.g., aspartic protease, type I and III chitinase, GDSL hydrolase) similar to those found in other carnivorous lineages. Although the enzyme activity is rather low and comparable to the members of the carnivorous Sarraceniaceae family, the active prey response and presence of secreted enzymes placed B. reducta among truly holocarnivorous plants. Our results showed that a nutrient-poor environment exerts the same selective pressures on even distantly related plants and, through the process of convergent evolution, leads to the co-option of the same proteins for digestive function.

works.title: The Class I TCP TCP15 Interacts With the bHLH Protein CESTA to Shape Aspects of Brassinosteroid Responses
works.abstract: Summary statement In Arabidopsis thaliana , BR signaling promotes TCP15 accumulation, and TCP15 interacts with CESTA to regulate BR‐responsive genes and growth, uncovering a TCP15‐CES module within the BR transcriptional network.

works.title: Biotype‐Specific Regulation of Wheat Mono‐ and Diterpenoid Defences by Diuraphis noxia
works.abstract: Summary Statement While avirulent Russian wheat aphids trigger defensive mono‐ and diterpenoid production in resistant ( Dn7 ) wheat, these downstream terpenoids are suppressed by a virulent biotype despite inducing upstream jasmonic acid (JA) biosynthesis. Concurrently, DnDCXR is upregulated in the virulent aphid, which we propose acts as a metabolic effector that scavenges in planta JA to disarm host defences.

works.title: A century of soybean breeding increased photosynthetic capacity but not NPQ relaxation
works.abstract: Accelerating photoprotective regulation to improve carbon assimilation is a promising strategy to increase crop productivity. Although rapid non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) relaxation has been validated as a target through metabolic engineering, it remains unclear whether conventional breeding has improved this trait. Here, we investigated whether more than a century of soybean breeding enhanced NPQ relaxation alongside light-saturated carbon assimilation and seed traits. We evaluated a historical panel of 24 soybean genotypes across vegetative and reproductive developmental stages by integrating NPQ relaxation, gas exchange parameters, xanthophyll-cycle pigment profiles, expression of key photoprotective genes (VDE, PsbS, and ZEP), seed number and seed weight. NPQ relaxation parameters were not consistently associated with genotype release year, seed number, or seed weight at either developmental stage. The only exception was the amplitude of the rapidly relaxing NPQ component (AqE), which was negatively correlated with all three variables during the reproductive stage. In contrast, genotype release year was positively associated with maximum net CO2 assimilation rate (Amax), maximum carboxylation rate of Rubisco (Vcmax), maximum electron transport rate (Jmax), seed number, and seed weight, while Amax and Vcmax were positively correlated with seed number and seed weight. These findings indicate that the greater photosynthetic capacity of modern genotypes was not accompanied by faster photoprotective response. Thus, photoprotective regulation has not kept pace with gains in photosynthetic capacity under field conditions. We conclude that rapid NPQ relaxation remains an important target for synchronizing photoprotection with the high photosynthetic capacity of modern soybean lines.

works.title: Multi‐locus genetic basis of stomatal density and size in maize revealed by integrated QTL and GWAS
works.abstract: grasses such as maize remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated linkage analysis across three recombinant inbred line populations and a genome-wide association study in a diverse maize panel to dissect the genetic architecture of six stomatal traits. This approach identified 33 quantitative trait loci and 51 association loci for 6 stomatal traits and revealed a significant negative genetic correlation between stomatal density (SD) and size, with multiple genomic intervals showing co-localization of effects on both trait categories. By integrating reported cell-type-specific transcriptomic data, we prioritized high-confidence candidate genes, including conserved stomatal regulators as well as previously uncharacterized candidates involved in processes such as cell wall biosynthesis. Functional analyses of EMS-induced mutants for candidates ZmbHLH140 and ZmCESA6 demonstrated that loss of ZmbHLH140 reduces SD, whereas mutation of ZmCESA6 has the opposite effect. In addition, the signature of selection at the ZmbHLH140 locus is consistent with a role for stomatal regulation during maize domestication. Together, our results establish a comprehensive genetic framework for stomatal development in maize, highlighting both conserved and grass-specific mechanisms that shape stomatal patterning and offering a foundation for future functional studies of stomatal development in cereals.

works.title: The SlHYL1 ‐ SlRBP1 module integrates gibberellin metabolism to promote plant height in tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum )
works.abstract: SUMMARY Plant height is an essential agronomic trait that significantly influences crop yield and quality. The HYPONASTIC LEAVES 1 (HYL1), a core component of microRNA biogenesis, remains poorly understood in terms of its regulatory mechanisms on agronomic traits in tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum , Sl). In this study, we demonstrated that CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated knockout of SlHYL1 caused dwarfism, and partial suppression of SlHYL1 in tomato cultivar “Ailsa Craig” (AC) via RNA interference (RNAi) increased internode number but reduced internode length, resulting in a semi‐dwarf phenotype, confirming the role of SlHYL1 in regulating plant height. Cytological analysis showed that SlHYL1 suppression decreased both cell number and size within internodes. Yeast two‐hybrid screening identified that SlHYL1 interacted with another tomato RNA‐binding protein 1 (SlRBP1). Knockdown of SlRBP1 resembled the SlHYL1‐RNAi semi‐dwarf phenotype. Further studies revealed that the SlHYL1‐SlRBP1 module additively promotes the expression of gibberellin (GA) biosynthetic genes, thereby facilitating GA accumulation. Additionally, the dwarf phenotypes of both SlHYL1‐RNAi and SlRBP1‐RNAi plants were partially rescued by exogenous GA 3 application. Notably, unlike SlHYL1, SlRBP1 did not affect the biogenesis of most miRNAs. In summary, our findings demonstrate that the SlHYL1‐SlRBP1 module regulates tomato plant height by enhancing GA accumulation.

works.title: Bringing seed barriers into focus: Optimized clearing and histological staining
works.abstract: Plant reproduction relies on tightly coordinated developmental programs that integrate environmental and endogenous signals. Within seeds, lipid-based extracellular polymers such as cutin and suberin are deposited at defined apoplastic interfaces, where they function as selectively permeable barriers. These structures are actively remodeled by hormonal and metabolic cues to regulate hydration, nutrient exchange, and stress responses. Although the genetic and biochemical pathways underlying these barriers are increasingly well understood, their spatial organization and developmental dynamics remain difficult to investigate because they are embedded within optically dense and multilayered tissues. Existing clearing approaches have substantially improved visualization of internal seed structures, yet systematic whole-mount imaging of multiple lipid-based barriers across development, particularly in combination with fluorescent reporters, remains challenging. To address this, we developed an optimized pipeline that enables rapid and efficient seed tissue clearing and selective visualization of polyaliphatic barriers across four key seed interfaces: the seed surface, seed coat suberin, cuticle at the endosperm/seed coat boundary, and embryo surface cuticle. The method preserves the spatial context of these barriers within intact seeds and enables their co-visualization with fluorescence-based marker lines. Using a common whole-mount imaging framework across successive developmental stages, we follow changes in the spatial organization of distinct barrier domains. The approach is also applicable to more complex seeds, such as those of Camelina sativa, and can be extended to other anatomically complex plant organs by combining the clearing and staining workflow with vibratome sectioning.

works.title: GmRVE8a , a circadian clock‐associated gene, negatively regulates flowering and maturity in soybean
works.abstract: SUMMARY Precise regulation of flowering time and maturity is critical for achieving high and stable soybean yields, and the circadian clock plays a central role in coordinating these developmental transitions. Soybean is a typical short‐day crop with a pronounced photoperiodic response; however, the molecular mechanisms linking circadian regulation to photoperiod‐dependent flowering and maturity remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated genome‐wide association analysis with deep learning approaches using 257 soybean germplasm accessions spanning 14 maturity groups and identified GmRVE8a , a homolog of the Arabidopsis circadian clock gene REVEILLE , as a strong candidate locus associated with soybean maturity across two field environments. Haplotype analysis demonstrated that accessions carrying the GmRVE8a H1 haplotype consistently flowered and matured significantly later than those carrying GmRVE8a H2 . Functional validation revealed that knockout of GmRVE8a markedly accelerated flowering and maturity, whereas overexpression of GmRVE8a significantly delayed both processes. qRT‐PCR assays further suggested that GmRVE8a may repress flowering and delay maturity by promoting the expression of GmFT4 , a flowering‐inhibitory member of the FT family, and is unlikely to act by directly regulating E1 expression. Collectively, our findings suggest GmRVE8a as a circadian clock‐associated negative regulator of soybean flowering and maturity, and highlight it as a promising candidate for molecular breeding aimed at improving adaptation to diverse photoperiodic environments.

works.title: Telomere‐to‐telomere genome assembly of the endangered Jacktree ( Sinojackia xylocarpa Hu) reveals its centromeric landscape and evolutionary dilemma as a small population
works.abstract: The endangered status of many plant species is often attributed to a decline in fitness, which drives a sustained decrease in population size under natural conditions. However, the role of highly repetitive genomic regions in the decline of endangered plants remains poorly understood. Here, we present the gap-free telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome for the endangered Jacktree (Sinojackia xylocarpa Hu). It has a genome size of 961.94 Mb, an N50 of 78.05 Mb, and 36 446 predicted protein-coding genes. Using CENH3 chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), we identified centromeric regions across all 12 chromosomes and revealed that S. xylocarpa centromeres are composed of diverse transposable element (TE) families, with long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons and LINE elements as major components. Notably, the right arm of chromosome 1 exhibited ectopic CENH3 enrichment and a TE accumulation similar to that of centromeric regions, suggesting the formation of a centromere-like chromatin domain. In addition, we detected inversion polymorphisms and inversion heterozygotes in natural populations, predominantly concentrated on the same chromosomal arm. These features may be associated with meiotic abnormalities. Using a high-quality T2T genome assembly, we identified a pattern of genomic erosion facing these small populations characterized by local suppression of recombination linked LTR proliferation and by the accumulation of deleterious mutations in DNA repair genes. This genomic erosion creates an evolutionary dilemma that impairs the purging of deleterious alleles, ultimately threatening long-term adaptability and survival. This study highlights the utility of T2T genome assembly for the conservation of endangered plants.

works.title: Arabidopsis thaliana BOLA proteins, new actors in plant growth and iron homeostasis
works.abstract: The universal iron-sulfur (Fe-S) clusters embedded in proteins support numerous fundamental biological processes. However, many proteins involved in Fe-S assembly machineries remain poorly characterized in plants. Here, we revealed that BOLA1 and BOLA4, two members of the BOLA family previously described as Fe-S assembly factors in various organisms, are critical growth regulators that play a role in Fe homeostasis in Arabidopsis thaliana. Expression analyses showed that BOLA1 and BOLA4 are ubiquitously expressed across most Arabidopsis tissues. Using protoplast transfection assays, we also demonstrated that both BOLA-GFP fusion proteins localize to chloroplasts and mitochondria. Mutant analyses revealed that while single bola1 or bola4 knock-out mutants are phenotypically indistinguishable from the wild type, double bola1 bola4 mutants display severe growth defects, including early growth arrest of the primary root. Notably, this phenotype was rescued by grafting a wild-type root system onto the bola1 bola4 aerial part. Fe quantification, Perls staining, and RT-qPCR analyses further demonstrated that bola1 bola4 double mutants exhibit altered Fe distribution and Fe-homeostasis-related gene expression. Overall, our findings show that BOLA1 and BOLA4 act redundantly to maintain primary root growth and rosette development and are essential players in Fe signaling and partitioning in Arabidopsis.

works.title: Two nearly complete genomes reveal the molecular mechanism underlying the significant fruit quality differences caused by bud sport between yellow and white‐fleshed loquat ( Eriobotrya japonica L.)
works.abstract: SUMMARY Bud sport is a common and stable somatic variation in perennial fruit trees. Loquat ( Eriobotrya japonica L.) is an evergreen fruit tree that can be categorized into yellow‐fleshed and white‐fleshed types based on the flesh color. To uncover the genetic basis, we herein assembled two nearly complete genomes for a yellow‐fleshed ‘Dongting’ loquat (TBY) and its white‐fleshed bud sport (TBW). The final sizes of assemblies were 773.29 Mb and 728.86 Mb with contig N50 of 31.87 Mb and 28.63 Mb for TBY and TBW, respectively. Comparative genomics analysis indicated that the heterozygosity ratio of TBY was nearly two‐fold higher than that of TBW (0.53% vs. 0.27%). Integrated multi‐omics and molecular marker detection results revealed that homozygosity of the EjPSY2A d / EjPSY2A d allele is the cause of the change in flesh color from yellow to white in TBY. Additionally, EjSUSs ( −1 , −2 , −3 , −12 ) and EjSPS3 might be the key genes responsible for the significant accumulation of hexoses and sucrose, respectively, in the flesh of TBY and TBW. Furthermore, high expression of EjC4H8 and Ej4CLs ( −7 , −10 , −20 ) in TBY might lead to the accumulation of more lignin in its flesh. Taken together, these findings provide valuable insights into the molecular mechanism differences between yellow‐ and white‐fleshed loquat and highlight the significance of bud sport as a valuable approach for generating novel germplasm resources in fruit trees.

works.title: Population genomics of heterosporous lycophytes: allopatric speciation and historical persistence through paleoclimatic fluctuations
works.abstract: Speciation is the fundamental process driving the origin of earth biodiversity. While speciation mechanisms have been revealed in many plant taxa, the evolutionary dynamics of heterosporous lycophytes remain largely unexplored. Here, we used the Selaginella sanguinolenta group, comprising seven montane species in eastern Asia, as a model system. We generated a high-quality, chromosome-level reference genome for S. aitchisonii, conducted whole-genome resequencing of 191 individuals across 49 populations, and integrated population genomic, phylogenomic, morphological, and ecological analyses. Our results revealed that strong geographic isolation, driven by Miocene paleogeographic events, led to high genetic differentiation and restricted interspecific gene flow. The unique combination of heterospory and independent gametophyte generations might exacerbate extreme inbreeding, further impeding the ability of these lineages to surmount geographical barriers. Ecological niche divergence indicated that these species experience heterogeneous selection pressures; moreover, evidence of selective sweeps, leaf arrangement variation, and functional gene divergence indicates that natural selection gives rise to new species with environmentally adaptive traits. Demographic reconstructions revealed a shared trajectory of expansion followed by contraction into bottlenecks from the late Miocene to the Pliocene. Montane refugia likely played a role in species persistence, preserving genetic diversity for the postglacial expansions observed in four species since the Last Interglacial. We conclude that the S. sanguinolenta group underwent allopatric speciation since the Miocene and successfully persisted through severe Quaternary climatic fluctuations, which provides novel insights based on population genomic analysis into the evolution of early-diverging vascular plants.

works.title: An S‐domain receptor‐like kinase regulates auxin distribution and root gravitropism via MPK signaling in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: Root system architecture (RSA) varies across environments and plays essential roles in plant adaptive growth. Auxin and its polar transport have been found to be key players in the regulation of RSA. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of RSA in fluctuating environments remain unclear. Using a forward genetic screen for root mutants under gravitropism interference conditions in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana, we revealed that HYPERSENSITIVE TO IBUPROFEN1 (HIB1) regulates root gravitropic growth and RSA by modulating auxin distribution in Arabidopsis. The hib1 seedlings presented defects in primary root elongation, lateral root organogenesis, and the root gravitropic response because of abnormal auxin distribution. Notably, the gravitropic defects of hib1 roots were correlated with increased MPK6 activity and could be rescued by loss-of-function mpk6 mutation. Furthermore, cell biological results revealed that HIB1 regulated PIN protein polar distribution and abundance at the plasma membrane, indicating that HIB1 is involved in polar auxin transport and the subsequent auxin response. Indeed, genetic perturbation of HIB1 results in impaired gravitropic root growth. Our work revealed that the HIB1-auxin module regulates root gravitropism and RSA, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying adaptive root growth.

works.title: Altered plastidial fatty‐acid condensation is associated with changes in membrane composition and postembryonic leaf development in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: Membrane lipid composition is fundamental to organelle structure and environmental adaptation, yet how plastidial fatty acid metabolism influences developmental plasticity remains poorly understood. We examined the effects of sustained elevation of the plastidial fatty-acid enzymes KASII (β-ketoacyl-ACP synthase II) and SSI2 (Δ9 stearoyl-ACP desaturase 2) in Arabidopsis thaliana using lipidomic, ultrastructural, cellular, molecular, and physiological analyses. KASII overexpressing plants (KASIIox), but not SSI2 overexpressing plants (SSI2ox), increased carbon 18-containing lipid species and exhibited reduced plastidial galactolipids together with increased extraplastidial phospholipids. KASIIox plants displayed enlarged chloroplasts with disrupted thylakoid organization, impaired palisade differentiation, altered mesophyll patterning, and reduced seed coat mucilage. Under low light, KASIIox plants failed to exhibit the characteristic petiole elongation observed in control and SSI2ox plants, accompanied by altered phyB and PIF4 protein abundance. Exogenous gibberellin intensified, whereas inhibition of gibberellin biosynthesis partially alleviated KASIIox leaf and cellular phenotypes. Together, these findings associate sustained KASII elevation with changes in membrane lipid composition, chloroplast architecture, light-responsive growth, and postembryonic leaf development, supporting a link between plastidial fatty-acid metabolism and developmental responses to light and gibberellin availability.

works.title: In conversation with Dr. María Fernanda Gómez
works.abstract: she expanded her expertise in plant biochemistry and metabolomics

works.title: Expression of a chimeric OXR protein remodels rice architecture for enhanced grain yield by modulating redox and hormonal pathways
works.abstract: SUMMARY The growth–defence trade‐off limits crop biotechnology because stress adaptation typically reduces productivity. We engineered and characterised OXR‐Q12 (Q12), a mitochondrial chimeric protein combining the regulatory N‐terminus of AtOXR1 with the catalytic TLDc domain of AtOXR2. In silico analysis predicted higher stability for Q12 than for native orthologues. Constitutive Q12 expression in Arabidopsis and rice ( Oryza sativa ) increased biomass, remodelled stem and vascular architecture, and enhanced grain yield. OsQ12 rice plants showed an ideal erect canopy leaf phenotype, productive tillering and a robust root system. Physiologically, Q12 conferred salinity and drought tolerance by establishing a primed basal redox state with elevated non‐toxic H 2 O 2 and an expanded glutathione content. Depleting this H 2 O 2 pool with exogenous ascorbate selectively reverses seedling growth, salinity tolerance, and leaf erectness, indicating that this basal redox priming is a principal driver of these phenotypic adaptations. Mechanistically, our data support a model in which Q12 uncouples stress resilience from growth penalties by attenuating brassinosteroid (BR) signalling, downregulating biosynthesis ( OsBRD1 ) and positive transcriptional regulators ( OsBZR1 , OsDLT and OsILI1 ), and differentially modulating the abscisic acid (ABA) response: the stress‐protection is kept, while the side that normally brakes growth is attenuated. Q12 lines exhibit partial resistance to ABA‐mediated growth and germination inhibition, yet display transcriptional hyperinduction of stress‐protective marker genes ( OsNCED3/4 , OsDREB2A ) upon salinity exposure. This redox‐mediated signal may enable rapid activation of protective pathways without typical metabolic costs or growth reduction. Our results show that engineering modular OXR proteins can overcome traditional physiological trade‐offs, supporting the development of high‐yielding, resilient crops.

works.title: Single‐nucleus transcriptomics reveals transcriptional dynamics underlying maize ligule development
works.abstract: The maize ligule arises from the preligule band (PLB) at the leaf blade-sheath boundary and provides a tractable system for investigating how boundary-associated positional cues direct local cell-fate specification and tissue outgrowth. Although key genes involved in ligule development have been identified and cell-resolved profiles are available for stages after PLB formation, how PLB acquires ligule identity and initiates outgrowth remains unclear at the cellular level. Here, we have used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to profile maize ligular regions at the preligule band and ligule outgrowth stages. The atlas resolved major cell populations and identified a ligule population supported by established marker genes, published laser microdissection transcriptomes, and RNA in situ hybridization. Pseudotime trajectory and co-expression network analyses resolved two sequential transcriptional programs corresponding to ligule initiation and subsequent outgrowth. ZmIDD30 was identified as a promising candidate transcriptional regulator, and molecular assays showed that it bound to the promoters of ZmPIN1c and ZmVG1 and activated their transcription, suggesting potential links to auxin transport and lipid metabolism during ligule development. Overall, these findings define a cell-resolved transcriptional progression in which a localized epidermal domain at the blade-sheath boundary progressively acquires ligule identity and progresses toward outgrowth.

works.title: Waterlogging stress disarms nicotine‐mediated defense to herbivores through the bHLH1 ‐ ERF1 transcriptional switch
works.abstract: Global climate change has intensified the frequency of flooding events, which not only threaten crop productivity but also drastically alters herbivore population dynamics, often leading to more severe pest outbreaks. However, the molecular mechanisms by which waterlogging reprograms plant insect resistance remain elusive. Here we show that waterlogging stress impairs the resistance of Nicotiana benthamiana to herbivores by reducing nicotine accumulation through downregulation of key biosynthetic genes, N-methyltransferase (PMT), and phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT). We further reveal that this process is precisely regulated by the JA-mediated bHLH1-ERF1 module. Normally, this module acts as a positive regulator of nicotine biosynthesis. Under waterlogging, impaired JA synthesis in roots leads to downregulation of NbbHLH1, thereby suppressing NbERF1 expression. Consequently, the downregulation of both NbERF1 and NbbHLH1 directly switches off the transcription of NbPMT and NbQPRT, leading to reduced nicotine accumulation and compromised plant resistance. Critically, the bHLH1-ERF1 module also negatively regulates waterlogging tolerance, thereby acting as a transcriptional switch that disarms defense to prioritize survival. These findings reveal the molecular mechanism governing plant trade-offs under combined stresses.

works.title: Deciphering the contributions of hybridization and genome dosage to vegetative vigor in perennial forage maize
works.abstract: SUMMARY Heterosis and genomic dosage each enhance plant vigor, yet their manifestation and underlying mechanisms in vegetative growth, particularly within polyploid systems, remain unclear. We synthesized and analyzed a series of Zea – Tripsacum allopolyploid trihybrids (MTPs) with varying genomic compositions to dissect the synergistic contributions of hybridization and polyploidy/aneuploidy effects to vegetative vigor. We demonstrate that increased Z. perennis genome dosage directly enhances fresh weight (FW) and photosynthetic capacity, whereas interspecific hybridization‐triggered extensive transcriptome reprogramming. Heterotic hybrids exhibited transcriptional signatures of improved energy use efficiency, characterized by the downregulation of energy‐costly protein quality control systems and upregulation of energy metabolism and carbon fixation pathways. Co‐expression network analysis linked modules of fructose metabolism and glycolysis positively to FW heterosis, while protein folding modules were negatively correlated. Field trials confirmed the agronomic superiority of elite MTP‐derived perennial forage cultivars, Yucao 6 and Yucao 9919, which achieved high yields (127.68–142.61 t ha −1 ) across diverse ecological zones, 156.28–186.25% higher than conventional silage maize. These perennial forage cultivars can be harvested for many years after a single planting, substantially lowering production costs and providing a practical option for utilizing sloping and abandoned lands in southern China. Our findings clarify how hybridization and genomic dosage, via transcriptional remodeling, jointly boost plant vigor, offering both a mechanistic framework and a practical breeding roadmap for integrating heterosis and genomic dosage strategies in crop improvement.

works.title: Beyond leaf mass per area: anatomical and economic drivers of toughness in evergreen and deciduous oaks
works.abstract: We examined how leaf habit (deciduous versus evergreen) shapes the structural, mechanical, and chemical traits of oaks (genus Quercus), aiming to determine whether evergreen leaf toughness arises from intrinsic chemical investment or greater tissue allocation per unit area. Leaves from 33 oak species were sampled, focusing on interveinal lamina. Morphological traits (LMA, thickness, density), mechanical properties, and cell wall composition (cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, cutin, nitrogen) were measured. The fiber fraction composition was used to estimate the construction costs and heat of combustion. Comparisons between deciduous and evergreen species were made on area- and mass-bases. Evergreen leaves had higher leaf mass per area, thickness, and toughness than deciduous leaves, with partial overlap in LMA. Area-based investments in cell wall polymers and construction costs were consistently higher in evergreens. Mass-based fiber construction costs were lower in evergreens, reflecting the dominance of metabolically inexpensive polysaccharides, whereas deciduous fibers contained more energetically costly compounds such as lignin and cutin. Evergreen leaf toughness is primarily driven by tissue quantity (LMA) and specific anatomical reinforcement rather than intrinsic fiber cost. Deciduous leaves are mechanically weaker, despite higher mass-based fiber cost. These results highlight a decoupling between chemical investment and mechanical properties and show how leaf structural design underpins functional divergence between leaf habits.

works.title: Fruit color and size provide reliable signals of macronutritional rewards for seed dispersers
works.abstract: Fruit color and size provide vital cues for determining seed dispersers' preferences; however, any consistent underlying link between these traits and fruit macronutritional rewards remains to be established by large-scale analyses. We collated a global database comprising 2626 observations of 1626 fruiting plant species from 460 global sites to test whether fruit color and size traits do indeed consistently signal macronutritional rewards to frugivores. We found that consistent fruit color and size signaled macronutrient reward specifically relating to bird-, mammal-, and mixed-dispersed dispersal syndromes. Lipids were the predominant macronutrient in black, blue, red, orange, and yellow fruits with birds (27.24%), whereas sugar predominated in mammal-dispersed fruits (72.55%). Fruits dispersed by mammals (25.55 mm) were consistently larger than those dispersed by birds (10.17 mm) regardless of fruit color, and total macronutrient mass per fruit increased with fruit size. These signal-mutualist relationships are shaped by associated disperser traits, demonstrating co-evolutionary mechanisms driving adaptive differentiation of fruit morphological and macronutrient traits. By integrating the disperser syndrome hypothesis and signal theory with nutritional geometry theory and trait-matching theory, our study expounds the role of seed disperser selective preferences in the evolution of fruit traits, thus advancing the seed disperser mutualism paradigm.

works.title: Thermal acclimation as an emergent property of economically optimal photosynthesis
works.abstract: Summary Leaf‐level photosynthesis acclimates to growth conditions over days to weeks, with the instantaneous optimal temperature for photosynthesis ( T opt ) increasing with growth temperature ( T growth ). We investigated how this behaviour emerges in the P model, a primary production model based on eco‐evolutionary optimality hypotheses. We evaluated the P model estimates against experimental data for three herbaceous species grown at different temperatures and examined mechanisms underlying the responses of T opt and the photosynthetic rate at T opt ( A opt ). The model yields a realistic increase in T opt with T growth and a peaked relationship between A opt and T growth . These responses emerge largely from adjustment of the stomatal sensitivity parameter ξ, which determines the internal‐to‐ambient CO 2 ratio ( c i : c a ) and its sensitivity to vapour pressure deficit. Rubisco kinetics ( K ) does not acclimate in the model, but its temperature dependence enters acclimation through optimality, mainly via ξ, shifting T opt . The decline in A opt at high growth temperatures, often attributed to heat stress, reflects the narrowing gap between T opt and T growth because the T opt shift has a slope below one. The P model provides a mechanistic explanation for observed trends in T opt and A opt and a scalable approach for representing biochemical and stomatal acclimation in land‐surface models.

works.title: Rethinking RNAi efficiency: the role of fungal lifestyle in HIGS and SIGS success
Rice bZIP11 acts as a transcriptional repressor that negatively regulates photosynthesis in response to nitrogen deficiency
works.abstract: Nitrogen (N)-deficiency responses, which are closely linked to plant biomass and crop yield, differ between plant tissues. A previous in silico analysis suggested that four transcription factors, including OsbZIP11, play vital roles in the gene regulatory network governing N-deficiency responses (NDRs) in rice roots. To investigate the role of OsbZIP11 in NDRs, the phenotypes, functional responses, and gene expression of rice plants that either lacked functional OsbZIP11 or overexpressed OsbZIP11 were analyzed. Contrary to expectations, OsbZIP11 function showed an overwhelmingly stronger association with photosynthetic gene expression than with any other physiological process, including the expression control of N-related genes. OsbZIP11 directly suppressed numerous photosynthetic genes as a transcriptional repressor. N deficiency increased OsbZIP11 expression in shoots, consistent with N deficiency-reduced photosynthetic activity. Furthermore, removing functional OsbZIP11 and OsbZIP11 overexpression produced opposite effects on the expression of genes involved in the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis and carbon dioxide fixation, as well as on growth and grain yield. These findings indicate that OsbZIP11 is a critical factor responsible for N deficiency-induced decreases in photosynthesis in rice and provide new insights into the mechanism underlying the coordination of C and N acquisition.

works.title: Aligning auxin supply to developmental demand in adventitious rooting
works.abstract: Adventitious root (AR) formation is the developmental process that makes vegetative propagation possible, underpinning forestry, horticulture, and the clonal multiplication of elite and hard-to-propagate genotypes. Despite a detailed understanding of auxin's stage-specific roles across the rooting program, propagation practice still treats auxin supply as a quantity to set rather than a profile to match. We argue that this produces a temporal mismatch between auxin supply and developmental demand: the available evidence shows that exogenous auxin availability frequently declines before the stages it should support are complete, particularly in slow-to-root and recalcitrant species, where developmental timelines are longest. New delivery tools, such as slow-release conjugates, encapsulation systems, and selective auxin agonists, now make time-structured delivery profiles feasible, but realizing their potential requires a different starting point. Rather than optimizing auxin dose empirically against rooting outcome, the field should characterize the spatiotemporal auxin demand curve across AR stages and design delivery profiles to match it. We outline the conceptual framework for this shift and the experimental approaches now available to support it.

works.title: Aridity reshapes leaf and root trait dispersion through distinct microbial pathways
works.abstract: Summary Aridity is a primary driver of plant community assembly, yet most trait‐based studies focus on mean traits rather than trait dispersion. Soil microbes may mediate plant responses to aridity, but whether leaf and root trait dispersion responds to aridity through shared or distinct microbial pathways remains unclear. Using 535 species‐by‐plot records (247 species) along an aridity gradient in north‐west China, we quantified four leaf and four root traits, soil properties, microbial diversity and composition, and microbial carbon use efficiency. We tested whether aridity differentially regulates leaf vs root functional dispersion (FD is ), and whether these responses are associated with different microbial predictors. Leaf traits shifted more consistently with aridity and were more tightly linked to environmental variation than root traits. Leaf FD is negatively correlated with CUE, whereas root FD is negatively correlated with fungal diversity and bacterial community composition. These associations weakened toward less arid sites. Structural equation modeling further showed that leaf FD is linked primarily to microbial functioning, whereas root FD is linked more strongly to microbial diversity and composition. Our results reveal that aridity reshapes trait dispersion through organ‐specific plant–microbe pathways, highlighting that predicting dryland community responses to increasing drought must treat above‐ and belowground traits separately.

works.title: mRNA Decay Mediates Evolution and Biological Functions in Plant Gene Expression
works.abstract: mRNA decay is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism that fine-tunes plant development and stress adaptation through dynamic mRNA stability control, bridging fundamental biology and crop improvement. Current knowledge of mRNA decay mechanisms in plants, largely derived from Arabidopsis, is poorly generalisable across plant lineages owing to insufficient exploration of other species. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing have accelerated the discovery of mRNA decay mechanisms. Here, we systematically illustrate its core molecular mechanisms alongside breakthrough advances. We further dissect evolutionary characteristics of highly conserved core components and lineage-specific adaptive variations across eukaryotes. Notably, conserved since the last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA), this machinery reflects a complex ancestral eukaryote and provides high-resolution phylogenetic markers for reconstructing eukaryotic origins. We also clarify the essential biological roles of mRNA decay in developmental modulation and stress responses. Finally, we propose precision breeding strategies based on mRNA stability regulation to develop high-yielding, climate-resilient crops. This review integrates up-to-date mechanistic evidence and comparative evolutionary perspectives, consolidates consensus findings and sorts out inconsistent research outcomes, and seeks to enrich the fundamental biological understanding of plant mRNA stability modulation.

works.title: Chromosomal rearrangements and sequence similarity drive preferential allosyndetic introgression from a wild relative into wheat
A haplotype-resolved lychee pangenome uncovers structural and haplotype variations associated with flowering time divergence and fruit sugar composition

A systemic auxin state integrates light and temperature to gate lateral rooting in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: How plants coordinate local organ formation with systemic information about environmental conditions remains largely unclear. Here we show that availability of the phytohormone auxin across the Arabidopsis root provides a shared hormonal state that integrates environmental cues and gates whether locally specified branching sites develop. Long-term luminescence imaging, time-resolved transcriptomics and metabolite profiling reveal approximately 24-hour rhythms in auxin abundance and signalling at 21°C, with shoot-perceived light setting the amplitude of the systemic signalling. At 29°C, this organisation is reprogrammed into a root-wide decline followed by a light-dependent systemic recovery of auxin signalling. Recovery under sufficient light supports root branching-site progression without requiring restored circadian rhythmicity. In contrast, weaker recovery under reduced light leads to arrest of early primordia. Genetic analyses implicate phytochrome B as well as cryptochromes photoreceptors and the morning loop of the circadian clock in this conditional response. The auxin oxidase DIOXYGENASE FOR AUXIN OXIDATION 1 (DAO1) reprograms systemic auxin dynamics at elevated temperature. Reducing auxin oxidation sustains signalling in branching sites and lateral root development during warming, whereas increased oxidation weakens recovery and enhances developmental inhibition. Our findings reveal how systemic metabolic control allows plants to interpret global environmental information in context and therewith align local de novo organ formation.

works.title: Metabolic shuttles between mitochondria and plastids: Roles of key transporters in coordinating carbon-nitrogen metabolism
works.abstract: Carbon and nitrogen metabolism in plant cells is distributed across multiple organelles, requiring extensive metabolite exchange to coordinate growth, development and environmental responses. Mitochondria and plastids function as interconnected metabolic hubs linked through the transport of carbon skeletons, amino acids, organic acids, and redox equivalents across organellar membranes. These transport processes are essential for integrating energy conversion processes, nitrogen assimilation, and biosynthetic metabolism. In this review, we integrate current knowledge of mitochondrial and plastid envelope transporters that mediate carbon-nitrogen exchange between organelles, focusing on recent characterisation of transporters with confirmed substrates. We discuss how these transporters contribute to the coordination of cellular metabolism, highlight emerging concepts regarding their regulation and integration, and identify major knowledge gaps in our understanding of interorganellar metabolic communication. Understanding how these transport systems collectively shape carbon-nitrogen fluxes is essential for deciphering metabolic flexibility and guiding metabolic engineering strategies in plants.

works.title: Receptor-like kinases mediate extracellular ABA perception
HiEGP: An environment-informed genomic prediction framework that facilitates soybean genebank germplasm evaluation and climate-smart breeding
works.abstract: The biodiversity preserved in gene banks drives crop improvement and strengthens climate resilience for feeding the future. However, only a limited fraction of germplasm has been well characterized, because phenotyping remains low-throughput and costly, especially for region-specific yield-related traits. This gap hinders the utilization of gene bank biodiversity in breeding, particularly for photoperiod and temperature-sensitive crops like soybean. Here, we constructed a multi-environment soybean dataset integrating phenotypes, genotypes, and environmental covariates for 1,421 diverse soybean germplasm accessions. It includes six key breeding traits collected across nine locations (latitudes 28.53°-45.64°), along with bioclimatic and soil data. We developed HiEGP (High-dimensional Environmental Factor Integration for Genomic Prediction), a feature-engineered hierarchical G×E prediction framework that integrates environmental main effects, genotype-specific environmental responses, genomic background, and environmental similarity. HiEGP achieved high predictive performance under both validation settings, reaching average trait-wise pooled correlations of 0.871 for predicting untested genotypes in observed environments and 0.775 for predicting untested genotypes in unobserved environments, outperforming the evaluated methods overall. In the external USDA soybean panel, HiEGP showed stable prediction for 100-seed weight, with environment-wise correlations ranging from 0.70 to 0.81. HiEGP enabled environment-response genome-wide association studies, recovering known maturity loci and identifying 175 candidate regions associated with environmental-response patterns. Phenotypic evidence from ethyl methanesulfonate mutants supported the prioritization of selected candidate genes. HiEGP supported regional adaptation assessment under the observed environmental conditions. This capability offers a scalable strategy to improve the characterization and breeding use of underexplored gene bank germplasm for environment-informed soybean breeding.

Plant sexual reproduction in a warming world
works.abstract: Sexual reproduction is the most heat-sensitive phase of the plant life cycle; however, studies of reproductive failure under heat stress have primarily focused on individual organs. Here, we propose a conceptual framework in which heat stress causes a system-level breakdown of male and female gametophyte development, shared metabolic and proteostatic support networks, and pollen-pistil interaction. This combined collapse within a narrow temperature window cannot be predicted from individual organs or gametophytes. Heat also remodels epigenetic makeup, generating stress memory, though its transmission across generations remains unresolved. We highlight that techniques such as single-cell omics, AI-driven phenotyping, and genome editing can provide valuable mechanistic insights to support the development of predictive, actionable breeding strategies for heat-resilient crops.

Zinc and Iron Homeostatic Interactions in a Mutant Lacking Nicotianamine Vacuolar Storage and Citrate Xylem Loading
works.abstract: Metal homeostasis in plants relies on coordinated uptake, chelation and transport mechanisms involving, but not limited to, citrate and nicotianamine (NA). In Arabidopsis (Arabidopsis thaliana), disruption of the citrate exporter FRD3 (FERRIC REDUCTASE DEFECTIVE 3) causes constitutive iron (Fe) deficiency responses, altered Fe, manganese (Mn) and zinc (Zn) distribution, with Fe accumulation in the root cell wall. This ultimately results in oxidative and biotic stress responses, and impaired root development, phenotypes that are partially alleviated by Zn excess. In this study, we investigated the consequences of impairing both citrate loading into xylem vessels and NA partitioning within cells. The frd3 zif1 double mutant exhibits enhanced sensitivity to Zn excess, severe defects in root system architecture and meristem maintenance, persistent oxidative stress and compromised reproductive development. These phenotypes correlate with sustained activation of Fe deficiency signalling and marked defects in root-to-shoot metal translocation. Our findings reveal that coordinated citrate export and NA compartmentation form an integrated buffering strategy required to maintain metal homeostasis and partitioning, as well as redox balance and proper development, including root plasticity and seed yield, under fluctuating metal availability.

works.title: RpFT5 Regulates Root‐Sprouting Rejuvenation in Robinia pseudoacacia Through Transcriptional Control by RpSPL9/RpSOC1 and Epigenetic Regulation via AGO4‐Mediated DNA Methylation
works.abstract: Root-based vegetative propagation enables mature trees to regain juvenile characteristics, a process commonly referred to as rejuvenation, yet the underlying transcriptional and epigenetic regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, Robinia pseudoacacia was employed as a model system owing to its strong natural sprouting capacity to dissect the molecular basis of root-derived rejuvenation. Transcriptomic profiling identified RpFT5 as a central hub gene associated with the transition between mature and juvenile states during root sprouting. Functional analyses demonstrated that RpFT5 was positively regulated by the transcription factors RpSPL9 and RpSOC1, which directly bound to distinct cis-elements in its promoter and activated its transcription. In addition, epigenetic analyses revealed that CHH DNA methylation in the RpFT5 promoter was dynamically associated with developmental phase changes and was significantly enriched in mature tissues. This methylation could be regulated through the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway involving an RpAGO4-like protein. RpAGO4-like contributed to CHH methylation of the RpFT5 promoter and physically interacted with RpSPL9 and RpSOC1, attenuating their transcriptional activation of RpFT5. This coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic regulatory network could result in fine-tuned repression or activation of RpFT5 during rejuvenation, thereby modulating juvenile trait re-establishment during root sprouting. Collectively, these findings define a dual-layer regulatory mechanism integrating transcription factor activity and DNA methylation in controlling root-based vegetative rejuvenation, and propose a model in which RdDM-associated CHH methylation functions as a dynamic regulatory module governing developmental phase transitions in perennial trees.

works.title: A CHH Methylation–Ubiquitination Cascade Links Light‐Induced Anthocyanin Accumulation in Pear Fruit
works.abstract: Light is a key environmental cue for anthocyanin biosynthesis in fruit, but the DNA methylation targets and downstream mechanisms remain largely unclear. Using the red-skinned pear cultivar 'Aohong No. 1', we performed whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) and RNA-seq on peels before and after light exposure following bag removal. Light-induced genome-wide CHH hypermethylation, with differentially methylated regions (DMRs) enriched in promoters. Integrative analysis identified the RING-type E3 ligase RGLG5 as a negative regulator of pigmentation. A 420-bp promoter fragment of RGLG5 underwent light-induced CHH hypermethylation, concomitant with RGLG5 transcriptional downregulation. This methylation blocked the binding of the AP2 transcription factor to the fragment, thereby silencing RGLG5. RGLG5 mediated ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation of the transcription factor WRKY75L. Silencing of RGLG5 allowed WRKY75L to accumulate and directly activate MYB10, promoting pigmentation. Co-expression assays further confirmed that RGLG5 antagonized WRKY75L-driven anthocyanin accumulation in pear peel and callus tissues. Collectively, these findings support a model in which light-triggered CHH methylation of the RGLG5 promoter links epigenetic silencing to protein stability during fruit pigmentation, and identify the RGLG5 promoter as a potential epigenetic target for breeding.

works.title: PpPKp1 Coordinates Growth and Cold Tolerance by Integrating Energy‐Cytokinin Signalling via Pyruvate Metabolism in Poa pratensis
works.abstract: Plastidial pyruvate kinase (PKp; EC 2.7.1.40), as a core enzyme regulating plant carbon metabolism, has been confirmed to be a key component in plant stress response. However, the specific regulatory network in cold response and the molecular mechanism mediating cold tolerance remain elusive. This study reveals that the expression of PpPKp1, a chloroplast-localized plastid pyruvate kinase gene from Poa pratensis var. anceps cv. Qinghai, is significantly induced by low temperature and drought stress. Overexpression of PpPKp1 in Arabidopsis thaliana and Poa pratensis enhanced pyruvate kinase activity and pyruvate content, thereby improving tillering capacity and biomass accumulation under cold conditions, while also promoting root elongation, shoot growth, and maintaining the relative stability of ROS. Conversely, RNAi-mediated suppression of PpPKp1 in P. pratensis elicited contrasting phenotypes and physiological responses. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that under cold stress, PpPKp1 facilitates energy supply by enhancing glycolytic/TCA cycle flux and simultaneously coordinates arginine biosynthesis with cytokinin signalling transduction. This integrated mechanism of 'energy provision-metabolite synthesis-signal regulation' is closely associated with the maintenance of plant growth and development under cold conditions, balancing resource allocation between stress resistance and growth. Ultimately, it leads to significantly enhanced cold tolerance. Our work unveils for the first time the molecular mechanism by which PpPKp1 regulates plant cold responses through coupling central carbon metabolism and hormone signalling. It provides novel insights into the synergistic network of 'plastid metabolism-systemic stress resistance' in plants, and offers candidate genes and a theoretical basis for the genetic improvement of cold tolerance in crops.

works.title: The pan-NLRome of section Lycopersicon and allied wild Solanum taxa reveals taxonomic-scope dependence of shared receptors and shell-enriched copy and sequence diversity
Integrated GWAS and RNA-Seq analyses identify candidate genes for drought tolerance in spring wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) from the cold and arid region of China
Long hypocotyls facilitate deeper sowing to improve canola establishment in a warming climate
works.abstract: KEY MESSAGE: Deeper sowing of canola into cooler, moist soil could improve crop establishment in stressful conditions. We demonstrate cultivars with long hypocotyls emerge better from deeper sowing than short hypocotyl cultivars. Poor seedling establishment is a major constraint to canola (Brassica napus L.) productivity globally. Optimum seeding depths are commonly 1-2 cm under favourable soil moisture and temperature conditions., However, drying autumn conditions with climate change coupled with increasing farm size often results in canola sown earlier when the soil surface is hot and dry. Deeper sowing (> 3-4 cm) into stored water and more stable temperature allows for timely establishment of early sown crops. Under favourable moisture and temperature conditions, current cultivars establish well at shallow sowing depths but emerge poorly when sown deeper. This study investigated the potential to breed canola cultivars with longer hypocotyls to improve emergence from deep sowing as a strategy to adapt to earlier sowing under climate change - a concept demonstrated successfully with longer coleoptile wheat. A diverse panel of 255 open-pollinated accessions was phenotyped using high-throughput laboratory assays for hypocotyl length and cross-sectional area. Genome-wide association analysis revealed hypocotyl length was under polygenic control, and several significant marker-trait associations were identified. Emergence was validated in multiple field environments with both conventional (2 cm) and deeper (5 cm) sowing. Increased hypocotyl length was strongly associated with improved emergence from deep sowing, supporting its value as a breeding target to improve canola establishment under increasingly variable and challenging growing conditions.

works.title: Modern breeding of root, tuber, and bulb crops to enhance food and nutritional security
works.abstract: KEY MESSAGE: Unlocking the molecular mechanisms and pathways of underground storage organ development and nutrient and non-nutrient traits may provide more avenues to tailor elite germplasm enriched with these characteristics in root, tuber, and bulb crops. Biofortified cassava, potato, and sweet potato provide food and nutritional security to millions of people in Africa, Asia, and Latin American regions. Root and tuber crops provide food and nutritional security to millions of people in Africa, Asia, and Latin America and the Caribbean, while garlic and onions, in addition to strong therapeutic potential, are widely used in food preparation to add flavour and taste. Root, tuber, and bulb (RTB) crops are a good source of carbohydrates, minerals, and bioactive compounds. However, these crops also possess a variety of allergens and toxic compounds, limiting their consumption. Here, we synthesized i) the contribution of RTB crops on food and nutrition security in the Global South, ii) the various types of allergens and toxic compounds detected in these crops, iii) catalogue germplasm resources across national and international genebanks, iv) document the range of genetic variation in edible organs morphology, nutrient and non-nutrient traits, v) discuss advances in high-throughput phenomics to monitor variability, vi) assess population structure and diversity in germplasm pool, vii) list genomic regions (QTL) and genes (both functionally characterized and candidate genes and QTL) associated with storage organs (roots or tubers) morphology, nutrient and non-nutrient traits, viii) uptake, transport, and storage of minerals in edible vegetable organs and their effects on consumers, and ix) advances in genetic improvement of nutritionally enhanced (nutrient and non-nutrient traits) and productive germplasm through crossbreeding and biotechnological interventions. Assessing and exploiting functional diversity, combined with the use of functionally characterized genes and associated markers for storage root growth/thickening, and nutrient and non-nutrient traits, can be deployed in breeding programs to improve these characteristics in RTB crops. Numerous candidate genes and genomic regions (or quantitative trait loci) reported herein must be functionally validated before being deployed in crop breeding programs. A greater emphasis should be placed on genetically and phenotypically characterizing RTB germplasm, and on combining empirical breeding with molecular tools to enhance precision, efficiency, and rapid genetic gain. Millions of rural households in parts of Africa, Asia, and Latin America are currently benefiting from the commercialization of provitamin A-enriched cassava, potato, and sweet potato. The development of orange-fleshed sweet potato cultivars with higher levels of provitamin A was awarded the ''World Food Prize'' in 2016. There are more opportunities to enhance nutrition status and food security through improvement of root, tuber, and bulb crops.

works.abstract: Natural genomic variation across species and cultivars underlies the diversity of flavors in plant fruit, seeds, leaves, and roots. Hu et al. (pages 3895–3913) discuss how diverse forms of genomic variation reshape the biosynthesis, transport, and accumulation of flavor‐related metabolites, thereby driving diversification in sweetness, acidity, bitterness, piquancy, astringency, and aroma. Integrating evidence from genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics establishes a mechanistic framework linking genomic variation to the molecular and metabolic basis of flavor traits. Artificial intelligence‐assisted breeding and precision gene editing can further accelerate the identification of causal variants and enable the targeted improvement of flavor traits.

works.title: The transcription factor SiROCX coordinates a stage-specific xylan- and cellulose-degrading secretome during immune-compatible colonization of monocot roots by Serendipita indica
works.abstract: Intracellular accommodation of beneficial fungi requires controlled remodelling of host cell walls while avoiding excessive activation of plant immune responses. During colonization of monocot roots, the endophytic fungus Serendipita indica induces a suite of carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) targeting xylan and cellulose, but how this program is transcriptionally controlled in basidiomycetes is unknown. Here, we combined co-expression network analysis of time-resolved colonization transcriptomes with DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq) of module-associated transcription factors. This identified Si ROCX, a Zn 2 Cys 6 transcription factor of an Agaricomycetes-specific Roc1/ROCX lineage, whose DAP-seq-defined regulon is enriched in CAZyme genes. Inducible overexpression of Si ROCX activated representative targets, enriched the secretome in CAZymes and enhanced xylanase and cellulase activities on xylan and delignified alcohol-insoluble residue (dAIR) of barley roots under in vitro conditions. Premature activation of this program during barley colonization was associated with early induction of a host immune marker despite comparable fungal biomass, consistent with a role for temporal control in maintaining symbiotic compatibility. Together, these findings identify Si ROCX as a major regulator of a host-adapted cell wall–degrading secretome and reveal an Agaricomycetes-specific regulatory module that coordinates host cell wall remodelling with immune-compatible symbiotic colonization.

works.title: Embodied intelligence for crop production
works.abstract: Global agriculture faces growing food demand, labor shortages, and climate uncertainty. Although automation has improved agricultural operations, adapting to variable crop states and unstructured environments remains challenging. Embodied intelligence integrates multimodal perception, contextual reasoning, and adaptive action through continuous interaction with crops and their environment. This review examines advances in embodied perception, decision-making, and execution for crop production. We discuss how multimodal sensing, crop growth models, and adaptive control connect individual operations with management objectives across the crop growth cycle. We further identify priorities for system integration, long-term validation, and practical deployment to support precise, sustainable, and resilient food production.

works.title: Lectin-centered signaling networks orchestrate plant immunity, stress adaptation, and development
works.abstract: Plant lectins are structurally diverse non-catalytic carbohydrate-binding proteins, some of which contribute directly to defense against herbivores and pathogens. However, emerging evidence suggests that lectins function far beyond passive defense factors and instead constitute a multilayered signaling system coordinating environmental perception, immunity, stress adaptation and development throughout the plant life cycle. Recent studies reveal that lectins perceive diverse endogenous and exogenous cues, including glycoconjugates, peptides and damage-associated molecules, and integrate these signals into conserved downstream signaling networks. In parallel, intracellular lectins contribute to pathogen restriction, physiological homeostasis and developmental regulation through direct modulation of cellular signaling pathways. Together, these findings position lectins as central components of a broader plant glyco-signaling framework linking extracellular information with adaptive physiological outputs. In this Review, we synthesize recent advances in lectin-mediated signaling across plant immunity, abiotic stress adaptation and developmental regulation, discuss how post-translational modifications expand lectin signaling plasticity, and highlight emerging translational opportunities in sustainable agriculture, including immune engineering, programmable receptor design and targeted biomolecule delivery. Finally, we propose that lectin-mediated signaling represents an underappreciated regulatory layer underlying plant environmental adaptation and outline key challenges for harnessing lectins in next-generation crop improvement.

works.title: The nuclear lamina protein KAKU4 coordinates jasmonate signaling through nuclear condensates and a MYC2-mediated feedback loop
works.abstract: Jasmonate (JA) signaling must be precisely controlled to prevent excessive activation, yet the nuclear mechanisms underlying signal attenuation and homeostasis remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the nuclear lamina protein KAKU4 as a negative regulator of JA signaling that modulates pathway activity via phase separation-associated nuclear condensates. Loss of KAKU4 confers hypersensitivity to JA, resulting in enhanced root growth inhibition and increased resistance to pathogen challenge. KAKU4 physically associates with MYC2 and JAZ3, and undergoes phase separation to generate dynamic nuclear-peripheral condensates that facilitate the organization of JAZ3-containing condensates and contribute to JAZ3 stabilization. This condensate-associated organization restricts MYC2 DNA binding activity and transcriptional output while promoting JAZ3 protein stability. Notably, JA signaling rapidly remodels KAKU4-associated condensate organization, accompanied by reduced KAKU4-JAZ3-associated puncta, linking condensate dynamics with pathway activation. In addition, JA promotes proteasome-dependent turnover of KAKU4, whereas MYC2-dependent transcriptional activation of KAKU4 forms a delayed feedback circuit that contributes to restoration of JA signaling homeostasis. Our findings reveal a phase-separation-associated nuclear lamina regulatory module that dynamically restrains JA signaling and contributes to balanced hormone responses.

works.title: An Integrated Framework to Develop and Deliver Salt-Tolerant Rice Varieties for Coastal Ecologies
works.abstract: Cultivated rice ( Oryza sativa ) is intrinsically salt-sensitive, with yield declining sharply once soil electrical conductivity (EC) exceeds ∼4 dS m -1 . Although mechanistic understanding of salinity tolerance has advanced considerably, its translation into farmer-adopted varieties remains limited. Genetic gains in rice salinity breeding programs remain critically low, at 0.10–0.33% per year, far below the ≥1.5–2% annual rates required for meaningful varietal impact. Three constraints recur: a narrow donor base, an over-reliance on single-gene approaches to a polygenic trait, and phenotypic screening in controlled environments that correlates only modestly with field performance. Here we outline an integrated breeding strategy that combines realistic field-based phenotyping in saline hotspots, the Connected Breeding framework for systematic polygenic introgression, and the Transition from Trait to Environment (TTE) approach—using the target saline environment itself as the selection background to implement genomic selection alongside modern breeding tools as a pragmatic framework for developing the next generation of salinity-tolerant varieties. Using a stochastic breeding simulation in which grain yield is modelled as an additive polygenic trait—without salinity-specific tolerance, genotype-by-salinity interaction, or stage-specific effects—we show that CB sustains a higher late-horizon rate of genetic gain than closed-pool genomic selection while retaining 2.2 times more of the allelic diversity on which further gain depends. In the baseline comparison, which grants CB greater genotyping and phenotyping resources and immediate bridge-line availability, CB also finished the 60-year horizon +1.26 t ha -1 ahead (P < 0.0001); this cumulative-yield advantage was not retained once resource and time costs were equalised, whereas the rate and diversity effects persisted under every constraint tested. The simulation therefore addresses the population-genetic logic of CB rather than salinity tolerance itself, and it does not evaluate the TTE design, whose value must be established empirically. We then situate this framework within a Technology–Investment–Partnership–Scaling (TIPs) roadmap to translate improved genotypes into farmer-ready rice products. The approach is, in principle, transferable to other abiotic stresses and crops.

works.title: Arabidopsis HMGA protein HON5 antagonizes ABF transcription factors to negatively regulate ABA signaling and stress tolerance
works.abstract: Plants inevitably face abiotic stresses such as drought and salinity. While the abscisic acid (ABA) signaling pathway has been extensively characterized, the involvement of chromatin structural factors in hormone responses remains poorly understood. This study investigates the roles of Arabidopsis Globular Domain of Linker Histone-High Mobility Group A (GH1-HMGA) proteins, specifically GH1-HMGA1 (HON4) and GH1-HMGA2 (HON5), in modulating ABA signaling and abiotic stress tolerance. Genetic analysis reveals that the loss-of-function hon45 double mutant exhibits hypersensitivity to ABA, salt, and osmotic stress, suggesting that HON4/5 function as negative regulators of the ABA and stress response signaling genes like RAB18 and RD29B. Mechanistically, HON4 and HON5 physically interact with the ABA-responsive element (ABRE)-binding factors (ABFs). Functional assays indicate that HON4 and HON5 impair the ability of ABFs to activate downstream stress-responsive genes. Genetic experiments demonstrate that HON4 and HON5 attenuate the ABF response to ABA and drought stress. Importantly, we identify a negative regulatory feedback loop in which the transcription factor ABF4 directly binds to the HON5 promoter and represses its transcription. Collectively, these findings establish HON4 and HON5 as novel nuclear co-repressors that attenuate ABA-mediated stress signaling by inhibiting the transcriptional activity of ABFs, revealing a previously unrecognized chromatin-associated layer of regulation in plant stress responses.

works.title: The pri-miR160-encoded small peptide miPEP160 regulates rice immunity and growth independent of miR160
Lineage-specific Emergence and Multi-layered Regulation of Limonoid Biosynthesis in Citrus
works.abstract: Limonoids are triterpenoid phytochemicals that contribute to delayed bitterness in citrus fruit, enhance pest resistance, and exhibit a wide range of bioactivities with nutraceutical and agrochemical potential. Despite their importance, the genetic and regulatory basis underlying limonoid biosynthesis in citrus remains poorly understood. Here, by integrating targeted metabolite profiling across 134 citrus and related accessions with comparative genomic analyses of 12 representative species from the orange subfamily (Aurantioideae), we show that the emergence of limonin, nomilin, and obacunone correlates with the citrus-specific acquisition of three downstream biosynthetic genes, CYP88A51, CYP716AC1, and limonoid furan synthase (LFS), while the upstream oxidosqualene cyclase 1 (OSC1) remains conserved across lineages. We further identify CsbHLH92 as a key transcriptional activator that directly regulates these genes, and its overexpression led to dramatic increases in limonin and nomilin levels. Moreover, CsbHLH92 activity is attenuated by CsMPK7-mediated phosphorylation, contributing to the downregulation of limonoid biosynthesis during leaf senescence, when senescing leaves are generally less preferred by insect pests. Together, our findings uncover how lineage-specific gene emergence and multi-layered regulation collectively shape the specialized metabolism of limonoids in citrus. These insights provide metabolic engineering targets for improving citrus flavor, enhancing pest resistance, and boosting the production of high-value bioactive compounds.

works.title: Catabolism of jasmonoyl-isoleucine modulates maize development and defense responses
works.abstract: Proper spatial and temporal accumulation of the phytohormone jasmonoyl-isoleucine (JA-Ile) requires precise control of both its biosynthesis and catabolism. Two pathways for JA-Ile catabolism are the conversion of JA-Ile to 12-hydroxy-JA-Ile (12OH-JA-Ile) by JA-Ile hydroxylases, and the reversible deconjugation of isoleucine from JA-Ile by amidohydrolases, followed by conversion of jasmonic acid to 11-hydroxy-jasmonic acid by jasmonate-induced oxygenases. JA-Ile hydroxylase activity is performed by enzymes of the cytochrome P450 94B (CYP94B) family. In this study, we generated single and double loss-of-function mutants of the two CYP94Bs of Zea mays (maize), the JA-Ile hydroxylase ZmCYP94B1 and its paralog ZmCYP94B12 and used these mutants in combination with in vitro and in vivo assays, to explore roles of these genes in JA-Ile catabolism, development, and defense in maize. In vitro assays showed both ZmCYP94B1 and ZmCYP94B12 have JA-Ile hydroxylase activity, and ZmCYP94B1 may also produce 12-carboxy-JA-Ile. Loss of function of both genes in maize leads accumulation of JA-Ile in unstressed leaves, and to enhanced resistance to the insect pest Spodoptera frugiperda and fungal pathogens Cochliobolus heterostrophus and Fusarium verticillioides. This study shows that the JA-Ile hydroxylase pathway plays an important role in JA-Ile catabolism and plant defense in maize. The zmcyp94b mutants also reveal that the genes have roles in regulating plant height and tassel architecture indicating that the ZmCYP94Bs contribute to balancing JA-Ile mediated growth-defense trade-offs.

works.title: Opposing modulation of QUAC1/ALMT12 by S-type channel inhibition and R-type channel activation during elevated-CO2 and ABA-induced stomatal movement
works.abstract: Atmospheric CO2 concentrations, now 50% higher than pre-industrial levels, induce plant stomatal closure. The slow (S)-type anion channels in guard cells are activated by elevated CO2/bicarbonate and promote that process. However, the response of the rapid (R)-type anion channels to CO2/bicarbonate remains unclear. Here, we show that bicarbonate fails to activate the R-type anion channel QUAC1 (ALMT12) in either Xenopus oocytes or guard cell protoplasts, which indicates that the two channel types are differentially in response to CO2/bicarbonate. Furthermore, we demonstrate that QUAC1/ALMT12 negatively regulates CO2/bicarbonate-induced stomatal closure, achieved through its inhibition of SLAC1. As such, ALMT12 has opposite functional consequences in ABA vs CO2 pathways due to differential upstream activation.

works.title: The LbBLH9-LbGeBP module regulates salt gland development and salt tolerance in Limonium bicolor
works.abstract: GLABROUS1 enhancer-binding protein (GeBP) transcription factors play pivotal roles in the regulating plant development and stress responses. However, the function of GeBP family members in regulating salt gland development and salt tolerance in Limonium bicolor remains unclear. In this study, the gene LbGeBP1 exhibited high expression levels during the early stages of salt gland development. We found that LbGeBP1 is mainly expressed in salt glands and LbGeBP1 localizes in the nucleus. Functional analysis through overexpression and knockout of LbGeBP1 in L. bicolor showed that LbGeBP1 negatively regulates salt gland development and salt tolerance. Further investigation revealed that the BEL1-like homeobox (BLH) LbBLH9 binds to the LbGeBP1 promoter and represses its expression. LbBLH9 was specifically expressed in salt glands. In contrast to LbGeBP1, LbBLH9 was found to positively regulate salt gland development and salt tolerance. Consistent with this regulatory relationship, silencing LbBLH9 in the LbGeBP1-overexpression background further increased LbGeBP1 expression and exacerbated defects in salt gland development and salt secretion. In contrast, simultaneous silencing of LbBLH9 and LbGeBP1 partially rescued the defects caused by silencing LbBLH9 alone. Together, these molecular and genetic data support a model in which LbBLH9 promotes salt gland development and salt tolerance by repressing the transcription of LbGeBP1. Furthermore, the LbBLH9-LbGeBP1 module regulates the expression of genes involved in salt gland development and salt stress responses. This study reveals a novel molecular mechanism governing salt gland development and salt tolerance in L. bicolor, providing a theoretical foundation for elucidating salt tolerance mechanisms in plants.

works.title: Guard cell size and initial conductance influence stomatal closure kinetics
works.abstract: Summary In fluctuating environments, the kinetics of stomatal opening and closing influence the balance between carbon gain and water loss. Smaller guard cells may respond faster to fluctuating environmental conditions because of their greater surface area for osmolyte flux relative to cell volume. A related hypothesis is that operational stomatal conductance () is often well below its theoretical maximum () because at this stomatal aperture, guard cell volume is poised to change rapidly with small changes in turgor pressure. We analyzed 2125 estimates of stomatal closure kinetics in response to an abrupt increase in vapor pressure deficit (VPD) among 29 diverse wild tomato populations in the genus Solanum . Leaves with small guard cells and a lower initial stomatal conductance () closed faster, but each explained variation in kinetic parameters at different levels of biological organization. Guard cell size had high phylogenetic heritability and varied relatively little within populations, whereas varied mostly among individuals and between light‐intensity treatments. Smaller stomata can be speedier, but the current physiological state of the leaf also affects the responsiveness of stomatal conductance to fluctuations. Selection on stomatal speed may influence not only anatomical traits like guard cell size but also physiological controls on .

works.title: Rhg1 -mediated selective autophagy degrades the nematode effector HgGID to increase soybean cyst nematode resistance
works.abstract: Plant-parasitic nematodes are sophisticated metazoan pathogens that deploy complex, animal-like effector repertoires to manipulate host cellular machinery. The Rhg1 locus drives the primary resistance against soybean cyst nematode (Heterodera glycines), yet the mechanism by which its encoded atypical Soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor Attachment Protein 18 (SNAP18) proteins restrict this evolutionarily advanced pathogen remains a long-standing enigma. Here, we reveal that Rhg1-mediated resistance operates as a suicide-bait strategy that converts a nematode virulence factor into a selective-autophagic trap. TurboID proximity labeling identified HgGID (glucose-induced degradation), a secreted nematode effector that physically associates with SNAP18 and co-enriches ubiquitin-proteasome components and SNARE-associated factors, consistent with a virulence strategy that engages host trafficking machinery during syncytium formation. Notably, the Rhg1-encoded atypical SNAP18 variant subverts this virulence strategy. We show that HgGID binds all 3 SNAP18 variants, whereas the resistance-associated SNAP18LC/HC variants favor increased dynamic accessibility of the HgGID AIM and promote its ATG8-dependent selective degradation. Ultimately, this targeted autophagic clearance efficiently neutralizes the virulence function of HgGID, establishing a novel paradigm for plant immunity against metazoan pathogens. Our findings uncover a molecular arms race where the host repurposes its vesicle transport machinery into an immune trap, highlighting the central role of selective autophagy in determining the outcome of host-metazoan interactions.

works.title: Tissue-specific accumulation of Na+ in leaves of 2 tomato species is linked to differences in symplastic transport
works.abstract: Abstract Soil salinization is a growing global threat that limits crop productivity. To cope with sodium (Na+) stress, plants have evolved tolerance mechanisms, including excluding Na+ from shoot tissues and tolerating elevated Na+ within shoots through tissue- and cellular-level mechanisms. Most current knowledge of Na+ accumulation comes from organ- or whole-plant measurements that lack the spatial resolution needed to resolve cellular tolerance mechanisms. Here, we used histological approaches to map leaf Na+ distribution in tomato (Solanum) species with contrasting salt-tolerance strategies. In the moderately salt-tolerant, Na+-excluding domesticated tomato (cv.
