Thus, stomatal traits of barley penultimate leaves and their association with yield are largely driven by environmental variation and coordinated stomatal trait responses of leaf surfaces to abiotic environment are important for barley adaptation.

works.title: Superior haplotypes for transforming crop breeding
CaSNF1 interacts with and phosphorylates CaHD-ZIP to enhance cold tolerance in pepper
Mediator CKM and MUTE-ICE1/SCRM2 reinforce auxin responsiveness to sustain MUTE expression during stomatal lineage differentiation
works.abstract: MUTE functions as a pivotal transcription factor that governs the transition from self-renewal to differentiation in meristemoids during stomatal development. This transition requires MUTE expression to reach a critical threshold, yet the mechanisms that maintain its expression homeostasis remain unclear. Here, we show that the Mediator CDK8 kinase module (CKM) acts as a transcriptional coactivator of the MUTE-ICE1/SCRM2 complex to regulate meristemoid fate. Specifically, CKM cooperates with MUTE-ICE1/SCRM2 to promote the transcription of the auxin-responsive genes, such as SAUR52 and SAUR53, thereby enhancing local auxin response in meristemoids. AUXIN RESPONSE FACTORs (ARFs), including ARF6, ARF7, and ARF19, then bind to MUTE promoter and contribute to its transcription, establishing a positive feedback loop. Disruption of CKM or MUTE-ICE1/SCRM2 components reduces SAUR52/53 expression and auxin responses, leading to decreased MUTE transcription, excessive meristemoid self-renewal divisions and arrested differentiation. These defects can be partially rescued by exogenous auxin application or by overexpression of SAUR53 in the mutants. Together, our results uncover a self-reinforcing transcriptional-auxin circuit in which CKM-assisted MUTE-ICE1/SCRM2 amplifies auxin response, and auxin reciprocally sustains MUTE expression. This feedback mechanism ensures that MUTE reaches the threshold required to terminate meristemoid self-renewal and initiate differentiation, revealing how transcriptional regulation and hormone signaling are integrated to control stem cell-like behaviors during tissue patterning.

works.title: How RNA methylation regulates jasmonic acid biosynthesis and plant aging
works.abstract: Annabelle Campbell; How RNA methylation regulates jasmonic acid biosynthesis and plant aging, The Plant Cell, , koag323, https://doi.org/10.1093/plcell/koa

works.title: MITE insertions generate enhancers for iron transporter CwIRT1 activation in citrus
works.abstract: Iron (Fe) deficiency constrains citrus productivity in alkaline soils. Although the high-affinity Fe transporter IRT1 is essential for Fe acquisition, its transcriptional regulation in citrus remains unclear. Here, we reveal that differential tolerance to Fe deficiency between Fe-sensitive Poncirus trifoliata (P. trifoliata) and Fe-tolerant Citrus wilsonii Tanaka (C. wilsonii) is linked to rapid induction of CwIRT1. We further identify 2 unique miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements (MITE1 and MITE2) in the promoter region of CwIRT1, which act as Fe-deficiency-responsive enhancers. These 2 MITEs, respectively, generate binding sites for the transcription factors CwERF12 and CwARF12, both of which are upregulated under low-Fe conditions. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated dual knockout of CwERF12 and CwARF12, but not single mutations, suppresses CwIRT1 expression and reduces root Fe uptake. We propose that MITEs carrying TF-binding motifs can serve as enhancers recruiting stress-responsive transcription factors to activate CwIRT1, highlighting transposable element-mediated cis-regulatory as a driver of nutrient stress adaptation in perennial crops.

works.title: A cotton MAPK cascade protects the cell wall against Verticillium wilt
works.abstract: Marcella Teixeira; A cotton MAPK cascade protects the cell wall against Verticillium wilt, Plant Physiology, , kiag795, https://doi.org/10.1093/plphys/kiag

works.title: Spatiotemporal Transcriptomics of Litchi Fruitlet Abscission Reveals a Compartmentalized Regulatory Network and Identifies LcERF61 as a Key Regulator
works.abstract: Organ abscission is a developmental process crucial for both plant life cycles and agricultural productivity, but its spatial restriction to the tiny abscission zone (AZ) has made investigating the underlying molecular mechanisms challenging. Here, we applied spatiotemporal transcriptomics to dissect fruitlet abscission in litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.). This approach reveals an unexpected spatial compartmentalization of the gene regulatory landscape within the AZ. Upon attenuation of IAA polar transport, local ET, ABA, and GA pathways within the AZ core may converge to form an abscission initiation center. These signals are subsequently interpreted by spatially defined transcription factors, which translate them into domain-specific outputs and coordinate the spatiotemporal programs of cell wall remodeling. Accordingly, we show that the onset of cell degradation within the AZ begins in the central region and then extends to the outer boundary. Crucially, we functionally established LcERF61, which is strongly induced in the AZ following abscission, as a key positive regulator of fruitlet abscission. Moreover, DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq) indicated that LcERF61 directly binds to and activates the promoters of LcIDL1 (INFLORESCENCE DEFICIENT IN ABSCISSION-like) and LcIDL3, which encode small signaling peptides essential for abscission. Our findings reveal a spatially compartmentalized regulatory framework for organ abscission and establish the LcERF61-LcIDL1/3 module as a key signaling hub, providing a conceptual advance in understanding how plants execute precise organ abscission.

works.title: Revisiting ethylene metabolism: Identification of an ethylene glycol-glucose conjugate reveals active ethylene metabolism in Populus
works.abstract: In many plant species, the role of ethylene as a phytohormone signal has been well-studied, yet its direct metabolism in planta has received less attention. Consequently, this gap constrains our understanding of the full impact ethylene has on plant systems. During multiple evaluations of resilience in Populus spp., we detected an unidentified metabolite with plausible links to ethylene. In this study, we structurally characterize and identify this molecule as an ethylene glycol glucose conjugate (EGGC). Ethylene-perturbation experiments revealed EGGC abundance is positively correlated with endogenous ethylene production, supporting EGGC as an ethylene-derived metabolite. Stable-isotope labeled EGGC supplied to the media was detected in stem/leaf tissue, indicating long-distance translocation of the compound. These studies also revealed enzymatic conversion in stem/leaf tissue of EGGC to ethylene glycol (EG), with EG levels maintained and accompanied by shifts in downstream metabolites (i.e., glycolic acid and oxalic acid). These results suggest that EGGC participates in active metabolism rather than serves as a waste product. Collectively, the findings reported in this study demonstrate that EGGC is a biomarker of whole-plant ethylene production and position it as a tool for monitoring ethylene-associated stress responses.

works.title: Reconstructing spore evolution recalibrates the timescale of land plant diversification
works.abstract: The origin and evolution of land plants precipitated fundamental changes to the Earth system and enabled the diversification of life on land. Their early evolution is documented by a rich fossil record of sporopollenin-walled spores that is difficult to interpret because the evolution of plant spore characteristics is unresolved. We employ a suite of ancestral state estimation methods to elucidate the pattern of spore character evolution among land plants. We find that the ancestral embryophyte underwent monoplastidic meiosis and produced unenveloped spores with a three-layered sporoderm. We infer that trilete spores (that developed in tetrahedral tetrads), traditionally considered a feature of vascular plants, were produced by the crown-embryophyte. We recalibrate the molecular timescale of early land plant evolution on the basis of a reinterpretation of the fossil record in this light. We find that crown-embryophytes originated in the Late Ordovician (457-450 Ma) and that both crown-tracheophytes (432-428 Ma) and crown-bryophytes (445-429 Ma) diverged in the early Silurian.

works.title: Synthetic activation of gibberellin signalling reveals spatial coordination of root growth
Author Correction: Light-induced LLPS of the CRY2/SPA1/FIO1 complex regulating mRNA methylation and chlorophyll homeostasis in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: In the version of this article originally published, several values in the Source Data for Fig. 4i were incorrectly transcribed during Source Data preparation. The published figure panel was generated from the correct original Prism datasets and is unaffected. In addition, one nonlinear-fit result used in Fig. 4j was derived from the mean of three experiments rather than the independent second replicate. Figure 4j and the corresponding Source Data have been corrected. Minor typographical errors in the Fig. 4 legend, Supplementary Table 6 and one Source Data worksheet label have also been corrected. None of these changes affects the conclusions of the article. For comparison, the original figure is available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

works.title: Gap‐Free Cannabis sativa Assemblies Reveal Post‐Polyploid Genome Remodelling and Refine the Evolution of Cannabinoid Synthase Genes
works.abstract: Despite the therapeutic importance of cannabinoids, the scarcity of gap-free Cannabis genomes has limited the dissection of the genetic and genomic basis of cannabinoid biosynthesis and genome evolution. Here, we generated two haplotype-phased, gap-free, gold-standard assemblies and used them to investigate post-polyploid genome remodelling and refine the evolutionary history of cannabinoid synthase genes. Analyses of these gap-free assemblies recovered a γ whole-genome triplication (WGT) signal shared with core eudicots and provided no evidence for additional lineage-specific whole-genome duplication (WGD) in Cannabis. The extant Cannabis genome reflects long-term retention and divergence of a subset of γ-derived duplicates, together with subsequent non-WGD-derived gene duplications and repeat-associated remodelling that contributed substantially to present-day genome diversification. Furthermore, phylogenomic, structural and syntenic evidence indicate that a precursor duplication predating the Cannabis-Humulus split gave rise to two lineages retained in Cannabis on chromosomes 7 and 2. In Cannabis, the chromosome 7 lineage subsequently expanded and diversified into the functional cannabinoid synthase genes, whereas Humulus retained only the lineage resembling the Cannabis chromosome 2 copy. This asymmetric retention and diversification provide new insights into the origin and specialization of cannabinoid biosynthesis in Cannabis. Together, these results provide a high-quality genomic framework for understanding the history of polyploidy, the evolution of the cannabinoid synthase gene and genome diversification in Cannabis.

works.title: High frequency minirhizotron observations reveal diel patterns of root growth under water stress
works.abstract: Growth and death of vegetation control both the amount of carbon held in living biomass and much of the flow between the atmosphere and soils, the largest terrestrial carbon reservoir. However, long-term field datasets on belowground growth dynamics are rare. Knowledge is lacking on how root growth patterns relate to the environment, fluctuating carbon and water availability, and internal plant physiological control, at both seasonal and diel scales. We imaged roots in a temperate grassland using automated minirhizotrons and interpreting root length density (RLD) automatically twice a day for nine months. From winter to autumn, we always observed some root growth in individual images, but with decreasing net RLD (indicative of net turnover) becoming predominant later in the season. Roots grew day-round except during a period of about one month in spring when root growth was only in daytime. This was a period without rain, during which soil moisture depleted rapidly, but not at its driest point. We discuss potential causes for both overall and short-term growth patterns, particularly the change in drivers of growth from internal storage to new photosynthates, or limits imposed by water availability - both soil moisture and rainfall - under shifting environmental conditions.

works.title: Positive feedback between cytokinins and sugars controls correlative inhibition in two-branched pea seedlings
works.abstract: The work proposed a correlative inhibition (CI) model based on positive feedback (PF) between sugars (Sug) and cytokinis (CKs) - CK activates Sug uploading to sink organs, and Sug increases CK content and activates CK signalling. This creates an unstable PF system capable of triggering the development of dominant and suppressed shoots on the same plant. The predictions of the Sug-CK model were tested on two-branched pea seedlings. Sug deficiency (removal of part of the cotyledons) and CK deficiency (treatment with an inhibitor of CK synthesis) in accordance with the model increased the occurrence of unequal-branched plants. Surprisingly, auxin was found to be inactive in the regulation of CI. In the apical buds of lateral shoots, a Sug deficiency reduced the CK signal, as measured by the expression of PsRR5 gene, whilst inhibition of CK synthesis reduced Sug accumulation, thereby confirming the presence of PF between CK and Sug. A deficiency of Sug enhanced the effect of a CK deficiency in reducing CK status, explaining the synergistic effect of both deficiencies on CI. A deficiency of strigolactones (SL) in the rms5 and rms1 mutants and SL insensitivity in the rms4 mutant completely abolished the effects of CK and Sug deficiencies on CI. It was demonstrated on the rms5 mutant that a CK deficiency did not affect Sug levels thus explaining the insensitivity to CK-Sug deficiencies in SL mutants. The BRANCHED1 (BRC1) gene is an important regulator of plant branching, and its absence in the brc1 mutant resulted in a lack of response to Sug deficiency with regard to both CI and CK status. It has thus been shown that SL signalling and the BRC1 gene are involved in the Sug-CK interaction, thereby playing a role in the regulation of CI.

works.title: Field‑Based Dissection of Stomatal Anatomy and Conductance Reveals Stable QTL Under Drought and Heat in Wheat
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Stomatal traits balance carbon gain with water loss, yet their breeding potential in wheat remains underexploited. This study investigated physiological and anatomical stomatal responses across 2 years of large‐scale field trials under water‐limitation and warming treatments. Across both seasons, stomatal conductance ( g s ) declined under stress, reflecting strong environmental constraint on gas‐exchange (water‐limitation: −26.9%; warming‐treatment: −13.8%). Partitioning responses by surface identified the adaxial surface as the dominant contributor to g s variation and the most stress responsive. Despite increases in theoretical anatomical gas‐exchange capacity ( g smax ), stomatal conductance efficiency ( g se ) declined, indicating decoupling between anatomical capacity and realised conductance. Drought reduced stomatal size while increasing density whereas warming increased size and density, yet both responses maintained gas‐exchange capacity. Moderate‐to‐high heritability was observed for anatomical traits (water‐limitation: 0.13–0.57; warming‐treatment: 0.42–0.71), contrasting with lower, less stable heritability for g s (water‐limitation: 0.13–0.41; warming‐treatment: 0.13–0.50). Genome‐wide‐association‐mapping identified 60 putative QTLs, predominantly for anatomical traits. Candidate loci on chromosomes 7B, 2B, 3B and 5 A emerged as pleiotropic genomic intervals influencing stomatal anatomy across environments. These findings indicate that wheat maintains anatomical gas‐exchange capacity while dynamically regulating realised conductance under stress, highlighting anatomically stable stomatal traits as promising breeding targets for climate resilience and yield stability.

works.title: Nano‐Biochar‐Assisted Intercropping Alleviates Fusarium Wilt of Faba Bean by Enhancing Rhizosphere Soil Health in Long‐Term Continuous Cropping Soil
works.abstract: Long-term faba bean (Vicia faba L.) monocropping degrades soil and promotes Fusarium wilt. Intercropping and nano-biochar (N-BC) can improve soil health and suppress soil-borne diseases. However, their combined effects on Fusarium wilt in faba bean remain unclear. This study assessed whether combining intercropping with N-BC could improve faba bean rhizosphere soil health and reduce Fusarium wilt under prolonged continuous cropping. A pot experiment was conducted to compare faba bean monocropping with faba bean-wheat intercropping under an unamended control, biochar (BC), and N-BC treatments. Fusarium wilt incidence and rhizosphere physicochemical and biological properties were assessed. Intercropping reduced disease incidence and disease index by 8.57%-34.53% and 8.32%-30.20%, respectively. Under intercropping, BC reduced these measures by 14.95% and 15.17% compared with the control. N-BC further reduced them by 50.02% and 54.74% compared with BC. The combined treatment increased soil water content, macroaggregate proportion, organic matter, dissolved organic carbon, ammonium nitrogen, nitrate nitrogen, available phosphorus, sucrase, urease, neutral phosphatase, catalase, and polyphenol oxidase. It decreased bulk density and benzoic, cinnamic, p-hydroxybenzoic, ferulic, and vanillic acids. These changes coincided with higher relative abundances of potentially beneficial bacteria, including Pseudomonas, and a lower relative abundance of Fusarium. Combining faba bean - wheat intercropping with N-BC amendment mitigated Fusarium wilt while improving rhizosphere soil structure, nutrient status, and enzyme activity, reducing phenolic acid accumulation, and reshaping microbial composition. These findings support a soil-health-based strategy for sustainable continuous cropping management.

works.title: Molecular Basis of Silicon‐Mediated Plant Defense: Transporters, Cell Wall Integrity, Redox‐Hormone Crosstalk, and Epigenetic Priming
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon (Si) is emerging as a key modulator, and its molecular mechanism of defense regulation keeps emerging. This review focus on Si‐uptake by Lsi‐type transporters, deposition in cuticles and cell wall, redox buffering, modify cell wall integrity (CWI) and hormonal signaling to increase resistance against adverse conditions and to reshape plant‐microbe‐soil interaction in rhizosphere. By highlighting the emerging research on Si‐mediated regulations at molecular scale, we proposed two working hypotheses which are ‘mechanical buffer model’ for soluble‐Si and ‘dynamic signaling model’ for Si‐nanomaterials (Si‐NPs). Mechanical buffer model states that Si‐fortified walls could stabilize the ROS profile and wall mechanics to maintain and primed state for cell while dynamic signaling model states that Si‐NPs follow an additional vesicle‐mediated uptake forming a corona protein, elicit ROS‐bursts, robust activation of FERONIA‐like receptors, Ca 2+ channels, and JA/SA signaling. Furthermore, association of Si‐associated chromatin and siRNAs were summarized and how these Si‐mediated alterations in DNA methylation under stress conditions could support the stress memory and defense priming. Overall, this framework could provide a molecular basis for Si‐mediated inputs and breeding approaches with the aim of climate‐resilient crops.

works.title: PyMYB106‐PyLAC12 Modulates Callus Browning Through Phenylpropanoid‐Flavonoid Metabolism in Pinus yunnanensis
works.abstract: Callus browning is the main obstacle in the process of in vitro culture of woody plants, which is more serious in conifers. Here, multi-omics integration and transgenic approaches are employed to dissect the regulatory network of callus browning in Pinus yunnanensis. Browning callus showed marked reductions in total phenolics, flavonoids, and flavanols, with a concurrent increase in total quinone content. Non-browning callus maintained low endogenous hormone homeostasis while sustaining elevated salicylic acid (SA) and 6-benzylaminopurine (6-BA) levels to enhance reactive oxygen species scavenging capacity. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and two-way orthogonal partial least squares (O2PLS) identified PyLAC12 as the central driver of browning. Overexpression of PyLAC12 substantially reduced phenolic acid and flavonoid contents and exacerbated browning, whereas PyLAC12 knockout produced the opposite effect. The upstream transcription factor PyMYB106 was further identified to directly bind the CAACCA motif and positively regulate PyLAC12. Collectively, this study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which the PyMYB106-PyLAC12 module drives callus browning through reprogramming flavonoid-phenylpropanoid metabolic network.

works.title: An edible invitation: Recruiting beneficial fungi through what they eat
works.abstract: Orchid seeds cannot germinate without help from fungi. This commentary features a recent study showing that Cremastra appendiculata seeds release two small compounds that attract a helpful fungus and also serve as food for it. This suggests that plants may recruit fungal partners before contact by offering edible chemical cues to nearby fungi.

works.title: Two roads to a full ear: How maize domestication shaped form and function
works.abstract: Early farmers turned bushy teosinte into maize by two genetic routes: one route reshaped the plant's architecture, and a newly identified route changed its physiology, sending more sugar and nitrogen to the ear. Both increased the share of the plant that becomes grain, and both can guide future crop improvement.

works.title: HYPK-ing up COP1 to put the brakes on photomorphogenesis
works.abstract: Jiajun Wang, Yueyao Wang; HYPK-ing up COP1 to put the brakes on photomorphogenesis, The Plant Cell, , koag322, https://doi.org/10.1093/plcell/koag322

works.title: Photosynthesis-derived carbon gates cell cycle activation to enable hormone-autonomous shoot regeneration
works.abstract: Shoot regeneration is a powerful model for cell fate reprogramming but how it occurs in nature remains poorly understood because studies in Arabidopsis thaliana conventionally rely on in vitro assays supplemented with exogenous hormones and sugars. Here, we established the Hormone-autonomY Direct Regeneration Assay (HYDRA) in which removal of the shoot apical meristem (SAM) initiates shoot regeneration from the cotyledon-hypocotyl boundary without hormone or sugar supplementation. We identify photosynthesis-derived carbon and the boundary domain as two separable but convergent requirements for shoot regeneration in HYDRA. Following SAM removal, carbon availability increases in the boundary domain where it activates cell-cycle progression via the RETINOBLASTOMA-RELATED1 (RBR1) pathway. Carbon deprivation blocks regeneration despite induction of shoot meristem genes, indicating proliferative activation is limiting. Pre-existing shoot-competent boundary cells give rise to regenerated shoots upon cell-cycle activation, while their perturbation impairs regeneration despite sufficient carbon. Carbon therefore gates the proliferative activation of these cells, enabling functional shoot meristem formation. Additionally, exogenous carbon supply overcomes the requirement for SAM removal to induce shoot formation, indicating that carbon availability also acts as an initiation cue. Together, this study reveals an inherent capacity for hormone-autonomous shoot regeneration and identifies photosynthesis-derived carbon as a central regulator of this process.

works.title: NIK receptor kinases propagate phytocytokine-triggered immunity by driving early phosphorylation events
Hierarchical Regulatory Module AcERF1–AcHAT5–AcERF10 Modulates Ethylene‐Dependent Starch Degradation in Postharvest Kiwifruit
works.abstract: The transcriptional regulatory network underlying ethylene-governed starch-to-sugar conversion remains poorly understood. We elucidated the hierarchical regulatory cascade linking ethylene signalling to starch degradation in postharvest kiwifruit. Ethylene treatment accelerated fruit softening, starch degradation, and soluble sugar accumulation, whereas 1-methylcyclopropene treatment produced opposite effects in kiwifruit. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified 3 β-amylase genes (AcBAM3.1/3.3/3.5) and 16 transcription factors (TFs) as highly correlated with starch-to-sugar conversion. AcERF10 was isolated as a direct transcriptional activator of AcBAM3.1/3.3/3.5 and the ethylene biosynthetic gene AcACO1. AcERF10 overexpression promoted starch degradation and sugar accumulation; silencing this gene resulted in opposite phenotypes. AcERF10 was directly activated by AcERF1 and AcHAT5-TFs that are induced by ethylene. AcERF1 bound to and activated the promoter of AcHAT5, while AcHAT5 bound to the AcERF10 promoter and interacted with AcERF10 to synergistically activate expression of AcBAMs and AcACO1, identifying a regulatory cascade of AcERF1-AcHAT5-AcERF10. Overexpression of either AcERF1 or AcHAT5 promoted downstream gene expression, accelerated starch degradation, and enhanced sugar accumulation, whereas silencing of either gene suppressed these processes. This study uncovers an ethylene-triggered, multi-layer transcriptional regulatory network that governs starch-to-sugar conversion during postharvest kiwifruit ripening, providing new mechanistic insights into ethylene-regulated fruit quality development during postharvest storage.

works.title: The Cytosolic Iron–Sulfur Cluster Assembly Targeting Complex Is Hijacked by Magnaporthe Effector AvrPi9 to Suppress Rice Resistance
works.abstract: The cytosolic iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster assembly (CIA) targeting complex mediates the maturation of cytosolic and nuclear Fe-S proteins and governs core eukaryotic cellular processes. However, whether this complex contributes to plant disease resistance remains unclear. Here, we show that the Magnaporthe oryzae avirulence effector AvrPi9 targets the host CIA targeting complex to suppress rice blast resistance. AvrPi9 physically interacts with and stabilizes OsAE7, a core subunit of the CIA targeting complex. Using biochemical and genetic approaches, we demonstrate that OsAE7 facilitates Fe-S protein maturation, including the Fe-S protein aconitase OsACO1, and negatively regulates blast resistance in cooperation with another CIA targeting complex subunit, OsCIA1, and the carrier protein OsNAR1 in rice. Furthermore, ectopic expression of AvrPi9 enhances the activity of the CIA complex and the maturation of OsACO1. Knockout of OsACO1 elevates ferrous iron levels, triggers a reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst, and activates pathogenesis-related gene transcription, thereby strengthening rice resistance to blast. Our findings reveal a critical role of the CIA targeting complex in plant disease resistance and uncover a novel virulence strategy whereby AvrPi9 hijacks the host CIA pathway to dampen basal resistance and promote infection.

works.title: Phospholipid analogs and beyond: pleiotropic roles of betaine lipids in phycology, ecology, and biomedicine
works.abstract: Betaine lipids (BLs) are a class of non-phosphorus glycerolipids widely found in microalgae, fungi, bacteria, mosses, and ferns. For decades, the central paradigm regarding the biological function of BLs has been their role in substituting for phospholipids under phosphate starvation-a crucial adaptive mechanism for survival in oligotrophic environments. However, accumulating evidence indicates that the functional diversity of BLs is far more extensive. Recent studies have demonstrated their distinct roles in fatty acid metabolism, adaptation to various environmental stresses, and ecological interactions such as symbiosis and predation. This review summarizes current insights into the pleiotropic roles of BLs in microalgal physiology and ecology, moving beyond their role as mere phospholipid surrogates. Furthermore, we highlight the recently discovered bioactive function of BL derivative in mammals.

works.title: Double mutants of granule-bound starch synthases, GBSSI and GBSSII, revealed their roles and the existence of amylose-like branched α-glucans in rice
works.abstract: Two isozymes of granule-bound starch synthase (GBSS), GBSSI and GBSSII, are present in rice. While GBSSI is solely responsible for amylose synthesis in endosperm and gbss1 mutants accumulate glutinous starch in grains, the role of GBSSII remains unclear. In this study, rice gbss2 mutants were isolated for the first time in cereals and gbss1 gbss2 double mutants were generated to clarify the respective roles of GBSS isozymes. Iodine staining of starch confirmed that amylose in pollen is synthesized by GBSSI and those in leaf and root tip are by GBSSII. Gel filtration chromatography of debranched starch from endosperm and leaf sheath revealed that GBSSI and GBSSII appear to be the primary amylose synthases in endosperm and in leaf sheath, respectively. However, the absence of the primary GBSS in the respective organs did not result in the complete elimination of amylose. A small peak detected in the fractions corresponding to amylose was shown to be α-glucans by glucoamylase digestion, and the presence of branches was revealed by detailed structure analyses. The amylose-like, branched α-glucans found in the double mutants, which probably also existed in single mutants and wild-type starches, were suggested to be synthesized by other enzymes than GBSSs.

works.title: Benzoic Acid Secreted From the Chickpea Root Promotes Persistent Colonisation by Specific Soil Microbes
works.abstract: The plant root tip is highly sensitive to environmental cues and exerts sensory, chemical and movement responses. However, the microbial diversification at the root tip, and the nature of root-selection for microbes, are poorly understood. This study investigated root exudation and microbiome colonisation in the chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) root tip and root base, in diverse soils. For the endosphere microbiome, deterministic effects were more important than stochastic processes in shaping the root tip microbiome, indicated by the stable endophyte composition independent of the soil microbiota background. A genotype with high secretion of benzoic acid (BA), was consistently colonised by 3 core ASV (Amplicon Sequence Variant) from the Burkholderia clade. Two of 98 isolated strains were confirmed as the culturable candidates of the core ASV, both of which were characterised by superior BA tolerance and the ability to utilise BA as a sole carbon source, demonstrated through high expression of BA degradation genes. Additionally, one IAA-producing coloniser specifically promoted the growth of its original host genotype across different soils, but provided no consistent benefits for other genotypes. Our results reveal the mechanisms by which soil microbes interact with root exudates of a host genotype to establish colonisation.

works.title: PPR9 mediates mitochondrial nad transcript maturation required for complex I biogenesis and early plant development in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: Abstract The biogenesis and function of plant mitochondria relies on the expression of the organellar genome, which involves extensive post-transcriptional processing of organellar transcripts in order to generate mature functional RNAs. This includes the removal of introns from many essential organellar transcripts through splicing, a process mediated by diverse nuclear-encoded RNA-processing factors, including numerous members of the pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) protein family. Here, we report the analysis of PPR9 (At1g03560), a mitochondrial P-class PPR protein originally identified in genetic screens for essential protein cofactors. Loss of PPR9 function results in embryonic arrest at early stages of seed development. In vitro rescued homozygous ppr9 mutant plants could be recovered and maintained using a modified in vitro embryo-rescue method. The mutants display delayed growth and development which are associated with altered mitochondrial functions. Molecular analyses reveal that PPR9 functions in the splicing of several mitochondrial transcripts encoding respiratory complex I (CI) subunits, including nad2 intron 3 and nad7 introns 1 and 2. Accordingly, CI assembly is disrupted in ppr9 plants, resulting in altered OXPHOS activity and broad physiological defects. Together, these findings identify PPR9 as a key regulator of mt-RNA maturation in Arabidopsis, enabling CI biogenesis and optimal respiratory functions, and further highlight the roles of nuclear-encoded factors in coordinating mitochondria functions and (early) plant growth and development.

works.title: MAKR6 integrates TMK and CAMEL/CANAR signalling for auxin canalization in Arabidopsis
works.abstract: Adaptive plant development is orchestrated, among other means, by directional, intercellular transport of the phytohormone auxin. Self-organizing phenomena such as flexible vasculature formation depend on auxin canalization, which manifests as the gradual formation of auxin-transporting channels through feedback between auxin signalling and transport. Here we identify MAKR6 as a component of this feedback. MAKR6 transcripts accumulate in vascular cells and are tightly regulated by auxin via the Aux/IAA-ARF-WRKY23 transcriptional cascade. MAKR6 is required for auxin canalization-dependent processes, including leaf venation, vascular regeneration and de novo channel formation from local auxin sources. Mechanistically, MAKR6 interacts with the PIN1 auxin transporter and modulates its trafficking and polarization. MAKR6 also associates with and integrates TMK1/4 and CAMEL-CANAR, two key receptor-like kinase complexes involved in canalization. Together, our study establishes MAKR6 as a multifaceted regulator that couples transcriptional auxin signalling to PIN1 repolarization and coordinates multiple RLK-mediated pathways into a concerted process. This provides mechanistic insight into auxin canalization and exemplifies a framework for exploring similar regulatory nodes in other developmental contexts.

works.title: A Heat‐Inducible Rubisco Activase Safeguards Photosynthesis via Multilevel Regulation and Dual Function
works.abstract: Rubisco activase (RCA) is critical for maintaining photosynthetic efficiency under heat stress, yet its regulatory mechanisms and functional diversification remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize a novel heat-inducible RCA family member (RCA1), which plays a pivotal role in mediating multidimensional thermotolerance in a tropical azalea. Both heterologous and homologous overexpression of RCA1 significantly mitigated heat-induced cellular damage and better maintained photosynthetic capacity, confirming its essential function in thermal resilience. Heat-induced RCA1 expression is transcriptionally activated by a synergistic HSFA1-HSFA2 complex and post-transcriptionally fine-tuned by extensive alternative splicing, forming a multilevel regulatory network under heat stress. Beyond its canonical Rubisco-activating enzymatic activity, RCA1 exhibits an additional thermoprotective function that suppresses the thermal aggregation of several chloroplast proteins, such as Lhca2, PetC and PsaK. RCA1 also interacts with the constitutive RCA2, likely through heteromeric RCA complex assembly, which helps retain RCA2 in a soluble pool under heat stress. Evolutionary analyses reveal functional divergence within the RCA family, with convergent evolution of heat-inducible RCA clades in Panicoideae grasses. Collectively, our findings uncover a novel dual-functional heat-inducible RCA, which provides a promising target for photosynthetic bioengineering to enhance crop thermotolerance and ensure agricultural sustainability under global warming.

works.title: VvSLR1-VvGAD1 mediated regulation of VvGA20ox4 contributes to GA homeostasis and seed development in grapevine
works.abstract: Gibberellins (GAs) are widely used in grape cultivation to promote berry enlargement and induce seedlessness, but their effects on seed development and the regulatory mechanism remain poorly understood. In this study, exogenous GA3 significantly reduced seed weight in grapevine, indicating impaired seed development. To investigate the underlying mechanism, we characterized the grape DELLA protein SLENDER RICE 1 (VvSLR1). Overexpression of VvSLR1 in tomato caused a dwarf and compact phenotype but had limited effects on fruit and seed development under normal conditions. However, GA3 treatment caused a stronger reduction in seed formation in VvSLR1-overexpressing plants, whereas paclobutrazol (PAC), an inhibitor of GA biosynthesis, allowed relatively normal seed formation, indicating that the effect of VvSLR1 on reproductive development is GA-dependent. In grape calli, VvSLR1 overexpression altered GA metabolism and the expression of several VvGA20ox and VvGA3ox genes, suggesting a role for VvSLR1 in GA homeostasis. We further identified GAMETOPHYTE DEFECTIVE 1 (VvGAD1), whose Arabidopsis homolog is involved in gametophyte development, as a nuclear-localized VvSLR1-interacting protein. VvGAD1 associated with the promoter of GA 20-oxidase 4 (VvGA20ox4), and co-expression of VvGAD1 and VvSLR1 significantly enhanced VvGA20ox4 promoter activity. Moreover, heterologous expression of VvGA20ox4 in Arabidopsis increased silique length and seed number, while exogenous GA3 suppressed VvGA20ox4 promoter activity. Together, these findings suggest that VvSLR1 acts as a regulatory node linking GA signaling and homeostasis, with the VvSLR1-VvGAD1-VvGA20ox4 relationship representing a potential regulatory branch involved in GA-dependent seed development.

works.title: Fruit growth rate influences cortical xylem transport, calcium delivery, and bitter pit incidence of apple
works.abstract: Bitter pit of apple is commonly ascribed to calcium dilution because symptoms are positively associated with fruit mass. A dilution effect implies that calcium transport or supply cannot keep pace with fruit growth but does not identify the mechanism. Disparate sink:source ratios or transient photosynthetic inhibition were used to alter 'Honeycrisp' fruit growth rate (FGR) to study fruit xylem transport kinetics and peel calcium concentration. FGR and xylem dysfunction increased with decreasing sink:source ratio. Xylem transport declined to 50% of maximum 1.7 weeks earlier under Low than High sink:source ratios and peel calcium decreased concomitantly with xylem transport. Treatment effects on bitter pit incidence were explained by integrating time-dependent xylem transport curves into an empirical 'cumulative xylem' function. Regressing this function on FGR conflated treatment differences. When photosynthetic light reactions were inhibited by episodic limb shading, FGR was reduced and xylem transport increased; shade removal caused transient surges in FGR and concomitant reduction in xylem transport. Changes in calcium concentration were less responsive to shade due to stomatal limits to water transport. Combined, the results support that FGR compromises xylem transport, effectively limiting calcium supply and exacerbating bitter pit, the magnitude of which depends on the onset of xylem dysfunction.

works.title: Multi-isolate GWAS identifies broad-spectrum and isolate-specific resistance-associated loci for Septoria tritici blotch in synthetic hexaploid wheat
works.abstract: Abstract Key message Synthetic hexaploid wheat harbours STB resistance-associated loci with multi-isolate and isolate-specific effects, with partly independent genetic control of pycnidia suppression and necrosis. Abstract Septoria tritici blotch (STB), caused by Zymoseptoria tritici , is a major constraint on wheat production. Erosion of host resistance and declining fungicide efficacy highlight the need to exploit new resistance sources, including synthetic hexaploid wheat (SHW). We used a three-family nested association mapping (NAM) population derived from Niab SHW donors (SHW.035, SHW.054, and SHW.075) crossed with the UK variety Robigus to dissect the genetic basis of STB resistance under controlled conditions. Seedlings were challenged with five UK Z. tritici isolates differing in virulence, and disease progress was quantified separately as necrosis (AUDPC_N) and pycnidia coverage (AUDPC_P). Many SHW-derived lines showed strong suppression of pycnidia despite visible necrosis, consistent with partial genetic decoupling of pathogen reproduction and host tissue damage. GWAS identified a major multi-isolate association on chromosome 3D ( qSTB-3D.1 ), contributed by SHW.035 and detected in response to four of the five isolates, defining a 23.7 Mb candidate resistance-associated interval. This interval encompasses the Stb16q region but also contains other plausible resistance candidates, including a WAK close to the strongest association at 609.21 Mb; the causal basis therefore remains unresolved. Additional isolate-specific resistance-associated intervals were detected on chromosomes 1B, 2D, 3A, and 6D. In a BC 2 F 2 population derived from a resistant SHW.035-derived NAM line, pycnidia suppression segregated in a 3:1 ratio consistent with a single dominant factor, whereas necrosis showed more complex inheritance. These findings show that Niab SHWs are a valuable source of STB resistance and highlight the potential to select for reduced pathogen reproduction independently of visible leaf damage.

works.title: Map-based cloning of the susceptibility locus conditioning bs6 resistance in pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) encoding mutant alleles of pseudokinase proteins
works.abstract: Abstract Key message The bs6 resistance gene against bacterial spot was identified by map-based cloning in pepper (C. annuum L.). Abstract The recessive bs6 61 locus of pepper Capsicum annuum L. var. 61R (Ca61R) conditions a non-hypersensitive resistance trait, characterized by a slightly swollen, pale green, photosynthetically active leaf tissue, following Xanthomonas euvesicatoria Race 6 (XeR6) infection. In contrast, C. annuum cv. Feherozon (CaFo) is susceptible to XeR6. Map-based cloning of the bs6 61 locus revealed that the bs6 61 locus encodes three predicted proteins, pbs6 61 npk, pbs6 61 n, pbs6 61 pk in Ca61R which are the counterpart of the three wild type predicted proteins, pBs6 Fo NPK, pBs6 Fo N and pBs6 Fo PK in CaFo, respectively. Sequence analysis revealed that the pBs6FoNPK protein showed 35% identity and 53% similarity to the ZRK4 pseudokinase (pAtZRK4) identified in Arabidopsis thaliana , which possesses N-terminal and C-terminal (pseudokinase) domains. The pBs6 Fo N and pBs6 Fo PK proteins resemble the N-terminal and C-terminal domains of the pBs6FoNPK protein, respectively, thus, they also contain pseudokinase domains/sequences. In Ca61R, pbs6 61 npk and pbs6 61 n are truncated counterparts of pBs6 Fo NPK and pBs6 Fo N, respectively, as a consequence of a single-nucleotide insertion that causes frameshifts and premature stop codons, whereas pbs6 61 pk differs from pBs6 Fo PK by a single amino acid, a serine to alanine substitution at position 133. These three proteins are considered functionless. The ORF of pBs6 Fo N, pBs6 Fo PK and pbs6 61 n, pbs6 61 pk, respectively, are encoded by a single transcript in both parental plants. For this reason the translation of pBs6 Fo PK was ambiguous, however, the expression of pBs6 Fo N-dsRed fusion protein demonstrated that pBs6 Fo PK in fact can be translated. The three wild type proteins (pBs6 Fo NPK, pBs6 Fo N and pBs6 Fo PK) were independently responsible for ETS (effector-triggered susceptibility), because all three genes had to be in mutant configuration to manifest the resistant phenotype, in addition, any one of the three was able to reverse the resistant phenotype to susceptibility. Functional analysis using virus-induced gene silencing and transient genetic complementation demonstrated that the three CaFo proteins contribute redundantly to XeR6 susceptibility. Silencing either Bs6 Fo NPK, Bs6 Fo N and Bs6 Fo PK alone did not alter susceptibility, whereas simultaneous silencing of these genes conferred resistance. Conversely, the individual expression of pBs6 Fo NPK, pBs6 Fo N, and pBs6 Fo PK, in the resistant Ca61R background each restored susceptibility. These results demonstrate that the three Bs6 proteins act redundantly to promote XeR6 susceptibility and that loss of function of all three corresponding proteins was required for the recessive resistance phenotype conferred by bs6 61 .

works.title: Genome-wide characterization of DUB genes in Betula platyphylla and BpUBP3 function in pollen tube growth
Generation and characterization of a barley strigolactone mutant collection: from plant architecture to drought stress response
works.abstract: Strigolactones (SLs) are known to regulate shoot architecture and to be involved in plant responses to environmental stress, whereas their specific contributions to drought adaptation in barley remain incompletely defined. In this study, we analysed transcriptional, hormonal, and physiological responses to water deficit in barley SL mutants affected in early biosynthesis (Hvd10 and Hvd17), late biosynthesis (Hvmax1a), or signalling (Hvd14). The Hvd10, Hvd17, and Hvd14 mutants exhibited the typical high-tillering phenotype of SL deficiency, whereas Hvmax1a displayed characteristics similar to the wild type (WT), indicating functional differences within the SL biosynthetic pathway. Transcriptome analysis showed a clear overlap in gene expression among the high-tillering SL mutants under both control and drought conditions. We also used computational methods to identify potential transcription factors that might regulate SL-dependent gene expression. A drought experiment showed that SL mutants exhibited reduced biomass, relative water content, and photosynthetic efficiency, with the most pronounced effects observed in the high-tillering lines. Drought also activated the abscisic acid (ABA) pathway in all genotypes, with particularly high accumulation of ABA metabolites in the high-tillering SL mutants. Notably, Hvmax1a resembled the mutant-like metabolic profile, despite maintaining a wild-type-like architecture. Taken together, these results provide new insights into the roles of SL pathway components in drought responses and highlight functional differences among individual genes influencing both plant architecture and stress-related transcriptional programmes. Furthermore, the mutants generated in this study using Cas9-mediated genome editing represent a valuable genetic collection for future research into SL-mediated development and stress responses in barley.

works.title: Manipulation of the PtWOX11-PagKNAT2/6b Module Bidirectionally Regulates Petiole Traits in Populus
works.abstract: Canopy architecture is a critical determinant of productivity in crops and trees, with leaf positioning being a key factor. Petiole length and angle govern leaf positioning and light interception in many flowering plants, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinately regulate these two traits in woody plants remain largely unexplored. Here, we show that a transcriptional module in poplar enables bidirectional control over petiole length and angle. Petiole morphogenesis entails a developmental transition from a meristematic state to a differentiation state, a process blocked by the class I KNOX transcription factor PagKNAT2/6b. Using yeast one-hybrid, electrophoretic mobility shift assays, chromatin affinity purification and transient expression assays in tobacco leaves, we provide evidence that WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX 11 (PtWOX11) binds the PagKNAT2/6b promoter in vitro and transactivates it in heterologous systems. Transcriptomic and qPCR analyses reveal that PtWOX11 maintains a meristematic transcriptional program and suppresses differentiation genes, including those for cell expansion and wall thickening. Accordingly, overexpression of PtWOX11 produces compact petioles with upright leaf angles, whereas its dominant repression yields hyperelongated petioles with reduced leaf angles. Together, these findings suggest a mechanistic framework for manipulating petiole traits and offer a potential strategy for modifying canopy architecture in bioenergy poplar.

works.title: Amino acids on the move: boosting transporters for high-quality crops under reduced nitrogen supply
works.abstract: Nitrogen availability is one of the main factors limiting crop productivity, and the low nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) of crops imposes significant economic and environmental costs. Research on NUE has traditionally focused on improving nitrogen uptake and assimilation; however, the efficient redistribution of assimilated nitrogen within the plant is equally important for growth, yield, and crop quality. Amino acids are the main form in which reduced nitrogen is transported over long distances. Their movement between source and sink tissues depends on a diverse group of membrane transporters belonging to the Amino Acid/Auxin Permeases (AAAP), Amino Acid/Polyamine/Choline transporters (APC), and Usually Multiple Acids Move In and Out Transporters (UMAMIT) families. These transporters mediate amino acid uptake, export, vascular loading and unloading, intracellular transport, and redistribution to developing organs, thereby influencing plant growth, reproductive development and the composition of harvested products. Recent work in cereals, legumes and horticultural crops has shown that modifying amino acid transport can alter biomass production, grain filling, seed protein content, fruit quality, and NUE. In this review, we summarize current knowledge of plant amino acid transporters, from their molecular and physiological functions to their roles in crop yield, nutritional quality and NUE. We also discuss how advances in genome editing, exploitation of natural genetic variation, high-throughput phenotyping and systems biology may facilitate the development of crops with more efficient nitrogen use and improved agricultural sustainability.

works.title: Far-red light enhances mesophyll conductance and photosynthesis in tomato on short timescale below sunlight far-red fraction only
works.abstract: Far-red (FR) light can enhance photosynthesis over short timescales, even at irradiances above the light-limited range. However, it remains unclear whether increasing FR beyond the fraction naturally present in direct sunlight further stimulates photosynthesis, and whether changes in mesophyll conductance to CO2 (gm) contribute to this response. Tomato leaves developed under artificial sunlight-mimicking PAR (16 h; 300 μmol PAR m-2 s-1) with a far-red fraction representative of direct sunlight (R:FR ratio 1.1) were exposed to two actinic light regimes (constant and sinusoidal intensity patterns) combined with three R:FR ratios (10.5, 1.1 and 0.48), representing FR fractions below, similar to, and above those occurring in direct sunlight. High-temporal-resolution gas exchange and carbon isotope (δ13C) measurements (0.2 Hz) were used to quantify gm, stomatal conductance (gs), net CO2 assimilation (Anet) and chloroplastic CO2 concentration. Increasing FR from a low level to the fraction occurring in direct sunlight enhanced both gm and Anet throughout the photoperiod in both actinic light regimes. However, a further increase in FR to levels characteristic of foliar shade did not result in additional increases in either gm or Anet. Estimates of chloroplastic CO2 concentration suggest that the FR-induced increase in apparent gm may help sustain chloroplastic CO2 supply as assimilation increases, but is not sufficient to explain the stimulation of Anet. These results indicate that the short-term photosynthetic response to FR is already established at the FR fraction occurring in direct sunlight and does not increase further with additional FR.

works.title: MucR/Ros family in plant-associated bacteria: from transcriptional regulators to c-di-GMP effectors
works.abstract: The MucR/Ros family are DNA-interacting proteins and pleiotropic regulators of key aspects of the lifecycle in α-proteobacteria, particularly in plant-associated bacteria. The early finding that MucR/Ros proteins contain a C-terminal domain resembling the Cys2His2 eukaryotic Zn-finger domain, indicated MucR/Ros were classical transcription factors binding specific DNA sequences. However, the pleiotropic phenotypes displayed by ros/mucR mutants and the involvement in regulating diverse functions, including cell cycle progression, symbiosis, virulence, motility, production of cell surface components, pointed MucR/Ros as global regulators. Structural and functional studies have positioned MucR/Ros as novel H-NS (Histone-like Nucleoid Structuring)-like proteins in α-proteobacteria, that bind AT-rich DNA sequences and are able of bridging DNA through formation of higher order oligomers. MucR/Ros have also been positioned as xenogeneic silencers (XS), with key roles in horizontal gene acquisition and genome evolution. At least one MucR member is reported to bind the bacterial universal second messenger c-di-GMP, what could thus represent an anti-silencing mechanism as proposed for other bacterial XS. The co-existence of functionally and structurally heterogeneous MucR homologs in the same genome adds further complexity but also warrants renovated interest to decipher the multiple roles of MucR in this important group of bacteria.

works.title: Transcriptome, metabolite profiling and functional genomics provide molecular insights into sweetpotato sprouting
works.abstract: Short dormancy period of sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas) storage roots causes significant economic losses. To unravel the molecular mechanism of sweetpotato sprouting, a comparative transcriptome was performed using storage roots incubated under non-sprout (15 °C) and sprout favouring conditions (25 °C). Our analysis revealed that 7404 genes were differentially expressed between non-sprouting and sprouted storage roots incubated at 25 °C. Further, we observed that gibberellin (GA) biosynthesis gene IbGA3OXIDASE and abscisic acid (ABA) catabolism gene ABA 8'-HYDROXYLASE were upregulated by > 10-fold and > 40-fold, respectively, at the onset of sprouting. Metabolite profiling showed increased GA and cytokinin levels, but reduced ABA content in the sprout initials. Based on conserved expression patterns of phytohormone-related genes during sprouting in potato tubers and sweetpotato storage roots, two genes that were downregulated during sweetpotato sprouting - IbPYL4 (ABA receptor) and IbGA2OXIDASE (GA catabolic enzyme) - were independently overexpressed in potato. Transgenic potato plants overexpressing IbPYL4 or IbGA2OXIDASE exhibited low percentages of tuber sprouting and reduced sprout length. Furthermore, knockdown of the ABA 8'-HYDROXYLASE gene (ABA catabolism) significantly reduced sprout length in sweetpotato storage roots compared to wild-type plants. Overall, our study suggests that selective candidate genes (ABA 8'-HYDROXYLASE, IbPYL4, IbGA3OXIDASE, and IbGA2OXIDASE) could be targeted for developing sweetpotato genotypes with enhanced shelf-life.

works.title: Creation of fragrant wheat by targeted mutagenesis of either BADH1 or both BADH1 and BADH2 using CRISPR/Cas9
works.abstract: Editing TaBADH1 alone or TaBADH1 and TaBADH2 via CRISPR/Cas9 produced fragrant wheat with up to 11.24-fold higher 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline than the wild type without yield penalty, revealing asymmetric functional redundancy between these two genes and providing elite germplasm for wheat quality improvement.

works.title: CPK10 phosphorylates zinc‐sensing transcription factors bZIP19/23 to establish time‐delayed negative feedback in plant zinc homeostasis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc (Zn) homeostasis is essential for plant growth; yet, how zinc‐deficiency‐triggered calcium (Ca) signals are decoded into homeostatic adjustments remains elusive. Here, we identify the calcium‐dependent protein kinase 10 (CPK10) as a key decoder of zinc‐deficiency‐triggered Ca 2+ signals. Under zinc‐deficient conditions, both the protein level and the kinase activity of CPK10 increase. Subsequently, CPK10 interacts with and phosphorylates the zinc‐sensing transcription factors bZIP19 and bZIP23, thereby repressing their DNA‐binding and transcriptional activities. Zrt/Irt‐like protein (ZIP) family members are the primary transporters responsible for zinc uptake from the soil, and CPK10‐mediated phosphorylation of bZIP19 and bZIP23 reduces the expression of ZIP1 , ZIP4 , and defensin‐like (DEFL) genes such as DEFL208 . CPK10 activation is time‐delayed, peaking at 72 h after zinc‐deficiency treatment, providing a braking mechanism that prevents prolonged high‐rate ion flux driven by sustained high‐level expression of zinc transporters. The CPK10‐targeted phosphorylation site Ser241 of bZIP19 is conserved in dicots but absent in monocots, suggesting evolutionary divergence in this zinc homeostasis‐regulatory module. Our work reveals a Ca 2+ –CPK10–bZIP19/23 module that mediates spatiotemporal control of zinc homeostasis, highlighting a key regulatory layer in plant nutrient signaling.

works.title: Evolving new signals from conserved protein scaffolds
Genome-wide characterisation of leaf rust resistance loci in an Eastern European barley collection
works.abstract: Abstract Key message GWAS and inheritance testing uncovered known and potentially new genetic sources of leaf rust resistance in barley, mapping the dominant locus RphCaspian ( RphCas ) to chromosome 4HL in close physical proximity to Rph21. This study has unravelled the genetic architecture of leaf rust in barley and also provides closely linked SNP markers on the 40k Infinium wheat barley array suitable for marker assisted selection. Abstract Barley leaf rust (BLR) is a damaging foliar disease affecting grain yield and quality. Genetic resistance offers a sustainable solution, but often succumbs to breakdown in the absence of stewardship. Sourcing and incorporating novel diverse alleles in breeding programs is challenging yet enhanced by mining unexplored gene pools available in gene banks. In this study, we investigated 318 barley accessions of Eastern European origin for BLR resistance using detailed greenhouse-based host–pathogen interaction assays at the seedling stage. The panel was genotyped using two marker platforms, targeted genotyping-by-sequencing and Infinium™ Wheat Barley 40 K BeadChip Array. Following marker curation, 35,059 SNPs were used for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) using GAPIT/FarmCPU, with associated regions further supported using a BayesR approach. GWAS identified significant peaks corresponding to known resistance loci, including Rph2 , Rph3 and Rph12 , as well as potentially uncharacterised BLR resistance QTL on chromosomes 1HL, 2HL, 3HS and 6HS. Several biparental populations were also developed by crossing three diverse EEB donors carrying broadly effective BLR resistance including: Caspian, Anska and Athenais, with the leaf rust-susceptible barley cultivar Gus. Genetic analysis at the F 3 generation revealed that resistance Athenais was consistent with two-gene inheritance, whereas resistance in Caspian was controlled by a single dominant gene ( RphCas ) and the inheritance of resistance in Anska was inconclusive. Bulked segregant RNA sequencing and conventional bulked segregant analysis (BSA) mapped the Caspian resistance locus to chromosome 4HL. An allelism test using an F 3 population derived from Riccardo, carrying Rph21 , and Caspian, tested with a Puccinia hordei pathotype (5457P+) avirulent to both resistance sources, susggested that the RphCas locus was distinct from Rph21 however their close physical proximity and haplotypic similarity requires further investigation for a formal gene designation for RphCas .

works.title: The class VIII myosin ATM2 stabilizes actin–plasma membrane contacts in tobacco pollen tubes by locally promoting PtdIns(4,5)P2 formation
works.abstract: Abstract The intersection of actin filaments with the plasma membrane (PM) in plant cells involves lipid–protein interactions by the Arabidopsis class VIII myosin ATM2 that are currently not understood. Using pollen tube cells as a model, we describe how ATM2 enables actin–PM contacts by modulating membrane lipid nano-organization. ATM2 bound anionic PM lipids, including phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P 2 ), with no apparent preference for any particular lipid species. Overexpression of ATM2 unexpectedly stabilized actin dynamics and altered pollen tube morphology. Actin dynamics remained unaltered upon overexpression of a lipid-binding-defective ATM2 variant. ATM2 effects on actin dynamics required PtdIns(4,5)P 2 , as artificial PtdIns(4,5)P 2 depletion in pollen tubes abolished the effects of full-length ATM2 on actin dynamics despite its retained PM association. ATM2 colocalized and interacted with the PI4P 5-kinase PIP5K2, which resides at actin–PM contacts and forms PtdIns(4,5)P 2 nanodomains facilitating rho-of-plants-dependent actin stabilization. Upon ATM2 overexpression, a fluorescent PtdIns(4,5)P 2 biosensor decorated an extended PM region in vivo, indicating a promoting effect of ATM2 on PtdIns(4,5)P 2 abundance. The catalytic activity of purified recombinant PIP5K2 protein was enhanced upon coincubation with a purified carboxy-terminal ATM2 fragment in vitro, suggesting that ATM2 contributes to the intrinsic regulation of PtdIns(4,5)P 2 formation. Actin dynamics are thus stabilized at the actin–PM interface by ATM2 locally promoting the formation of PtdIns(4,5)P 2 nanodomains, thereby self-reinforcing ATM2 recruitment while also facilitating rho of plants activation to stabilize membrane-proximal actin filaments.

works.title: Nobels oblige
Assembly-graph-assisted haplotype-resolved scaffolding of polyploid genomes
works.abstract: Assembling polyploid genomes at the chromosome level remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of accurately distinguishing homologous chromosomes, leaving a vast number of polyploid species without high-quality genome sequences. Current chromatin conformation capture (3C)-based haplotype-resolved scaffolding methods often produce highly incomplete and mis-phased assemblies of complex polyploids, as short sequences lacking sufficient interaction support and collapsed regions with misleading signals are difficult to resolve. Here we present GPhase, a haplotype-resolved scaffolding algorithm that integrates 3C (for example, Hi-C, Pore-C and Omni-C) data with assembly graphs to enhance accuracy, completeness and contiguity. By leveraging graph connectivity derived from long-read overlaps, GPhase effectively overcomes key limitations of 3C. When applied to 15 complex polyploid genomes, GPhase reduced the sequence missing rate (BUSCO-based) by up to tens-fold, decreased the sequence error rate (k-mer-based) by up to an order of magnitude and improved the contiguity (N50) of gap-free sequences by several-fold compared with existing tools.

works.title: Rhizobial type III effectors as regulators of root-nodule symbiosis in legumes
works.abstract: The rhizobia-legume nitrogen-fixing symbiosis begins when plants perceive rhizobial Nod factors (NF), activating the Common Symbiosis Signalling Pathway (CSSP) that drives nodule organogenesis. Rhizobia also inject Type III effectors (T3E) into host cells through a Type III Secretion System (T3SS) related to those of pathogenic bacteria. These effectors were long viewed only as suppressors of plant immunity and determinants of host compatibility, but this picture has changed. Recent studies revealed that rhizobial effectors (known as Nodulation Outer Proteins, Nops) such as NopT, NopM, NopL, NopP and NopZ directly target NF receptors or associated kinases, thereby regulating CSSP activation. The effector-triggering nodulation proteins (ET-Nods), a separate class of T3Es found in various Bradyrhizobium species, can activate nodule organogenesis independently of NF perception by rewiring host transcriptional and SUMOylation-based signalling. We trace the evolutionary origins of these activities, which may derive either from redirection of ancestral immune-targeting effectors toward symbiotic functions or from rhizobium-specific innovations. We ask whether the T3SS contributed to nodulation. We then consider what this interference means for the host, ranging from reinforced partner choice to partial loss of host control, and argue that rhizobial effectors have evolved as specialised modulators that converge on the signalling hubs governing symbiosis.

works.title: Tracing the evolutionary origins of jasmonate signaling: co-evolution of oxylipin metabolism and hormone perception in the green lineage
works.abstract: Jasmonates constitute a central class of lipid-derived signaling molecules that regulate plant defense, development, and environmental adaptation. Although jasmonic acid (JA) and its bioactive conjugate jasmonoyl-L-isoleucine (JA-Ile) are well characterized in angiosperms, recent evolutionary, biochemical, and structural studies have revealed that jasmonate signaling predates the origin of land plants. Jasmonates occur in streptophyte algae but are absent from chlorophytes, indicating that jasmonate biosynthesis evolved in the last common ancestor of streptophytes. However, the molecular nature, perception mechanisms, and biological functions of jasmonates have undergone profound changes during plant evolution. During terrestrialization, the recruitment of a pre-existing transcriptional regulatory network by a newly evolved COI1 receptor module established the canonical COI1/JAZ signaling system. Early diverging land plants employed dn-OPDA, a JA precursor, as the ancestral ligand, which was progressively replaced by JA amino acid conjugates such as JA-Ile in vascular plants. Here, we synthesize current evidence supporting a stepwise evolutionary model progressively shaping the COI1/JAZ-dependent hormone pathway. We discuss how (bio)chemical diversification of oxylipins, co-evolution of receptors and ligands, and the emergence of JA-Ile in vascular plants enabled the expansion, specificity, and systemic integration of jasmonate signaling as a requirement for plant terrestrialization.

works.title: Genome-wide association study and transcriptome analysis reveal candidate genes associated with mesosulfuron-methyl tolerance in wheat
From stress perception to metabolite disposition: dynamic regulation of stilbene biosynthesis in plants
works.abstract: Stilbenes are inducible plant specialized metabolites, best exemplified by resveratrol, a phytoalexin that links environmental perception, defense responses, and phenylpropanoid resource allocation. Stilbene accumulation may be controlled at 3 mechanistically distinct levels: signaling cascades that connect environmental and hormonal cues to kinase-dependent activation; combinatorial transcriptional control, which governs the response amplitude and specificity of stilbene synthase (STS) genes; and branch selection together with product disposition, which shapes the final metabolic output. Within this framework, MYB and WRKY proteins serve as major transcriptional nodes as activators or repressors, yet their regulatory effects depend on combinatorial interactions, phosphorylation events, competitive promoter occupancy, and metabolic context. We explicitly distinguish strongly supported mechanisms, defined by genetic perturbation, direct target validation, and metabolite quantification from emerging models built primarily on transient expression assays or co-expression correlations. This distinction avoids equating regulators supported by disparate levels of experimental evidence, identifies the most robust principles governing pathway control, and highlights experiments required to turn descriptive associations into causal mechanistic models. We further highlight conceptual insights extending beyond stilbene metabolism to inducible specialized metabolism in general, and outline research priorities for comparative genetics, cell-resolved analysis, and predictive pathway engineering.

works.title: PbSnRK1 ‐Mediated Phosphorylation of PbTCP13 Regulates Glucose‐Responsive Lignin Biosynthesis via PbMYB11 During Pear Stone Cell Formation
works.abstract: Stone cell lignification is a key determinant of pear fruit texture and commercial quality, and this process has been reported to be tightly coupled to cellular glucose availability. However, how glucose dose-dependently targets transcription factor phosphorylation during lignin biosynthesis remains largely unknown. Using yeast two-hybrid library screening and phosphorylation assays, we found that PbSnRK1, a glucose-responsive kinase, interacts with and directly phosphorylates PbTCP13, thereby participating in the regulation of stone cell lignification. PbSnRK1 serves as an energy-status sensor linking glucose signalling to biphasic regulation of lignin metabolism in pear. Under low-glucose conditions, activated PbSnRK1 phosphorylates the transcription factor PbTCP13 at Ser265, targeting it for 26S proteasome-mediated degradation and thereby derepressing PbMYB11-PbCCR1 cascade associated with lignin biosynthesis. Under high-glucose conditions, suppressed PbSnRK1 kinase activity results in PbTCP13 protein accumulation, which restricts excessive lignification by both repressing PbCCR1 transcription and physically interacting with PbMYB11 to inhibit its transactivation capacity. This PbSnRK1-PbTCP13-PbMYB11 cascade, balanced by glucose concentration, acts as a molecular switch that activates stone cell formation and lignification at low-glucose levels during early fruit development, while restricting excessive lignification at high-glucose levels during later stages, providing new mechanistic insights into energy-coupled secondary wall metabolism in fleshy fruits.

works.title: The BIK1–WRKY9 module activates jasmonate signaling to confer apple resistance to Alternaria blotch
works.abstract: Apple Alternaria blotch, caused by Alternaria alternata f. sp. mali (A. alternata), is a devastating fungal disease threatening global apple production. However, the early signaling pathway underlying apple resistance to A. alternata remains unclear. In this study, through transcriptomic analysis, we identified that MdWRKY9 is a key positive regulator of apple resistance to A. alternata, whose expression is induced in the resistant "Hanfu" while being reduced in the susceptible "Gala" following A. alternata infection. Stable overexpression of MdWRKY9 enhanced apple resistance to A. alternata, whereas RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated knockdown of MdWRKY9 increased susceptibility. We further demonstrated that MdWRKY9 directly represses the expression of MdJAZ8, a key repressor of jasmonate (JA) signaling. Accordingly, stable overexpression of MdJAZ8 in apple calli reduced resistance to A. alternata and suppressed JA signaling. Consistently, transient overexpression of MdJAZ8 in apple leaves decreased resistance to A. alternata, whereas transient silencing of MdJAZ8 via RNAi enhanced disease resistance. Furthermore, we identified that the receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase MdBIK1 (BOTRYTIS-INDUCED KINASE1, a core component of the PTI pathway) interacts with and phosphorylates MdWRKY9 at Thr-2. The phosphorylation of MdWRKY9 enhances resistance to A. alternata by further suppressing MdJAZ8 and activating JA signaling. Together, our findings define a complete PTI-associated signaling module in which the MdBIK1-MdWRKY9 complex enhances JA-mediated immunity against A. alternata by directly repressing MdJAZ8. This study refines the regulatory mechanism by which the BIK1 family kinases modulate JA signaling, providing new insights into the plant immune signaling network.

works.title: Two linked nitrate reductase genes CR8.1 and CR8.2 positively coregulate yield and NUE in rice
works.abstract: The qCR8 locus contains two linked nitrate reductase genes, CR8.1 and CR8.2. Genetic and biochemical evidence shows that their additive activity promotes nitrate uptake and transport, grain yield and nitrogen use efficiency, and that alleles from the cultivar 9311 are favorable for rice breeding.

works.title: Genomic dissection of divergent selection reveals a roadmap for reciprocal improvement of Chinese and American soybean
works.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max [L.] Merr.) was domesticated in China over five millennia ago; yet, its global expansion has resulted in two distinct, independently evolved breeding pools in China and the Americas. While regional breeding has optimized specific traits, a comprehensive roadmap for the reciprocal exchange of these "breeding-specific" beneficial alleles is lacking. Here, we performed a large-scale genomic dissection of 2,377 soybean accessions, integrating 8.4 million high-quality SNPs with multi-environment phenotyping across 11 locations. Through genome-wide association studies (GWAS), we identified 261 significant loci (223 novel) governing six key agronomic traits, revealing that Chinese and American germplasms have accumulated distinct sets of beneficial alleles of seed size/protein in China and oil/yield in the Americas. To harness this untapped potential, we developed the Soybean Targeted Improvement Navigation System (STINS), a framework integrating population genomics, GWAS, and genomic selection (GS). We demonstrate the potential of targeted beneficial allele introgression between populations via gene modification for rapid trait improvement. Proof-of-concept functional evaluation through CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of GmST05 in an American cultivar and overexpression of a resistant GmSNAP18 haplotype in a Chinese cultivar provided experimental support for STINS-predicted targets for protein content and SCN resistance improvement. Our study provides a navigable genomic resource for "knowledge-driven design breeding", offering a blueprint for the global exchange of elite alleles to ensure future food security.
